Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verses 1–5:

Medinan (madaniyya). It contains 5,790 letters, 1,280 words, and 73 verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad informed me, by my reading to him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Abu Amr al-Himyari and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Basri informed me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab al-Abdi said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, on the authority of Salam ibn Sulaym, on the authority of Harun ibn Kathir, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of [Abu Umama], on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ahzab and teaches it to his family and to those whom his right hand possesses, he will be granted safety from the punishment of the grave." [1] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/115.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "O Prophet, fear Allah..." (the verse).

It was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war Amr ibn [Abi] Sufyan al-Sulami. That was because they came to Medina and stayed with Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, after the battle of Uhud. The Prophet (ﷺ) had granted them safe conduct so that they could speak with him. Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh and Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq went with them. They said to the Prophet (ﷺ), while Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him: "Abandon the mention of our gods, al-Lat, al-Uzza and Manat, and say that they have intercession and benefit for those who worship them, and we will leave you and your Lord." This grieved the Prophet (ﷺ). Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Permit us, O Messenger of Allah, to kill them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I have granted them safe conduct." [2] Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Go out, under the curse and wrath of Allah!" The Prophet (ﷺ) then commanded Umar to expel them from Medina. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O Prophet, fear Allah..." [[Asbab al-nuzul of al-Wahidi: 236.]] [3]

"And do not obey the disbelievers": from the people of Mecca, meaning Abu Sufyan, Abu al-A'war and Ikrima. "And the hypocrites": Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Abdullah ibn Sa'd and Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq.

"Indeed Allah is ever Knowing, Wise." "And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do." In the reading "what you do" (ta'malun) is read with the ya' by Abu Amr, and with the ta' by the others.

"And rely upon Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, on the authority of Musa ibn Ali, [on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Alawayh], on the authority of Isma'il ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Musayyab, on the authority of a shaykh from the people of Syria, who said: A delegation from Thaqif came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him to grant them a respite of one year regarding al-Lat and al-Uzza, and they said: "So that Quraysh may know our standing with you." The Prophet (ﷺ) was inclined to do so [[It was not permissible for the Prophet (ﷺ) to be inclined toward this, either because he does not speak from desire, or because it contradicts tawhid (the oneness of Allah), for how could he accept the worship of other than Allah, the Exalted?]]. Then Allah, Exalted, revealed: "O Prophet, fear Allah..." (the verses).

His saying: "Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body." It was revealed concerning Abu Ma'mar Jamil [ibn Ma'mar] ibn Habib ibn Abdullah al-Fihri. He was an intelligent man who retained what he heard. Quraysh said: "Abu Ma'mar has not retained these things unless he has two hearts." He used to say: "I have two hearts, and with each one of them I understand better than Muhammad." On the day of Badr, when the polytheists were defeated, and Abu Ma'mar was among them, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb met him, and he was holding one of his sandals in his hand while the other was on his foot. Abu Sufyan said to him: "O Abu Ma'mar, what is the state of the people?" He said: "They have fled." Abu Sufyan said: "Then what about your sandal, one of them in your hand and the other on your foot?" Abu Ma'mar said to him: "I did not realise except that they were both on my foot." So on that day they knew that if he had had two hearts, he would not have forgotten his sandal in his hand. [[Majma' al-Bayan: 8/117.]]

Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: This is a parable which Allah struck for the one who makes his wife unlawful to himself by saying she is like his mother (zihar), and for the one who adopts the son of another. It means: just as a man cannot have two hearts, so too the wife of one who makes zihar cannot be his mother, and a son cannot be the son of two fathers.

His saying: "Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers..." Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr and Warsh read the word al-la'i without elongation or hamza, and with a ya' omitted... [The text reads: "Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr and Warsh read al-la'i (اللَّاء) without madd (elongation) and without hamza, with the elongated and hamzated form without ya'; Nafi' (other than Warsh), Ayyub, Ya'qub and al-A'raj (read it so)"] and he recited:

"From al-la'i who did not seek chastity, desiring reward, but who would surely kill the innocent, the heedless."

[[Lisan al-Arab: 15/445; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/108.]]

The people of Kufa and Syria read it with madd, hamza, and the ya', and Abu Ubayd preferred this for its fullness, though there was a difference of transmission from Ibn Kathir. All of these are well-known dialects (lughat).

"Tuzahirun" (who make zihar): with a fatha on the ta' and shadda on the za' is the reading of Syria (Shami). With a fatha on the ta' and a light za' is the reading of Kufa, except Asim. Abu Ubayd preferred it with a damma on the ta', a light za', and a kasra on the ha', which is the reading of Asim and al-Hasan.

Abu Amr said: This is unacceptable, because zihar is from mutual assistance (muzahara), and the verse was revealed concerning Aws ibn al-Samit ibn Qays ibn Asram, brother of Ubada, and his wife Khawla bint Tha'laba ibn Malik. Allah, Exalted, says: "He has not made your wives, whom you say, 'You are to us as the backs of our mothers,' your mothers. They are not your mothers. Your mothers are none but those who gave birth to you." [Continuing] "...but that is a statement of falsehood and an evil. Allah pardons and forgives. Your wives are lawful to you." We will mention the story and the ruling in Surat al-Mujadila, if Allah wills.

His saying: "Nor has He made your adopted sons (adi'a'akum) your sons (abna'akum)," meaning those whom you have adopted.

It was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Haritha ibn Sharahil al-Kalbi, from the Banu Abd Wadd. He had been a slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom he freed and adopted before revelation. He also established brotherhood between him and Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib in Islam, making the poor man a brother to the rich man so that it would benefit him. When the Prophet (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadi, who had been married to Zayd ibn Haritha, the Jews and the hypocrites said: "Muhammad has married his son's wife, while he forbids the people from it." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses.

He also said: "That is your saying by your mouths, which has no reality," meaning their saying: "Zayd, son of Muhammad." "But Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way." "Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients (mawali)." That is: they are your brothers in religion, and your clients, if they were your freed slaves, and not your sons.

Aqil ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani informed me, on the authority of al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, on the authority of Ibn Ulayya, on the authority of Uyayna ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Bakr said: Allah, Exalted, says: "Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients." So I am among those whose father is not known, and I am among your brothers in religion. He said: My father said: "I think that if he knew that his father was a donkey, he would still claim affiliation with him." "And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error" (before the prohibition), when you attributed him to other than his father. Qatada said: meaning that you call him by other than his father while you think that he is so. "But what your hearts have intended" (after the prohibition), when you attributed him to other than his father, while you knew he was not his son. The position of "ma" in His saying "ma ta'ammadat qulubukum" is in the genitive, as a reply to the "ma" in His saying "fima akhta'tum bihi." Its meaning is: "But [there is blame] in what your hearts have intended." "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims affiliation to other than his father, or to other than the people of his favour, upon him is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all people." [4] [[Sahih Muslim: 4/115, with variation; Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/905; Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/502.]]

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamdun informed us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Abu Salih informed me, al-Layth told me, Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and Amra bint Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha: that Abu Hudhayfa ibn Utba ibn Rabi'a ibn Abd Shams, who was among those who witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), adopted Salim and married him to the daughter of his brother, Hind bint al-Walid ibn Utba ibn Rabi'a. Salim was a client (mawla) of a woman from the Ansar, and he adopted him, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had adopted Zayd. Whoever adopted a man in the Jahiliyya, people would call him by his name, and he would inherit from his estate, until there was revealed: "Call them by [the names of] their fathers..." (the verse).

al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 33, verses 6–8:

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The Prophet has more right over the believers than they have over themselves﴾, meaning that he may judge over them as he wills, and his judgment over them is valid.

Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata said: this means that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) calls them to something and their own selves call them to something else, obedience to the Prophet is more deserving of them than obedience to their own selves. Muqatil said: this means obedience to the Prophet (peace be upon him) is more deserving than the obedience of some of you to others. Ibn Zayd said: ﴿The Prophet has more right over the believers than they have over themselves﴾ as you have more right over your slave, so whatever he decides about them is lawful, just as whatever you decide about your slave is lawful. It was also said: he (peace be upon him) has more right over them in enforcing rulings and carrying out the prescribed punishments upon them, because of what this contains of benefit for creation and distance from corruption. It was also said: he has more right over them in calling them to jihad and in giving up one's life rather than him. The wise said: ﴿The Prophet has more right over the believers than they have over themselves﴾, because their selves call them to that which brings their destruction, while the Prophet calls them to that which brings their salvation. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: because the Prophet calls them to reason, while their selves call them to desire. Bassam ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Iraqi said: because their selves guard them from the fire of this world, while the Prophet guards them from the fire of the Hereafter.

Sufyan narrated from Talha, from 'Ata, from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: ﴿The Prophet has more right over the believers than they have over themselves, and he is a father to them﴾.

Sufyan narrated from 'Amr, from Bujala or another, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by a boy who was reading in the codex: ﴿The Prophet has more right over the believers than they have over themselves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them﴾. He said: "O boy, erase it." The boy said: "This is the codex of Ubayy." So he went to him and asked him, and he said: "The Qur'an used to occupy me, and the market and its bargaining used to occupy you."

'Ikrimah said: I was informed that it was in the first recension: "and he is their father."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 9–17 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ – the verse. This was when the Muslims, together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), were besieged during the days of the Trench (al-Khandaq), ﴿when there came upon you hosts﴾, meaning the confederates (al-Ahzab): Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, meaning the al-Saba (the east wind). ʿIkrima said: On the night of the confederates, the South wind said to the North wind: "Set out with the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The North wind said: "Indeed, the free woman does not travel by night." So the wind that was sent against them was the al-Saba.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was given victory by the al-Saba, and ʿAd were destroyed by the al-Dabur" [Musnad Ahmad: 2/228; Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/22].

﴿And hosts you did not see﴾, and they were the angels, who did not fight that day. ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ The exegetes said: Allah sent upon them, during the night, a cold wind, and sent the angels, who uprooted the tent pegs, cut the ropes of the tent-canopies, extinguished the fires, overturned the cooking pots, and the horses ran about among one another. Allah cast terror into them, and the takbir of the angels grew loud on the sides of their camp, so that every chief of a tribe would say: "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" When they gathered around him, he would say: "Escape! Escape! You have been overtaken," because of the terror Allah had cast upon them, and they fled without any fighting.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi informed me, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Sulayti informed me, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Hasan informed me, from al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Ash'arani [in the Isfahan copy: al-Sha'rani], from ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn, from Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abu Saʿd Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Baqqal, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father. And ʿAqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, from Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi, from Salama, who said: Muhammad ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, both of whom said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and accompany him?" He said: "Yes, my nephew." He said: "And how did you used to act?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive greatly." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him, we would not have let him walk on the earth, but we would have carried him on our necks, and served him, and done such and such."

Then Hudhayfa said: "My nephew, by Allah, I saw myself on the night of the Confederates with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Trench, on a cold night, the like of whose cold I had never found before or after. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who will stand up and go to these people and bring us their news? Allah will admit him to Paradise.'" [7] [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 10/449; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/185.]

No man among us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said the like of it. The people fell silent and no man among us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said: "Is there a man who will stand up and look for us what the people have done, on condition that he will be my companion in Paradise?" No man stood up, out of the intensity of fear, the intensity of hunger, and the intensity of cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "O Hudhayfa!" I had no choice but to stand up when he called me. I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah," and I rose and came to him, while my two sides were trembling. He wiped my head and face and said: "Go to these people until you bring me their news, and do not do anything until you return to me."

Then he said: "O Allah, protect him from before him, behind him, on his right, on his left, above him, and below him." So I took my bow and tightened my joints, then I set off walking toward them as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I went and entered among the people, and Allah had sent upon them a wind which cut their tent-ropes, uprooted their tents, and carried off their horses, leaving nothing without destroying it. Abu Sufyan was sitting warming himself at the fire. I took my arrow and placed it on the string of my bow, but then I remembered the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not do anything until you return," so I returned the arrow to my quiver.

When Abu Sufyan saw what the wind and the hosts of Allah were doing to them, that no cooking pot, fire, or building would stay firm for them, he stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each man take the hand of his companion and see who he is." So I took the hand of the one sitting beside me and said: "Who are you?" He said: "Subhan Allah, do you not know me? I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." And behold, he was a man from Hawazin.

Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not woken up in a place of settlement. The horses and camels have perished, Banu Qurayza have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind what you see. So depart, for I am departing." Then he rose to his camel, which was tied, sat upon it, and struck it; it leapt up on three legs, and he did not release its tether until it was standing.

Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands. Allah repelled the confederates, and that is His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see﴾. He said: So I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and informed him of the news, and he laughed until his canine teeth showed in the darkness of the night. He said:

"Warmth left me, and the Prophet (ﷺ) brought me near, made me sleep at his feet, cast over me the edge of his garment, and pressed my chest against the sole of his foot."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾, meaning from above the valley, from the east side, and upon them were Malik ibn ʿAwf al-Nadari and ʿUyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari with a thousand of Ghatafan; with them Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi among Banu Asad, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab among the Jews of Banu Qurayza. ﴿And from below you﴾, meaning from the bottom of the valley, from the west side, and it was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb with Quraysh and those who followed him, and Abu al-Aʿwar ʿAmr ibn Sufyan al-Sulami from the side of the Trench. What prompted the Battle of the Trench, it is said, was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'s expulsion of Banu al-Nadir from their homes.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and one whom I do not accuse, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and from ʿAsim ibn Qatada, and from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, some of whose narrations enter into others. They said: Among the account of the Trench was that a group of Jews, including Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Hawdha ibn Qays, and Abu ʿAmmar al-Wa'ili, with a group from Banu al-Nadir and a group from Banu Wa'il, who are those who gathered the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), went out until they came to Quraysh in Mecca. They invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." Quraysh said to them: "O assembly of Jews, you are the People of the first Book and knowledge. Tell us: we differ with Muhammad, so is our religion better or his?"

They said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than them." He said: They are the ones about whom Allah revealed:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in idols and false deities…﴾ to His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire﴾ [Surat al-Nisa: 51–55].

When they said that to Quraysh, what they said pleased them, and they were eager for what they had invited them to, the war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So they resolved upon it and prepared for it. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays ibn Ghaylan, invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and informed them that they would be with them against him, and that Quraysh had already pledged themselves to that and had resolved upon it. They responded to them. So Quraysh went out, their leader being Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Ghatafan went out, their leader being ʿUyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr, with Banu Fazara; and al-Huwayrith ibn ʿAwf ibn Abi Jariya al-Murri with Banu Murra; and Mas'ud ibn Jabala ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif ibn Shahma ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hilal ibn Khalawa ibn Ashja' ibn Zayd ibn Ghatafan, with those of his people from Ashja' who followed him.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of them and of what they had resolved upon, he dug a trench around Medina. The one who suggested the trench to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Salman al-Farisi, and it was the first battle Salman witnessed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was then a free man. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we were in Persia and were besieged, we dug a trench around ourselves." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims with him worked on it until they perfected it.

We have mentioned the hadith of Salman concerning the manner of digging the Trench in Surat Al ʿImran. They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the Trench, Quraysh came and descended at the gathering place of al-Asyal, beyond it, between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba, with ten thousand of their Ahabish and those who followed them of Banu Kinana and the people of Tihama. Ghatafan and those who followed them of the people of Najd came and descended [at Dhanab Naqma] by the side of Uhud.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims went out and made their backs to Sal', with three thousand Muslims, and there he pitched his camp, with the Trench between him and the enemy. He ordered the women and children to be raised up into the fortresses. The enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadari, set out until he came to Kaʿb ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the holder of the covenant and pact of Banu Qurayza, who had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on behalf of his people and had pledged to that. When Kaʿb heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he locked his fortress against him, and he asked permission to enter but Kaʿb refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Kaʿb, open to me!" He said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what is between me and him, and I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness."

He said: "Woe to you, open to me so I may speak with you." He said: "I will not do it." He said: "By Allah, if you shut me out, it will only be over your little bit of dried food, so that I may eat with you from it." The man was cautious, but he opened to him. He said: "O Kaʿb, woe to you! I have brought you the glory of the age and a sea that has overflowed. I have brought you Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the gathering place of al-Asyal beyond it, and Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Dhanab Naqma by the side of Uhud. They have pledged to me and made a covenant with me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him."

Kaʿb ibn Asad said to him: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age, with a cloud that has poured out its water, thundering and lightning, yet holds nothing. Leave me and Muhammad and what I am upon. I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity."

Huyayy ibn Akhtab kept coaxing Kaʿb, stroking him on the crown and back, until he yielded to him, on condition that he gave him a covenant from Allah and a pledge: "If Quraysh and Ghatafan return without reaching Muhammad, I will enter with you into your share, until what befalls you befalls me." So Kaʿb ibn Asad broke his covenant and disavowed what was between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

When the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Saʿd ibn Muʿadh ibn al-Nuʿman ibn Imru' al-Qays, of Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbada ibn Dulaym, of Banu Saʿida ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, together with ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, brother of al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khuwat ibn Jubayr, brother of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.

He said: "Go and see whether what has reached us about these people is true. If it is true, then signal to me with a sign that I may understand, and do not weaken the arms of the people. If they are upholding the covenant between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." They set out until they reached them, and found them at the most wicked [of positions] of what had been reported about them. They said: "Who is the Messenger of Allah?" and they said: "There is no covenant between us and Muhammad, nor any pact." Saʿd ibn ʿUbada insulted them and they insulted him, and Saʿd was a man with a hot temper. Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insults." Then Saʿd and Saʿd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), greeted him, and said: "ʿAdl and al-Qara," meaning like the treachery of ʿAdl and al-Qara against the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Companions of al-Raji', Khubayb ibn ʿAdi and his companions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!" At that the trial grew great, fear intensified, and the enemy came upon them from above them and from below them, until the believers thought every kind of thought. Hypocrisy stirred among some of the hypocrites, until Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, said to them: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while one of us cannot even go out to relieve himself!" [Quoted at length in Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/157–159, the occasion of the verse.] ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾. Then Aws ibn Qayzi, of Banu Haritha, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and that was in the presence of men of his people. "So permit us to return to our homes, for they are outside Medina."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained, and the polytheists remained besieging him for some twenty nights, nearly a month, and there was no fighting between the two sides except shooting with arrows and pebbles. When the trial grew severe on the people, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to ʿUyayna ibn Hisn and to al-Harith ibn ʿAwf, the two leaders of Ghatafan, and offered them a third of the produce of Medina on condition that they return with those who were with them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. A peace was arranged between them and him, until they wrote the document, but the witnesses had not yet attested it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned this to Saʿd ibn Muʿadh and Saʿd ibn ʿUbada and consulted them about it. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it something God has commanded you, which we must carry out, or a matter you love and so you do it, or something you do for us?" He said: "No, rather it is for you. By Allah, I would not do this, except that I have seen the Arabs shooting at you from one bow and gathering against you from every side, so I wished to break their strength from you."

Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, we and these people were upon polytheism and the worship of idols, not worshipping Allah nor knowing Him, and they did not hope to eat from our produce except as guests or by purchase. Now that Allah has honoured us with Islam and strengthened us through you, shall we give them our wealth?! We have no need of this. By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword until Allah judges between us and them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions said: "Then you and that matter are yours." Saʿd took the document and erased what was written in it, then said: "Let them strive against us."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims remained in their state while the polytheists besieged them, and there was no fighting between them except that some horsemen of Quraysh, among them ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Abi Qays, brother of Banu ʿAmir ibn Lu'ayy, and ʿIkrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Hubayra ibn Abi Wahb, both of Makhzum, and Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Allah, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, and Mirdas, brother of Banu Muharib ibn Fihr, had armed themselves for battle, and they rode out on their horses and passed by Banu Kinana.

One of them, from Banu al-Harith, said: "O Banu Kinana, you will know today who the horsemen are!" Then they came and stopped at the Trench. When they saw it, they said: "By Allah, this is a trick, which the Arabs had never devised." Then they sought a narrow place in the Trench and struck their horses, and they burst through it, and their horses galloped about in the marshy ground between the Trench and Sal'.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) set out with a group of Muslims until he blocked the breach through which they had forced their horses, and the horsemen came toward them. ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd had fought at the Battle of Badr until a wound incapacitated him, so he had not witnessed [any other battle]. When it was the day of the Trench, he came out marked with a sign to show his position. When he and his horses stood still, ʿAli said to him: "O ʿAmr, you used to make a covenant with Allah that no man from Quraysh would invite you to two qualities without your accepting one of them." He said: "Indeed." He said: "I invite you to Allah, to His Messenger, and to Islam." He said: "I have no need of that." He said: "Then I invite you to single combat." He said: "Why, O nephew? By Allah, I do not wish to kill you."

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "But by Allah, I wish to kill you." Then ʿAmr became enraged, leapt down from his horse, struck or wounded its face, and turned to ʿAli. They grappled and fought, and ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) killed him.

And his cavalry fled in defeat until they plunged back through the trench in flight. [[On that day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The duel of ʿAlī with ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd is better than the deeds of my community until the Day of Resurrection." In another wording: "The striking of ʿAlī is better than the worship of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn)." See Mustadrak al-Sahihayn 3/32, Kanz al-ʿUmmal 6/158, and al-Sira al-Halabiyya 2/349.]] Along with ʿAmr, two men were killed: Munabbih ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbaq ibn ʿAbd al-Dar, who was struck by an arrow and died from it in Makkah; and Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi. Nawfal had plunged into the trench, became trapped in it, and they pelted him with stones. He said: "O company of the Arabs, a death better than this!" ʿAlī then descended to him and killed him. The Muslims then gained control of his body, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to sell them his body. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no need of his body or its price; do with him as you wish." So he left them free to take it.

ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, said: "On the day of the Trench we were in the fortress of Banu Harītha, which was one of the strongest fortresses of Madina. Umm Saʿd ibn Muʿadh was with us in the fortress, and that was before the veil was imposed upon us. Saʿd ibn Muʿadh passed by, wearing a coat of mail that was short, so that his entire forearm was exposed, and he had his spear in his hand, saying:

'Wait a little, the battle will witness a charge;
There is no harm in death when its appointed time comes.'"

His mother said: "Hurry, my son, for by Allah you have been delayed!" ʿĀʾisha said: "I said to her: 'O Umm Saʿd, by Allah, I wish Saʿd's coat of mail were more complete than it is,' and I feared for him where the arrow struck him." She said: "Saʿd was struck that day, and his artery (al-akhal) was cut. It is reported that whoever's artery was cut would not stop bleeding until he died. Ḥibbān ibn Qays ibn al-Ghurqa, one of Banu ʿĀmir ibn Lu'ayy, struck him. When he hit him, he said: 'Take it, for I am the son of al-Ghurqa!' Saʿd said: 'May Allah drown your face in the Fire!' Then Saʿd said: 'O Allah, if You have kept any of the war against Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than those who harmed Your Messenger, denied him and expelled him. And if You have ended the war between us and them, then make it a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until my eyes are cooled by Banu Qurayẓa,' who were his allies and clients in the Jahiliyya."

Muḥammad ibn Isḥaq ibn Yasār narrated, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father ʿAbbād, who said: "Ṣafiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was in the fortress of Ḥassān ibn Thābit." She said: "Ḥassān was with us in it, with the women and children."

Ṣafiyya said: "A man of the Jews passed by us and began circling the fortress. Banu Qurayẓa had gone to war and cut off what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there was no one between us and them to repel for us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were at the throats of their enemy and could not turn away from them to us if someone came to us." She said: "I said: 'O Ḥassān, this Jew, as you see, is circling the fortress, and by Allah I do not feel safe that he will point out our weak spot to the Jews behind us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions are occupied with us, so go down to him and kill him.'"

He said: "May Allah forgive you, O daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib! By Allah, you know I am not the one for this." She said: "When he said that to me and I saw nothing with him, I tucked up my garment, took a pillar, went down from the fortress to him, and struck him with the pillar until I killed him. When I finished with him, I returned to the fortress and said: 'O Ḥassān, go down to him and strip him, for what kept me from his spoils was only that he was a man.'" He said: "I have no need of his spoils, O daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib."

They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions remained in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described of fear and hardship, due to the support their enemy gave one another against them and their attack from above them and below them. Then Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn [Unayf] ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Qunfudh ibn Hilāl ibn Ḥalāwa ibn Ashja' ibn Zayd [[In Tarikh al-Tabari (2/242): Rabīth.]] ibn Ghaṭafān came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, but my people do not know of my Islam, so command me in whatever you wish.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You are only one man among us, so cause discord among them if you are able, for war is deception.'"

Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd went out until he came to Banu Qurayẓa, who had been his companions (nadīm) in the Jahiliyya. He said to them: "O Banu Qurayẓa, you know my affection for you and the special bond between me and you." They said: "You have spoken the truth; you are not suspected by us." He said: "Quraysh and Ghaṭafān have come to fight Muḥammad, and you have aided them against him. Quraysh and Ghaṭafān are not in the same situation as you. This is your land, where your wealth, your sons and your women are, and you cannot move away from it to another place. Quraysh and Ghaṭafān have their wealth, sons and women elsewhere. If they see a chance for plunder and booty they will seize it; otherwise they will return to their lands and leave you alone with the man, while the man is in your land, and you will have no power against him if he is left alone with you. So do not fight with the people until you take hostages from their nobles who will remain in your hands as a guarantee for you, that they will fight alongside you against Muḥammad until you finish with him." They said: "You have given sound and sincere advice."

Then he went out until he came to Quraysh, and said to Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and those with him of the men of Quraysh: "O company of Quraysh, you know my affection for you and my separation from Muḥammad. A matter has reached me which I believe is a duty upon me to convey to you, as sincere counsel. Keep it secret from me." They said: "We will."

He said: "You know that the Jews have regretted what they did between them and Muḥammad, and they have sent to him saying: 'We regret what we did.' Would it please you if we took men of the nobles of the two tribes, Quraysh and Ghaṭafān, and handed them over, so that you may cut off their necks, and then we will be with you against those who remain of them?"

Then he sent to them: "Yes." He added: "If the Jews send to you seeking hostages from your men, do not give them a single man from you." Then he went out until he came to Ghaṭafān and said: "O company of Ghaṭafān, you are my origin, my clan, and the people most beloved to me, and I do not think you suspect me." They said: "You have spoken the truth." He said: "Keep it secret from me." They said: "We will." Then he said to them the same as he had said to Quraysh, and warned them of what he had warned them of.

When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal of the fifth year, and this was among what Allah did for His Messenger, Abū Sufyān and the chiefs of Ghaṭafān sent ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl with a group from Quraysh and Ghaṭafān to Banu Qurayẓa. They said to them: "We are not a people who can remain. The hoof and the camel have perished. So go out to fight in the morning, until we finish with Muḥammad and settle what is between us and him."

They sent back to them: "Tomorrow is Saturday, a day on which we do nothing. Some of us had committed a transgression on it, and what befell him is not hidden from you. Moreover, we will not fight with you until you give us hostages from your men who will remain in our hands as a guarantee for us until we finish with Muḥammad. For we fear that if the war hurts you and the fighting becomes severe upon you, you will travel to your lands and leave us with the man in our land, and we have no power against Muḥammad."

When the messengers returned to them with what Banu Qurayẓa had said, Quraysh and Ghaṭafān said: "You know, by Allah, that what Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd told you is true." They sent to Banu Qurayẓa: "By Allah, we will not give you a single man from our men. If you want to fight, then come out and fight."

Banu Qurayẓa, when the messengers reached them with this, said: "What Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd mentioned to you is true. The people want nothing but that you fight, so that if they find an opportunity they seize it; and if not, they will slip away to their lands and leave you alone with the man in your land." They sent to Quraysh and Ghaṭafān: "By Allah, we will not fight with you until you give us hostages." They refused, and Allah sowed discord between them. Allah sent upon them a wind on cold, harsh, wintry nights, until they turned back and returned. "And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Allah, the Exalted, said: "When the eyes swerved (zāghat)," meaning they were turned and fixed, "and the hearts reached the throats (al-ḥanājir)," meaning they were displaced from their places until they reached the throats out of terror, "and you assumed about Allah assumptions." As for the hypocrites, they thought Muḥammad and his companions would be defeated and uprooted. As for the believers, they were certain that what Allah had promised them was true, [namely] that He would make His religion prevail "over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it." [[Extended in Tafsir al-Qurtubi 14/135–138, on the occasion of revelation, and Tarikh al-Tabari 2/243.]]

The reciters differed regarding His saying: al-ẓunūnā, al-rasūlā, and al-sabīlā. Those who affirmed the alif in them both in pause and in continuation were the people of Madina, al-Shām, Ayyūb, and ʿĀṣim through the transmission of Abū Bakr, and Abū ʿAmr through the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Kisāʾī through the transmission of Qutayba. They said: "Their alifs are firmly established in the ʿUthmānic codex and in all the codices of the other regions." Abū ʿAmr read them without an alif in all other transmissions, and Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb read them without an alif in both states, in accordance with the original form.

The rest read with the alif in pause and without it in continuation. They argued that the Arabs do this at the rhyme-endings of their poems and their hemistiches: they add an alif at the place of fatḥa when pausing, and they do not do this within the body of lines. So affirming the alif in these words is fitting, because they are the endings of verses, likened to rhyme.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "There the believers were tested" (hunālika ubtiliya al-mu'minūn), meaning they were examined and purified, so that the believer might be distinguished from the hypocrite. "And they were shaken (zulzilū) with a severe shaking," meaning they were moved and frightened. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read zalzālan with a fatḥa on the zāy; both are verbal nouns (maṣdar).

"And when the hypocrites say," meaning Muʿattib ibn Qushayr and his companions, "and those in whose hearts is a disease," meaning doubt and weakness of conviction, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." "And when a faction of them said," meaning from among the hypocrites, and they were Aws ibn Qayẓī and his companions. Muqatil said: they were from Banu Sālim. "O people of Yathrib," meaning Madina. Abū ʿUbayda said: Yathrib is the name of a land, and the city of the Messenger (peace be upon him) is in one part of it. "There is no station for you" is the reading of the majority with a fatḥa on the mīm, meaning there is no place for you to remain. al-Sulamī read it with a ḍamma on the mīm, meaning there is no staying for you; this is the transmission of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim. "So return to your homes": they commanded them to flee from the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn ʿAbbās said: the Jews said to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions among the hypocrites: "What drives you to kill yourselves at the hands of Abū Sufyān and his companions? Return to Madina." So they returned. "And a group of them asked permission of the Prophet" to return to their homes, and they were Banu Ḥāritha ibn al-Ḥārith, "saying: 'Indeed our houses are exposed (ʿawra),'" meaning they are empty [and unprotected], and they are on the side facing the enemy, and we fear for them from the enemy and thieves. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read ʿawira with a kasra on the wāw, meaning walls that are short, with gaps and openings. The Arabs say: "So-and-so's house is ʿawra" when it is not fortified, and "the horseman has become ʿawira" when there is a gap in his defense against blows. The poet said:

"When you meet them, you will not find in the house one with an exposed side,
nor a guest stricken, nor a neighbor left destitute." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi 14/148.]]

Allah, the Exalted, said: "And they were not exposed; they intended only to flee." "And if it had been entered upon them," meaning if these armies they fight against had entered Madina "from its sides," its surroundings and areas, its singular being qaṭr, and there is another form, qaṭr and aqṭār.

"Then they were asked to commit fitna," meaning shirk, "they would have given it." The reading of the people of Ḥijāz is with a short alif, meaning they would have come to it and done it, and they would have reverted from Islam and disbelieved. The others read with the long vowel, meaning they would have given it. They said: when there is a request, there is giving. "And they would not have hesitated over it but briefly," meaning they would not have been held back from the fitna except briefly, and they would have hastened to respond to it, willingly with their souls. This is the statement of most exegetes. al-Ḥasan and al-Farrāʾ said: they would not have remained in Madina after giving up disbelief except briefly, until they perished. "And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs," meaning before the Battle of the Trench.

Yazīd ibn Dūmān said: they were Banu Ḥāritha, who had intended on the day of Uhud to falter along with Banu Salama. When what was revealed about them was revealed, they made a covenant with Allah never to return to such a thing again. So Allah mentioned to them what they had given of themselves. Qatāda said: they were people who had been absent from the battle of Badr and saw what Allah had given the people of Badr of honor and virtue, and they said: "If Allah shows us a battle, we will surely fight." So Allah brought this upon them in a corner of Madina.

Muqatil and al-Kalbī said: they were seventy men who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of ʿAqaba, and said to him: "Stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves, your wives, your children, and your wealth." They said: "If we do that, what will we have, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For you is victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter." [8] [[Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 6/48.]] They said: "We have done it." That is their covenant. "And the covenant of Allah is ever questioned."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, which is decreed upon you; and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little," until your appointed terms; and all of this world is little.

"Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm," meaning defeat, "or intends for you mercy," meaning victory. "And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or any helper."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 9–17 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ – the verse. This was when the Muslims, together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), were besieged during the days of the Trench (al-Khandaq), ﴿when there came upon you hosts﴾, meaning the confederates (al-Ahzab): Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, meaning the al-Saba (the east wind). ʿIkrima said: On the night of the confederates, the South wind said to the North wind: "Set out with the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The North wind said: "Indeed, the free woman does not travel by night." So the wind that was sent against them was the al-Saba.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was given victory by the al-Saba, and ʿAd were destroyed by the al-Dabur" [Musnad Ahmad: 2/228; Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/22].

﴿And hosts you did not see﴾, and they were the angels, who did not fight that day. ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ The exegetes said: Allah sent upon them, during the night, a cold wind, and sent the angels, who uprooted the tent pegs, cut the ropes of the tent-canopies, extinguished the fires, overturned the cooking pots, and the horses ran about among one another. Allah cast terror into them, and the takbir of the angels grew loud on the sides of their camp, so that every chief of a tribe would say: "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" When they gathered around him, he would say: "Escape! Escape! You have been overtaken," because of the terror Allah had cast upon them, and they fled without any fighting.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi informed me, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Sulayti informed me, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Hasan informed me, from al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Ash'arani [in the Isfahan copy: al-Sha'rani], from ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn, from Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abu Saʿd Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Baqqal, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father. And ʿAqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, from Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi, from Salama, who said: Muhammad ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, both of whom said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and accompany him?" He said: "Yes, my nephew." He said: "And how did you used to act?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive greatly." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him, we would not have let him walk on the earth, but we would have carried him on our necks, and served him, and done such and such."

Then Hudhayfa said: "My nephew, by Allah, I saw myself on the night of the Confederates with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Trench, on a cold night, the like of whose cold I had never found before or after. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who will stand up and go to these people and bring us their news? Allah will admit him to Paradise.'" [7] [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 10/449; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/185.]

No man among us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said the like of it. The people fell silent and no man among us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a little of the night, then turned to us and said: "Is there a man who will stand up and look for us what the people have done, on condition that he will be my companion in Paradise?" No man stood up, out of the intensity of fear, the intensity of hunger, and the intensity of cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "O Hudhayfa!" I had no choice but to stand up when he called me. I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah," and I rose and came to him, while my two sides were trembling. He wiped my head and face and said: "Go to these people until you bring me their news, and do not do anything until you return to me."

Then he said: "O Allah, protect him from before him, behind him, on his right, on his left, above him, and below him." So I took my bow and tightened my joints, then I set off walking toward them as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I went and entered among the people, and Allah had sent upon them a wind which cut their tent-ropes, uprooted their tents, and carried off their horses, leaving nothing without destroying it. Abu Sufyan was sitting warming himself at the fire. I took my arrow and placed it on the string of my bow, but then I remembered the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not do anything until you return," so I returned the arrow to my quiver.

When Abu Sufyan saw what the wind and the hosts of Allah were doing to them, that no cooking pot, fire, or building would stay firm for them, he stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each man take the hand of his companion and see who he is." So I took the hand of the one sitting beside me and said: "Who are you?" He said: "Subhan Allah, do you not know me? I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." And behold, he was a man from Hawazin.

Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not woken up in a place of settlement. The horses and camels have perished, Banu Qurayza have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind what you see. So depart, for I am departing." Then he rose to his camel, which was tied, sat upon it, and struck it; it leapt up on three legs, and he did not release its tether until it was standing.

Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands. Allah repelled the confederates, and that is His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see﴾. He said: So I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and informed him of the news, and he laughed until his canine teeth showed in the darkness of the night. He said:

"Warmth left me, and the Prophet (ﷺ) brought me near, made me sleep at his feet, cast over me the edge of his garment, and pressed my chest against the sole of his foot."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾, meaning from above the valley, from the east side, and upon them were Malik ibn ʿAwf al-Nadari and ʿUyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari with a thousand of Ghatafan; with them Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi among Banu Asad, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab among the Jews of Banu Qurayza. ﴿And from below you﴾, meaning from the bottom of the valley, from the west side, and it was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb with Quraysh and those who followed him, and Abu al-Aʿwar ʿAmr ibn Sufyan al-Sulami from the side of the Trench. What prompted the Battle of the Trench, it is said, was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'s expulsion of Banu al-Nadir from their homes.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and one whom I do not accuse, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and from ʿAsim ibn Qatada, and from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, some of whose narrations enter into others. They said: Among the account of the Trench was that a group of Jews, including Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Hawdha ibn Qays, and Abu ʿAmmar al-Wa'ili, with a group from Banu al-Nadir and a group from Banu Wa'il, who are those who gathered the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), went out until they came to Quraysh in Mecca. They invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." Quraysh said to them: "O assembly of Jews, you are the People of the first Book and knowledge. Tell us: we differ with Muhammad, so is our religion better or his?"

They said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than them." He said: They are the ones about whom Allah revealed:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in idols and false deities…﴾ to His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire﴾ [Surat al-Nisa: 51–55].

When they said that to Quraysh, what they said pleased them, and they were eager for what they had invited them to, the war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So they resolved upon it and prepared for it. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays ibn Ghaylan, invited them to war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and informed them that they would be with them against him, and that Quraysh had already pledged themselves to that and had resolved upon it. They responded to them. So Quraysh went out, their leader being Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Ghatafan went out, their leader being ʿUyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr, with Banu Fazara; and al-Huwayrith ibn ʿAwf ibn Abi Jariya al-Murri with Banu Murra; and Mas'ud ibn Jabala ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif ibn Shahma ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hilal ibn Khalawa ibn Ashja' ibn Zayd ibn Ghatafan, with those of his people from Ashja' who followed him.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of them and of what they had resolved upon, he dug a trench around Medina. The one who suggested the trench to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Salman al-Farisi, and it was the first battle Salman witnessed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was then a free man. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we were in Persia and were besieged, we dug a trench around ourselves." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims with him worked on it until they perfected it.

We have mentioned the hadith of Salman concerning the manner of digging the Trench in Surat Al ʿImran. They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the Trench, Quraysh came and descended at the gathering place of al-Asyal, beyond it, between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba, with ten thousand of their Ahabish and those who followed them of Banu Kinana and the people of Tihama. Ghatafan and those who followed them of the people of Najd came and descended [at Dhanab Naqma] by the side of Uhud.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims went out and made their backs to Sal', with three thousand Muslims, and there he pitched his camp, with the Trench between him and the enemy. He ordered the women and children to be raised up into the fortresses. The enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadari, set out until he came to Kaʿb ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the holder of the covenant and pact of Banu Qurayza, who had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on behalf of his people and had pledged to that. When Kaʿb heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he locked his fortress against him, and he asked permission to enter but Kaʿb refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Kaʿb, open to me!" He said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what is between me and him, and I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness."

He said: "Woe to you, open to me so I may speak with you." He said: "I will not do it." He said: "By Allah, if you shut me out, it will only be over your little bit of dried food, so that I may eat with you from it." The man was cautious, but he opened to him. He said: "O Kaʿb, woe to you! I have brought you the glory of the age and a sea that has overflowed. I have brought you Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at the gathering place of al-Asyal beyond it, and Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Dhanab Naqma by the side of Uhud. They have pledged to me and made a covenant with me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him."

Kaʿb ibn Asad said to him: "You have come to me, by Allah, with the humiliation of the age, with a cloud that has poured out its water, thundering and lightning, yet holds nothing. Leave me and Muhammad and what I am upon. I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity."

Huyayy ibn Akhtab kept coaxing Kaʿb, stroking him on the crown and back, until he yielded to him, on condition that he gave him a covenant from Allah and a pledge: "If Quraysh and Ghatafan return without reaching Muhammad, I will enter with you into your share, until what befalls you befalls me." So Kaʿb ibn Asad broke his covenant and disavowed what was between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

When the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Saʿd ibn Muʿadh ibn al-Nuʿman ibn Imru' al-Qays, of Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbada ibn Dulaym, of Banu Saʿida ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, together with ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, brother of al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khuwat ibn Jubayr, brother of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.

He said: "Go and see whether what has reached us about these people is true. If it is true, then signal to me with a sign that I may understand, and do not weaken the arms of the people. If they are upholding the covenant between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." They set out until they reached them, and found them at the most wicked [of positions] of what had been reported about them. They said: "Who is the Messenger of Allah?" and they said: "There is no covenant between us and Muhammad, nor any pact." Saʿd ibn ʿUbada insulted them and they insulted him, and Saʿd was a man with a hot temper. Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insults." Then Saʿd and Saʿd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), greeted him, and said: "ʿAdl and al-Qara," meaning like the treachery of ʿAdl and al-Qara against the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Companions of al-Raji', Khubayb ibn ʿAdi and his companions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!" At that the trial grew great, fear intensified, and the enemy came upon them from above them and from below them, until the believers thought every kind of thought. Hypocrisy stirred among some of the hypocrites, until Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, said to them: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while one of us cannot even go out to relieve himself!" [Quoted at length in Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/157–159, the occasion of the verse.] ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾. Then Aws ibn Qayzi, of Banu Haritha, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and that was in the presence of men of his people. "So permit us to return to our homes, for they are outside Medina."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained, and the polytheists remained besieging him for some twenty nights, nearly a month, and there was no fighting between the two sides except shooting with arrows and pebbles. When the trial grew severe on the people, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to ʿUyayna ibn Hisn and to al-Harith ibn ʿAwf, the two leaders of Ghatafan, and offered them a third of the produce of Medina on condition that they return with those who were with them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. A peace was arranged between them and him, until they wrote the document, but the witnesses had not yet attested it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned this to Saʿd ibn Muʿadh and Saʿd ibn ʿUbada and consulted them about it. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it something God has commanded you, which we must carry out, or a matter you love and so you do it, or something you do for us?" He said: "No, rather it is for you. By Allah, I would not do this, except that I have seen the Arabs shooting at you from one bow and gathering against you from every side, so I wished to break their strength from you."

Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, we and these people were upon polytheism and the worship of idols, not worshipping Allah nor knowing Him, and they did not hope to eat from our produce except as guests or by purchase. Now that Allah has honoured us with Islam and strengthened us through you, shall we give them our wealth?! We have no need of this. By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword until Allah judges between us and them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions said: "Then you and that matter are yours." Saʿd took the document and erased what was written in it, then said: "Let them strive against us."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims remained in their state while the polytheists besieged them, and there was no fighting between them except that some horsemen of Quraysh, among them ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Abi Qays, brother of Banu ʿAmir ibn Lu'ayy, and ʿIkrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Hubayra ibn Abi Wahb, both of Makhzum, and Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Allah, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, and Mirdas, brother of Banu Muharib ibn Fihr, had armed themselves for battle, and they rode out on their horses and passed by Banu Kinana.

One of them, from Banu al-Harith, said: "O Banu Kinana, you will know today who the horsemen are!" Then they came and stopped at the Trench. When they saw it, they said: "By Allah, this is a trick, which the Arabs had never devised." Then they sought a narrow place in the Trench and struck their horses, and they burst through it, and their horses galloped about in the marshy ground between the Trench and Sal'.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) set out with a group of Muslims until he blocked the breach through which they had forced their horses, and the horsemen came toward them. ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd had fought at the Battle of Badr until a wound incapacitated him, so he had not witnessed [any other battle]. When it was the day of the Trench, he came out marked with a sign to show his position. When he and his horses stood still, ʿAli said to him: "O ʿAmr, you used to make a covenant with Allah that no man from Quraysh would invite you to two qualities without your accepting one of them." He said: "Indeed." He said: "I invite you to Allah, to His Messenger, and to Islam." He said: "I have no need of that." He said: "Then I invite you to single combat." He said: "Why, O nephew? By Allah, I do not wish to kill you."

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "But by Allah, I wish to kill you." Then ʿAmr became enraged, leapt down from his horse, struck or wounded its face, and turned to ʿAli. They grappled and fought, and ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) killed him.

And his cavalry fled in defeat until they plunged back through the trench in flight. [[On that day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The duel of ʿAlī with ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd is better than the deeds of my community until the Day of Resurrection." In another wording: "The striking of ʿAlī is better than the worship of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn)." See Mustadrak al-Sahihayn 3/32, Kanz al-ʿUmmal 6/158, and al-Sira al-Halabiyya 2/349.]] Along with ʿAmr, two men were killed: Munabbih ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbaq ibn ʿAbd al-Dar, who was struck by an arrow and died from it in Makkah; and Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi. Nawfal had plunged into the trench, became trapped in it, and they pelted him with stones. He said: "O company of the Arabs, a death better than this!" ʿAlī then descended to him and killed him. The Muslims then gained control of his body, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to sell them his body. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no need of his body or its price; do with him as you wish." So he left them free to take it.

ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, said: "On the day of the Trench we were in the fortress of Banu Harītha, which was one of the strongest fortresses of Madina. Umm Saʿd ibn Muʿadh was with us in the fortress, and that was before the veil was imposed upon us. Saʿd ibn Muʿadh passed by, wearing a coat of mail that was short, so that his entire forearm was exposed, and he had his spear in his hand, saying:

'Wait a little, the battle will witness a charge;
There is no harm in death when its appointed time comes.'"

His mother said: "Hurry, my son, for by Allah you have been delayed!" ʿĀʾisha said: "I said to her: 'O Umm Saʿd, by Allah, I wish Saʿd's coat of mail were more complete than it is,' and I feared for him where the arrow struck him." She said: "Saʿd was struck that day, and his artery (al-akhal) was cut. It is reported that whoever's artery was cut would not stop bleeding until he died. Ḥibbān ibn Qays ibn al-Ghurqa, one of Banu ʿĀmir ibn Lu'ayy, struck him. When he hit him, he said: 'Take it, for I am the son of al-Ghurqa!' Saʿd said: 'May Allah drown your face in the Fire!' Then Saʿd said: 'O Allah, if You have kept any of the war against Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than those who harmed Your Messenger, denied him and expelled him. And if You have ended the war between us and them, then make it a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until my eyes are cooled by Banu Qurayẓa,' who were his allies and clients in the Jahiliyya."

Muḥammad ibn Isḥaq ibn Yasār narrated, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father ʿAbbād, who said: "Ṣafiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was in the fortress of Ḥassān ibn Thābit." She said: "Ḥassān was with us in it, with the women and children."

Ṣafiyya said: "A man of the Jews passed by us and began circling the fortress. Banu Qurayẓa had gone to war and cut off what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there was no one between us and them to repel for us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were at the throats of their enemy and could not turn away from them to us if someone came to us." She said: "I said: 'O Ḥassān, this Jew, as you see, is circling the fortress, and by Allah I do not feel safe that he will point out our weak spot to the Jews behind us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions are occupied with us, so go down to him and kill him.'"

He said: "May Allah forgive you, O daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib! By Allah, you know I am not the one for this." She said: "When he said that to me and I saw nothing with him, I tucked up my garment, took a pillar, went down from the fortress to him, and struck him with the pillar until I killed him. When I finished with him, I returned to the fortress and said: 'O Ḥassān, go down to him and strip him, for what kept me from his spoils was only that he was a man.'" He said: "I have no need of his spoils, O daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib."

They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions remained in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described of fear and hardship, due to the support their enemy gave one another against them and their attack from above them and below them. Then Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn [Unayf] ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Qunfudh ibn Hilāl ibn Ḥalāwa ibn Ashja' ibn Zayd [[In Tarikh al-Tabari (2/242): Rabīth.]] ibn Ghaṭafān came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, but my people do not know of my Islam, so command me in whatever you wish.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You are only one man among us, so cause discord among them if you are able, for war is deception.'"

Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd went out until he came to Banu Qurayẓa, who had been his companions (nadīm) in the Jahiliyya. He said to them: "O Banu Qurayẓa, you know my affection for you and the special bond between me and you." They said: "You have spoken the truth; you are not suspected by us." He said: "Quraysh and Ghaṭafān have come to fight Muḥammad, and you have aided them against him. Quraysh and Ghaṭafān are not in the same situation as you. This is your land, where your wealth, your sons and your women are, and you cannot move away from it to another place. Quraysh and Ghaṭafān have their wealth, sons and women elsewhere. If they see a chance for plunder and booty they will seize it; otherwise they will return to their lands and leave you alone with the man, while the man is in your land, and you will have no power against him if he is left alone with you. So do not fight with the people until you take hostages from their nobles who will remain in your hands as a guarantee for you, that they will fight alongside you against Muḥammad until you finish with him." They said: "You have given sound and sincere advice."

Then he went out until he came to Quraysh, and said to Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and those with him of the men of Quraysh: "O company of Quraysh, you know my affection for you and my separation from Muḥammad. A matter has reached me which I believe is a duty upon me to convey to you, as sincere counsel. Keep it secret from me." They said: "We will."

He said: "You know that the Jews have regretted what they did between them and Muḥammad, and they have sent to him saying: 'We regret what we did.' Would it please you if we took men of the nobles of the two tribes, Quraysh and Ghaṭafān, and handed them over, so that you may cut off their necks, and then we will be with you against those who remain of them?"

Then he sent to them: "Yes." He added: "If the Jews send to you seeking hostages from your men, do not give them a single man from you." Then he went out until he came to Ghaṭafān and said: "O company of Ghaṭafān, you are my origin, my clan, and the people most beloved to me, and I do not think you suspect me." They said: "You have spoken the truth." He said: "Keep it secret from me." They said: "We will." Then he said to them the same as he had said to Quraysh, and warned them of what he had warned them of.

When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal of the fifth year, and this was among what Allah did for His Messenger, Abū Sufyān and the chiefs of Ghaṭafān sent ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl with a group from Quraysh and Ghaṭafān to Banu Qurayẓa. They said to them: "We are not a people who can remain. The hoof and the camel have perished. So go out to fight in the morning, until we finish with Muḥammad and settle what is between us and him."

They sent back to them: "Tomorrow is Saturday, a day on which we do nothing. Some of us had committed a transgression on it, and what befell him is not hidden from you. Moreover, we will not fight with you until you give us hostages from your men who will remain in our hands as a guarantee for us until we finish with Muḥammad. For we fear that if the war hurts you and the fighting becomes severe upon you, you will travel to your lands and leave us with the man in our land, and we have no power against Muḥammad."

When the messengers returned to them with what Banu Qurayẓa had said, Quraysh and Ghaṭafān said: "You know, by Allah, that what Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd told you is true." They sent to Banu Qurayẓa: "By Allah, we will not give you a single man from our men. If you want to fight, then come out and fight."

Banu Qurayẓa, when the messengers reached them with this, said: "What Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd mentioned to you is true. The people want nothing but that you fight, so that if they find an opportunity they seize it; and if not, they will slip away to their lands and leave you alone with the man in your land." They sent to Quraysh and Ghaṭafān: "By Allah, we will not fight with you until you give us hostages." They refused, and Allah sowed discord between them. Allah sent upon them a wind on cold, harsh, wintry nights, until they turned back and returned. "And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Allah, the Exalted, said: "When the eyes swerved (zāghat)," meaning they were turned and fixed, "and the hearts reached the throats (al-ḥanājir)," meaning they were displaced from their places until they reached the throats out of terror, "and you assumed about Allah assumptions." As for the hypocrites, they thought Muḥammad and his companions would be defeated and uprooted. As for the believers, they were certain that what Allah had promised them was true, [namely] that He would make His religion prevail "over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it." [[Extended in Tafsir al-Qurtubi 14/135–138, on the occasion of revelation, and Tarikh al-Tabari 2/243.]]

The reciters differed regarding His saying: al-ẓunūnā, al-rasūlā, and al-sabīlā. Those who affirmed the alif in them both in pause and in continuation were the people of Madina, al-Shām, Ayyūb, and ʿĀṣim through the transmission of Abū Bakr, and Abū ʿAmr through the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Kisāʾī through the transmission of Qutayba. They said: "Their alifs are firmly established in the ʿUthmānic codex and in all the codices of the other regions." Abū ʿAmr read them without an alif in all other transmissions, and Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb read them without an alif in both states, in accordance with the original form.

The rest read with the alif in pause and without it in continuation. They argued that the Arabs do this at the rhyme-endings of their poems and their hemistiches: they add an alif at the place of fatḥa when pausing, and they do not do this within the body of lines. So affirming the alif in these words is fitting, because they are the endings of verses, likened to rhyme.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "There the believers were tested" (hunālika ubtiliya al-mu'minūn), meaning they were examined and purified, so that the believer might be distinguished from the hypocrite. "And they were shaken (zulzilū) with a severe shaking," meaning they were moved and frightened. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read zalzālan with a fatḥa on the zāy; both are verbal nouns (maṣdar).

"And when the hypocrites say," meaning Muʿattib ibn Qushayr and his companions, "and those in whose hearts is a disease," meaning doubt and weakness of conviction, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." "And when a faction of them said," meaning from among the hypocrites, and they were Aws ibn Qayẓī and his companions. Muqatil said: they were from Banu Sālim. "O people of Yathrib," meaning Madina. Abū ʿUbayda said: Yathrib is the name of a land, and the city of the Messenger (peace be upon him) is in one part of it. "There is no station for you" is the reading of the majority with a fatḥa on the mīm, meaning there is no place for you to remain. al-Sulamī read it with a ḍamma on the mīm, meaning there is no staying for you; this is the transmission of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim. "So return to your homes": they commanded them to flee from the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn ʿAbbās said: the Jews said to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions among the hypocrites: "What drives you to kill yourselves at the hands of Abū Sufyān and his companions? Return to Madina." So they returned. "And a group of them asked permission of the Prophet" to return to their homes, and they were Banu Ḥāritha ibn al-Ḥārith, "saying: 'Indeed our houses are exposed (ʿawra),'" meaning they are empty [and unprotected], and they are on the side facing the enemy, and we fear for them from the enemy and thieves. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read ʿawira with a kasra on the wāw, meaning walls that are short, with gaps and openings. The Arabs say: "So-and-so's house is ʿawra" when it is not fortified, and "the horseman has become ʿawira" when there is a gap in his defense against blows. The poet said:

"When you meet them, you will not find in the house one with an exposed side,
nor a guest stricken, nor a neighbor left destitute." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi 14/148.]]

Allah, the Exalted, said: "And they were not exposed; they intended only to flee." "And if it had been entered upon them," meaning if these armies they fight against had entered Madina "from its sides," its surroundings and areas, its singular being qaṭr, and there is another form, qaṭr and aqṭār.

"Then they were asked to commit fitna," meaning shirk, "they would have given it." The reading of the people of Ḥijāz is with a short alif, meaning they would have come to it and done it, and they would have reverted from Islam and disbelieved. The others read with the long vowel, meaning they would have given it. They said: when there is a request, there is giving.
