They have not gone away, meaning they have not turned back from their fight, although some of them and groups among them have already departed. ﴿And if the confederates should come [again],﴾ that is, if they should return to you a second time.

﴿They would wish, out of fear and cowardice, that they were out in the desert among the Bedouins,﴾ that is, outside among the Bedouins, ﴿asking about your news,﴾ that is, your news and what your affair has come to. The common reading is with a light (non-doubled) sīn, while ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and Yaʿqūb, in the narration of Ruways and Zayd, read it doubled and lengthened, meaning yatasāʾalūn, that is, some of them ask others.

﴿And if they were among you, they would fight only a little,﴾ meaning these hypocrites, out of ostentation and not for the sake of God. And if that little had been for Allah, it would have been much.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example,﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿an excellent model.﴾ ʿĀṣim read ʾUswa (with a ḍamma on the alif) here and in Surat al-Mumtaḥina, while the others read it with a kasra, and both are dialectal forms, like ʿudwa and ʿidwa, rushwa and rishwa, kiswa and kiswa. Yaḥyā ibn Thābit used to read it with a kasra here and with a ḍamma in the other place.

Abu ʿUbayd said: We do not know of any distinction that Yaḥyā made between these two places.

The exegetes said: That is, ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example,﴾ a good sunna: that you should support him, back him, not stay behind him, and not prefer yourselves over his self or over the place of his desire, just as he did when his incisor was broken, his forehead above the eyebrow was wounded, his uncle Hamza was killed, and he was afflicted with various kinds of harm. Despite all this, he consoled you with himself. So you too should do likewise and follow his sunna.

﴿For those who hope for Allah and the Last Day, and remember Allah much,﴾ in ease and in trial.

Then He mentioned the believers and their affirmation of the promises of Allah, exalted is He, so He said: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said: this is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke truly.﴾ They said this in submission to the command of Allah and in affirmation of His promise.

Allah's promise to them is His saying: ﴿Do you think you will enter Paradise while the like of those who passed away before you has not come to you? …﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Surely the help of Allah is near.﴾

[Surat al-Baqara: 214.]

﴿And it did not increase them except in faith and submission.﴾

His saying: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow,﴾ meaning he has completed his pledge and fulfilled his covenant, so he persevered in jihad until he was martyred. Naḥb means a vow, and naḥb also means death. Dhu al-Rumma said:

"On the evening the Ḥārithīs fled, after
he had fulfilled his naḥb at the meeting of the two peoples, Hawbar."

[Hawbar: the name of a man, and naḥb: the stake.]

[Lisan al-ʿArab: 5/248; Taj al-ʿArus: 3/609.]

That is, he died. Muqatil said: ﴿Fulfilled his naḥb,﴾ meaning his term, so he was killed while faithful, meaning Hamza and his companions.

It was also said: ﴿Fulfilled his naḥb,﴾ that is, he exerted himself [to the utmost] in fulfilling his covenant, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so exerted himself in his journey for the whole day and night, and did not stop." Jarir said:

"At Ṭakhfa we fought the kings, and our horses,
on the evening of Bisṭām, ran with exertion."

[Ṭakhfa: the name of a place; al-mujālada: striking.]

﴿And among them is he who awaits martyrdom,﴾ ﴿and they did not change [their word, their covenant, their vow] in any way.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Nahr ibn Asad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, from Anas, who said: And Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Marani narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, from ʿAbdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: My uncle Anas ibn al-Nadr, after whom Anas was named, was absent from the battle of Badr, and this grieved him when he returned. He said: "I was absent from the first battle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) witnessed. By Allah, if Allah, mighty and majestic, lets me witness a battle, Allah will surely see what I do."

He said: When the day of Uhud came and the Muslims were routed, he said: "O Allah, I disown before You what these polytheists have brought, and I apologise to You for what these have done," meaning the Muslims. Then he walked forward with his sword, and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh met him. He said: "O Saʿd, by Him in whose hand my soul is, I smell the fragrance of Paradise beyond Uhud."

Saʿd said: "I could not do what Anas did, O Messenger of Allah." We found him among the slain with more than eighty wounds, from sword blows, spear thrusts and arrow shots, and they had mutilated him. We did not recognise him until his sister recognised him by his molars. This verse was revealed: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await, and they did not change in any way.﴾

He said: We used to say that this verse was revealed concerning him and his companions.

Abdullah ibn Hamid narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan, from Jaghwayh ibn Muhammad al-Tirmidhi, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hazm, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAʾisha, concerning His saying: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true … Among them are those who fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await,﴾ she said: Among them was Talha ibn ʿUbayd Allah, who stood firm with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until his hand was struck, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Talha has made Paradise obligatory."

And with its chain, from Salih, from Muslim ibn Khalid, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Najih: that Talha ibn ʿUbayd Allah on the day of Uhud was shielding the Prophet (peace be upon him) with his body among the horsemen, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had become exhausted. He said: An arrow came flying straight towards the Prophet (ﷺ), and Talha protected him with his hand, and it struck his little finger. He said: "Ḥass!" Then he said: "In the name of Allah." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "If you had said 'Bismillah' (in the name of Allah), the angels would have lifted you up until they brought you into Paradise."

[Al-Ṭabaqat al-Kubra: 3/217.]

Muʿawiya ibn Ishaq narrated, from ʿAʾisha bint Talha, from ʿAʾisha the Mother of the Believers, who said: I was in my house, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions were in the courtyard, with a curtain between me and them, when Talha came. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to see a man walking on the earth who has fulfilled his vow, let him look at Talha."

[Majma al-Zawa'id: 9/148.]

Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Babawayh ibn Qahrawayh informed me, saying: Abu ʿAbdullah Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar al-Sufi informed me, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad al-Wasiti, from Makki ibn Ibrahim, from al-Salt ibn Dinar, from Ibn Nadr, from Jabir, from Abu ʿAbdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever would like to see a martyr walking on the face of the earth, let him look at Talha ibn ʿUbayd Allah."

﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ ﴿And Allah turned back those who disbelieved, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, in their rage; they gained no good, meaning victory and triumph. And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting, through the angels and the wind. And Allah is Strong, Mighty.﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And He brought down those who supported them,﴾ meaning those who aided the Confederates, Quraysh and Ghatafan, against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people of faith, and they were the Banu Qurayza. That was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the morning of the night when the Confederates turned back to their lands and the Messenger (peace be upon him) and the Muslims withdrew from the trench to Medina and laid down their weapons, when it was noon, Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wearing a turban of brocade, on a mule with a saddle, over which was a silk cloak, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was washing his head, and he had washed one side. [Jibril] said: "Have you laid down the weapons, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "May Allah pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights, and I have only now returned from pursuing the people. Allah commands you, O Muhammad, to march to Banu Qurayza, and I am heading to Banu Qurayza. So rise up against them, for I have cut their bowstrings, opened their gates, and left them in tremor and confusion." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered a caller, who called out: "Whoever is listening and obedient, let him not pray ʿAṣr except in Banu Qurayza."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sent ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib ahead with his banner towards them, and people hastened after it. ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib set out until, when he came close to the fortresses, he heard from them an ugly saying against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He turned back and met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the road and said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not draw near to these vile people." He said: "Why? I suppose you heard harm from them against me." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said any of that." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew near their fortresses, he said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine, has Allah disgraced you and sent down His vengeance upon you?" They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you are not ignorant."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed by his companions at al-Ṣawwarīn before he reached Banu Qurayza and said: "Has anyone passed by you?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi passed by us, on a white mule with a saddle over which was a brocade cloak." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That was Jibril, sent to Banu Qurayza to shake their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts."

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came to Banu Qurayza, he alighted at a well of theirs in a part of their property called Yurayqa. People caught up with him, and some men came after the late evening prayer (ʿishāʾ) without having prayed ʿAṣr, because of the Messenger of Allah's saying: "Let none of you pray ʿAṣr except in Banu Qurayza." So they prayed ʿAṣr there after the ʿishāʾ prayer. Allah did not reproach them for that in His Book, nor did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuke them for it.

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/181, the verse's entry.]

He said: The Messenger of Allah besieged them for twenty-five nights until the siege exhausted them, ﴿and He cast terror into their hearts.﴾ Ḥuyayy ibn Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayza in their fortress when Quraysh and Ghatafan withdrew from them, and Kaʿb ibn Asad [the leader of Qurayza] had kept to what he had covenanted. When they became certain that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not turn away from them until he fought them, Kaʿb ibn Asad said to them: "O assembly of Jews, there has come upon you what you see, and I am putting three options before you. Choose whichever you wish." They said: "What are they?" He said: "We follow this man and believe him. By Allah, it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent, and that he is the one you find in your Book. Then you will be safe for your homes, your wealth, your sons and your women." They said: "We will never abandon the judgment of the Torah, nor exchange it for anything else."

He said: "If you refuse this, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad and his companions with drawn swords, and leave behind us no burden that would concern us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we will have left behind nothing to fear for. If we prevail, then by my life, we will surely take wives and children." They said: "We will kill these wretched ones, and there is no good in life after them."

He said: "If you refuse this, then tonight is the night of Saturday, and perhaps Muhammad and his companions have felt secure during it, so come down, perhaps we can catch Muhammad and his companions unawares." They said: "We would be desecrating our Sabbath and doing in it what those before us did, as you know, and what befell them of transformation is not hidden from you." He said: "Not a single man among you has spent a single night since his mother bore him without being resolute."

Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): "Send us Abu Lubaba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir, the brother of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, who were allies of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sent him to them. When they saw him, the men rose to him, and the women and children came rushing to him, weeping in his face. He was moved by them, and they said: "O Abu Lubaba, do you think we should come down to the judgment of Muhammad?" He said: "Yes," and pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning: it is slaughter.

Abu Lubaba said: "By Allah, my feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then Abu Lubaba went off on his own way and did not come to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), until he tied himself to one of the pillars in the mosque. He said: "I will not leave this place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I have done," and he vowed to Allah that he would never set foot in Banu Qurayza's land, and that Allah would never see him in a land where he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger.

When the news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he was delayed by it, he said: "As for me, had he come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done this, I will not release him from his place until Allah accepts his repentance." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed the acceptance of Abu Lubaba's repentance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in the house of Umm Salama. Umm Salama said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) laughing at dawn, so I said: 'Why are you laughing, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah make you laugh always?'"

He said: "Abu Lubaba has been forgiven." She said: "Shall I give him the good news of this, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, if you wish." He said:

She stood at the door of her chamber, and that was before the veil was imposed on the women. She said: "O Abu Lubaba, rejoice, for God has accepted your repentance." He said: The people went to him to release him, but he said: "No, by God, not until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the one who releases me with his own hand." When he passed by him going out to the morning prayer, he released him.

He said: Then Tha'laba ibn Sha'ba, Usayd ibn Sha'ba and Usayd ibn Ubayd, who were a group from Banu Hazl, not from Banu Qurayza or al-Nadir, and their lineage was beyond that, being cousins of the people, embraced Islam on the night in which Qurayza descended to the judgment of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). On that night, Amr ibn Sa'di al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which was commanded that night by Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari. When he saw him, he said: "Who is this?" He said: "Amr ibn Sa'di." Amr had refused to join Banu Qurayza in their treachery against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he had said: "I will never betray Muhammad." When Muhammad ibn Maslama recognized him, he said: "O God, do not deprive me of the rewards of the noble." Then he let him go, and he went off on his own way until he spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina. Then he left, and no one knows where he went in God's land until this day. His matter was mentioned to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "That is a man whom God saved by his fidelity."

Some people claim that he [Abu Lubaba] had been tied to a post among those of Banu Qurayza who were tied up when they descended to the judgment of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and that in the morning his post was lying there, and no one knew where he had gone. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made that statement, and God knows best.

When they awoke, they descended to the judgment of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Aws stirred. They said: "O Messenger of God, they are our clients rather than the clients of Khazraj, and you have done what you know to the clients of Khazraj yesterday." Before Qurayza, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had besieged Banu Qaynuqa', who were allies of Khazraj, and they descended to his judgment, and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him for them and he granted them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:
"Are you not content, O assembly of Aws, that a man from among you should judge concerning them?" They said: "Yes."
He said: "Then the matter is up to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." [10] [[al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/139.]] Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the tent of a Muslim woman called Rufayda, in his mosque. She used to treat the wounded and devoted herself to serving whoever among the Muslims was afflicted. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said to his people when the arrow struck him at the Trench: "Put him in the tent of Rufayda until I visit him soon." [11] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 21/181.]]

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) appointed him as judge over Banu Qurayza, his people came to him, lifted him onto a donkey, and had spread for him a cushion of leather. He was a massive man. Then they came along with him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying:
"O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) only appointed you over them so that you would be good to them." When they pressed him, he said: "The time has come for Sa'd that he should not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause." Some of those who were with him returned to the house of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, and before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them, the men of Banu Qurayza were informed of the words they had heard from him.

When he reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the Messenger said: "Stand up for your chief and bring him down." They stood up to him and said:
"O Abu Amr, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has appointed you over your clients so that you may judge concerning them." Sa'd said: "Will you pledge to me the covenant and oath of God that the judgment concerning them is what I judge?" They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon me [is the covenant] from here, in the direction where the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is," while he turned away from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) out of reverence for him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Yes."

Sa'd said: "Then I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the women and children be taken captive." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Sa'd: "You have judged by the judgment of God from above the seven heavens." Then they were brought down, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confined them in the house of Bint al-Harith, a woman from Banu al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to the market of Medina, which is its market today, dug trenches in it, then sent for them and struck their necks. They were in those trenches, brought out to him in groups, and among them was the enemy of God, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred, and the one who gave the highest figure said they were between eight hundred and nine hundred.

It is said: They said to Ka'b ibn Asad, as he was being led to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in groups: "O Ka'b, what do you think will be done with us?" Ka'b said: "In every situation you do not understand! Do you not see that the caller does not return, and that whoever is taken away from you does not come back? By God, it is death." Their practice continued in this way until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) finished with them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of God, was brought, wearing a garment of tafsi color, which had been cut from every side, at the width of a fingertip [fingertip by fingertip], so that it would not be stripped from him. His hands were tied to his neck with a rope. When he saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he said: "By God, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes God is forsaken." Then he turned to the people and said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of God; it is the Book of God and His decree, and a massacre written for the Children of Israel." Then he sat down, and his neck was struck. Hubal [[In Tafsir al-Tabari (21/185) it is Jabal ibn Jawwal.]] ibn Hawwas [al-Tha'labi] [[This appears so in the original, and perhaps it is: al-Tha'labi.]] said:
"By your life, Ibn Akhtab did not blame himself,
but whoever forsakes God is forsaken.
He strove until his soul reached its excuse,
and the one who shakes [the earth] causes every shaker of glory to shake." [[al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/143.]]

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Aisha, who said: No woman of Banu Qurayza was killed except one woman. She said: "By God, she was with me, talking to me and laughing heartily, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was killing their men in the market. Then a caller called out her name: 'Where is so-and-so?' She said: 'I am, by God.' I said: 'Woe to you, what is wrong with you?' She said: 'I am to be killed.' I said: 'Why?' She said: 'Because of something I did.'" He said: She was taken away and her neck was struck. Aisha used to say: "I do not forget how amazed I was at her, her good spirits and her much laughter, though she knew she was going to be killed."

Al-Waqidi said: The name of that woman was Bunana, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had killed Khallad ibn Suwayd, having dropped a millstone on him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) summoned her, and her neck was struck, and Khallad ibn Suwayd was avenged. Ali and al-Zubayr used to strike the necks of Banu Qurayza while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat there.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri that al-Zubayr ibn Bata al-Qurazi, who was called Abu Abd al-Rahman, had once shown a favor to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas in the pre-Islamic period, on the day of Bughath, when he had taken him captive and pulled his forelock, and then let him go. On the day of Qurayza, al-Zubayr came to him, being an elderly man, and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do you recognize me?" He said: "Would one like me not know one like you?" He said: "I wish to repay you with your favor to me." He said: "The noble repays the noble." Then Thabit went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, al-Zubayr had a favor upon me, and I have a debt to him, and I wish to repay it, so grant me his life." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "He is yours."

So he went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has granted me your life." He said: "An old man with no family and no children, what would he do with life?" Thabit went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, [grant me] his family and children." He said: "They are yours." So he went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your wife and children, and they are yours." He said: "A household of the Hijaz with no property, how will they survive in that state?" Thabit went to the Messenger of God and said: "O Messenger of God, [grant me] his property." He said: "It is yours." So he went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your property, and it is yours." He said: "O Thabit, what became of the one whose face was like a Chinese mirror in which the maidens of the tribe saw themselves, Ka'b ibn Asad?" He said: "He was killed." He said: "What became of the lord of the settled and the nomad, Huyayy ibn Akhtab?" He said: "He was killed." He said: "What became of our vanguard when we charged, and our defender when we attacked, Azal ibn Samaw'al?" He said: "He was killed." He said: "What became of the two councils?" meaning Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayza and Banu Amr ibn Qurayza. He said: "They went; they were killed." He said: "I ask you, O Thabit, by the favor I have with you, to join me with my people, for by God there is no good in life after these." "So here I am, patient before God until I meet my beloved." Thabit brought him forward and struck his neck. When his words "until I meet my beloved" reached Abu Bakr, he said: "By God, he will meet them in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever."

Thabit ibn Qays said concerning that:
"My pledge was fulfilled, for I am noble,
and I am steadfast when the people deviate from patience.
Al-Zubayr was the greatest of men in favor to me,
yet when his two wrists were bound in captivity.
I came to the Messenger of God that I might release him,
and the Messenger of God was a sea flowing for us." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/252.]]

They said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had commanded the killing of those of them who were captured. Salma bint Qays, the mother of al-Mundhir and the sister of Sulayt ibn Qays, who was one of the maternal aunts of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), had prayed with him toward both qiblas and had pledged allegiance to him with the pledge of women, asked him for Rifa'a ibn Samaw'al al-Qurazi, who was an adult man. He took refuge with her, and he had known her before that. She said: "O Prophet of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, grant me Rifa'a ibn Samaw'al, for he claims that he will pray and eat camel meat." So he granted him to her [and she spared him]. [[Thus in the original.]]

They said: Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) divided the property, women and children of Banu Qurayza among the Muslims. He announced on that day two shares for horses and one share for men, and set aside the fifth from it. The horseman received three shares: two for the horse and one for the rider, and the foot soldier who had no horse received one share. The horses on the day of Banu Qurayza numbered thirty-six. This was the first spoil in which the two shares were applied, and the fifth was taken from it. So the practice was established according to it, and what passed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning it, the divisions were made and the practice continued in the campaigns. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Sa'd ibn Zayd al-Ansari, brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, with captives from the captives of Banu Qurayza to Najd, and he bought horses and weapons with them.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had chosen for himself from their women Rayhana bint Amr ibn Khanafa, one of the women of Banu Amr ibn Qurayza. She remained with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he died, while she was in his possession. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was eager to marry her and to impose the veil upon her, but she said: "O Messenger of God, rather leave me as a possession, for that is lighter for me and for you." So he left her. She had disliked Islam when she was captured and refused anything but Judaism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was displeased with her and felt something in himself about her matter. While he was with his companions, he heard the sound of sandals behind him, and he said: "This is Tha'laba ibn Sha'ba bringing me the good news of Rayhana's embracing Islam." He came and said: "O Messenger of God, Rayhana has embraced Islam." This pleased him.

When the matter of Banu Qurayza was concluded at dawn, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh went out. This was because, after he had given his judgment concerning Banu Qurayza, he supplicated, saying: "O God, You know that there was no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who denied Your Messenger. O God, if You have left any of the war of Quraysh against Your Messenger, then let me remain for it; and if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You." His wound burst open, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had him brought back to his tent, which had been pitched for him in the mosque.

Aisha said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) attended him, along with Abu Bakr and Umar. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could tell Umar's weeping from Abu Bakr's, and I was in my chamber. She said: They were, as God, Mighty and Majestic, described them: "compassionate among themselves" [Q. 48:29].

Alqama said: [that is, his mother] [[He means Aisha.]] How did the Messenger of God (ﷺ) behave? She said: His eye did not weep over anyone, but when his grief intensified, he would simply hold his beard. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Only six men from the Muslims were killed on the day of the Trench, and three men from the polytheists were killed. On the day of Qurayza, Khallad ibn Suwayd ibn Tha'laba was killed from the Muslims: a millstone was dropped on him and crushed him. [[See: Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/252.]]

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from the Trench and Qurayza, he said: "Now we will campaign against them, meaning Quraysh, and they will not campaign against us." It was so until God granted His Messenger the conquest of Mecca. The conquest of Banu Qurayza occurred at the end of Dhu'l-Qa'da in the fifth year after the Hijra. This is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "And He brought down those of the People of the Book who backed them from their fortresses" [Q. 33:26], meaning their strongholds and fortresses; its singular is sayssiya, and from it is said of the horn of a cow sayssiya, and of the spur of a rooster and of the weaver's comb sayssiya. The poet said:
"Like the fall of the combs upon the stretched weave."
"And He cast terror into their hearts; a group you killed" [Q. 33:26], meaning the men, "and a group you took captive" [Q. 33:26], meaning the women and children. "And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their possessions, and a land you had not trodden before" [Q. 33:27]. Yazid ibn Ruman, Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: this means Khaybar. Qatada said: We used to be told that it is Mecca. Al-Hasan said: Persia and Byzantium. Ikrima said: every land that will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection. "And God is over all things capable" [Q. 33:27].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 28–32:

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release.﴾ ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾

The exegetes said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) had asked him for something of worldly goods, and they hurt him by asking for more maintenance and by jealousy. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) abandoned them, and he swore that he would not approach them for a month, and he did not come out to his companions. They said: "What is the matter with him?" Umar said: "If you wish, I will go and find out for you what is the matter with him." So he went to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began saying to myself: "What can I say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that perhaps he will be pleased?" So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen So-and-so, and she asked me for maintenance, so I slapped her with a slap," and he said: "That is what made me sit apart from you."

Then Umar went to Hafsah and said: "Do not ask the Messenger of Allah for anything; whatever need you have, come to me." He said: Then he followed the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and began to speak to them. He said to Aishah: "Does it please you that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you, so that you would either cease, or there would be revealed concerning you a Qur'an?" He said: Then Umm Salamah said to him: "O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you but to interfere between the Messenger of Allah and his wives?! Who asks a woman except her husband?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed these verses.

At that time, under the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were nine wives: five from Quraysh: Aishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint Umar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; and Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Khaybariyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah. When the verse of choice was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began with Aishah, for she was the most beloved of them to him. He gave her the choice and recited the Qur'an to her, and she chose ﴿Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾. The joy was seen in the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the others followed her in that.

Qatadah said: When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that, restricted him to them, and said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ — the verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar: Al-Zuhri informed me, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: When twenty-nine nights had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, and you have entered upon me after twenty-nine, which I count." He said: "Indeed the month is twenty-nine." Then he said: "O Aishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hastening in it until you consult your two parents." She said: Then he recited to me this verse:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾

Aishah said: "By Allah, he knew that my parents would not have commanded me to separate from him." She said: "In this, should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me that Aishah said: "Do not inform your fellow wives that I have chosen you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sent me as a conveyer of the message and did not send me as one who seeks to embarrass."

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamdun informed us, from [Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan] [[In the Isfahan copy: Ibn al-Sharqi.]], from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Uthman ibn Umar, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from [Abu] [[In the Isfahan copy: Ibn.]] Salamah, that Aishah said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: "I am going to tell you a matter, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents." Then he said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾"

I said: "In this should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." She said: Then the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did the same as I did.

His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency…﴾ Al-Jahdari read it with the feminine ta' (تأت). Others read it with the ya' (يأت). ﴿...clear indecency﴾: a manifest disobedience. ﴿...her punishment will be doubled in the Hereafter, twofold.﴾ Ibn Amir and Ibn Kathir read: nudaʿʿif (نضعّف) with the nun, the ʿayn kasra and shaddah, without alif, and (al-ʿadhab) in the accusative.

Abu Amr and Yaʿqub read yudaʿʿif (يضعّف) with the ya', the ʿayn fathah and shaddah, and (al-ʿadhab) in the nominative. Abu Amr said: "I read this one alone with shaddah because of His saying: twofold (ḍiʿfayn)." The rest read nuḍaʿif (نضاعف) with alif and raised the b・ (ب) of (al-ʿadhab), and both are dialects, like "bāʿada" and "baʿuda."

Abu Amr and Abu Ubaydah said: "ḍaʿʿaftu al-shayʾ" means when I made it like its counterpart, and muḍaʿafah means I made it into its multiples.

﴿And that is easy for Allah.﴾ His saying: ﴿And whoever of you is obedient (yaqnut)...﴾ means: yuṭiʿ (obeys).

Qatadah said: Every qunut in the Qur'an is obedience. [The common reading is taqnut with the ta'] [[Thus it appears in the Isfahan copy: the common reading is with the ya' except what is narrated from Ibn Amir and Yaʿqub that they read taqnut with the ta'.]] Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (yaʿmal) (yu'tihā) with the ya'. Others read them with the ta'.

Al-Farra' said: He said (yaʾti) and (yaqnut) because man (من), a particle that stands in place of a noun, is used to express the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And among them is one who looks at you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 43], and He said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 42], and He said: ﴿And whoever of you is obedient to Allah﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 31]. And al-Farazdaq said about the dual:

"Come, for if you pledge to me that you will not betray me, you will be like the two who, O wolf, accompany each other."

﴿...to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice﴾ — meaning, like my other wives among the women.

﴿And We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾ — meaning Paradise.

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun, from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Yazid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', who said: Umar used to recite in the dawn prayer Surah Yusuf and al-Ahzab, and when he reached ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾ he raised his voice with it. It was said to him, and he said: "I am reminding them of the covenant."

The scholars differed concerning the ruling on the choice. Umar and Ibn Mas'ud said: If a man gives his wife the choice and she chooses her husband, there is nothing upon him; and if she chooses herself, she is divorced [three times] [[In the Isfahan copy: then three.]]. The exegetes said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) had asked him for something of worldly goods, and they hurt him by asking for more maintenance and by jealousy. Umar said: "If you wish, I will go and find out for you what is the matter with him." So he went to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began saying to myself: "What can I say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that perhaps he will be pleased?" So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen So-and-so, and she asked me for maintenance, so I slapped her with a slap," and he said: "That is what made me sit apart from you."

Then Umar went to Hafsah and said: "Do not ask the Messenger of Allah for anything; whatever need you have, come to me." He said: Then he followed the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and began to speak to them. He said to Aishah: "Does it please you that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you, so that you would either cease, or there would be revealed concerning you a Qur'an?" He said: Then Umm Salamah said to him: "O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you but to interfere between the Messenger of Allah and his wives?! Who asks a woman except her husband?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed these verses.

At that time, under the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were nine wives: five from Quraysh: Aishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint Umar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; and Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Khaybariyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah. When the verse of choice was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began with Aishah, for she was the most beloved of them to him. He gave her the choice and recited the Qur'an to her, and she chose ﴿Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾. The joy was seen in the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the others followed her in that.

Qatadah said: When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that, restricted him to them, and said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ — the verse.

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, and you have entered upon me after twenty-nine, which I count." He said: "Indeed the month is twenty-nine." Then he said: "O Aishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hastening in it until you consult your two parents." She said: Then he recited to me this verse:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾

Aishah said: "By Allah, he knew that my parents would not have commanded me to separate from him." She said: "In this, should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me that Aishah said: "Do not inform your fellow wives that I have chosen you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sent me as a conveyer of the message and did not send me as one who seeks to embarrass."

Then he said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾"

I said: "In this should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." She said: Then the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did the same as I did.

His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency…﴾ Al-Jahdari read it with the feminine ta' (تأت). Abu Amr and Yaʿqub read yudaʿʿif (يضعّف) with the ya', the ʿayn fathah and shaddah, and (al-ʿadhab) in the nominative. Abu Amr said: "I read this one alone with shaddah because of His saying: twofold (ḍiʿfayn)." Qatadah said: Every qunut in the Qur'an is obedience. ﴿...to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice﴾ — meaning, like my other wives among the women.

﴿And We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾ — meaning Paradise.
