Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun, from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Yazid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', who said: Umar used to recite in the dawn prayer Surah Yusuf and al-Ahzab, and when he reached ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾ he raised his voice with it. It was said to him, and he said: "I am reminding them of the covenant."

The scholars differed concerning the ruling on the choice. Umar and Ibn Mas'ud said: If a man gives his wife the choice and she chooses her husband, there is nothing upon him; and if she chooses herself, she is divorced [three times] [[In the Isfahan copy: then three.]]. This is also the view of Malik.

Al-Shafi'i said: If he intended divorce in the giving of choice, it is a divorce; otherwise it is not. Those who did not consider the choice itself a divorce argued by His saying: ﴿and I will release you with a fair release﴾, and by the saying of Aishah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us the choice, and we chose him, and we did not count it as a divorce."

His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women, if you fear Allah. So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.﴾ Al-Farra' said: He did not say "like one of them," because aḥad (أحد) is general and suitable for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 285], and He said: ﴿Then there is none of you who could withhold from Him﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 47].

﴿...lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾ — meaning, lewdness and weakness of faith. ﴿...but speak with appropriate speech﴾ — sound and good.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 28–32:

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release.﴾ ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾

The exegetes said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) had asked him for something of worldly goods, and they hurt him by asking for more maintenance and by jealousy. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) abandoned them, and he swore that he would not approach them for a month, and he did not come out to his companions. They said: "What is the matter with him?" Umar said: "If you wish, I will go and find out for you what is the matter with him." So he went to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began saying to myself: "What can I say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that perhaps he will be pleased?" So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen So-and-so, and she asked me for maintenance, so I slapped her with a slap," and he said: "That is what made me sit apart from you."

Then Umar went to Hafsah and said: "Do not ask the Messenger of Allah for anything; whatever need you have, come to me." He said: Then he followed the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and began to speak to them. He said to Aishah: "Does it please you that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you, so that you would either cease, or there would be revealed concerning you a Qur'an?" He said: Then Umm Salamah said to him: "O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you but to interfere between the Messenger of Allah and his wives?! Who asks a woman except her husband?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed these verses.

At that time, under the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were nine wives: five from Quraysh: Aishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint Umar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; and Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Khaybariyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah. When the verse of choice was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began with Aishah, for she was the most beloved of them to him. He gave her the choice and recited the Qur'an to her, and she chose ﴿Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾. The joy was seen in the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the others followed her in that.

Qatadah said: When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that, restricted him to them, and said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ — the verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar: Al-Zuhri informed me, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: When twenty-nine nights had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, and you have entered upon me after twenty-nine, which I count." He said: "Indeed the month is twenty-nine." Then he said: "O Aishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hastening in it until you consult your two parents." She said: Then he recited to me this verse:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾

Aishah said: "By Allah, he knew that my parents would not have commanded me to separate from him." She said: "In this, should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me that Aishah said: "Do not inform your fellow wives that I have chosen you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sent me as a conveyer of the message and did not send me as one who seeks to embarrass."

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamdun informed us, from [Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan] [[In the Isfahan copy: Ibn al-Sharqi.]], from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Uthman ibn Umar, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from [Abu] [[In the Isfahan copy: Ibn.]] Salamah, that Aishah said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: "I am going to tell you a matter, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents." Then he said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life…﴾ until ﴿a great reward.﴾"

I said: "In this should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode." She said: Then the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did the same as I did.

His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency…﴾ Al-Jahdari read it with the feminine ta' (تأت). Others read it with the ya' (يأت). ﴿...clear indecency﴾: a manifest disobedience. ﴿...her punishment will be doubled in the Hereafter, twofold.﴾ Ibn Amir and Ibn Kathir read: nudaʿʿif (نضعّف) with the nun, the ʿayn kasra and shaddah, without alif, and (al-ʿadhab) in the accusative.

Abu Amr and Yaʿqub read yudaʿʿif (يضعّف) with the ya', the ʿayn fathah and shaddah, and (al-ʿadhab) in the nominative. Abu Amr said: "I read this one alone with shaddah because of His saying: twofold (ḍiʿfayn)." The rest read nuḍaʿif (نضاعف) with alif and raised the b・ (ب) of (al-ʿadhab), and both are dialects, like "bāʿada" and "baʿuda."

Abu Amr and Abu Ubaydah said: "ḍaʿʿaftu al-shayʾ" means when I made it like its counterpart, and muḍaʿafah means I made it into its multiples.

﴿And that is easy for Allah.﴾ His saying: ﴿And whoever of you is obedient (yaqnut)...﴾ means: yuṭiʿ (obeys).

Qatadah said: Every qunut in the Qur'an is obedience. [The common reading is taqnut with the ta'] [[Thus it appears in the Isfahan copy: the common reading is with the ya' except what is narrated from Ibn Amir and Yaʿqub that they read taqnut with the ta'.]] Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (yaʿmal) (yu'tihā) with the ya'. Others read them with the ta'.

Al-Farra' said: He said (yaʾti) and (yaqnut) because man (من), a particle that stands in place of a noun, is used to express the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And among them is one who looks at you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 43], and He said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 42], and He said: ﴿And whoever of you is obedient to Allah﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 31]. And al-Farazdaq said about the dual:

"Come, for if you pledge to me that you will not betray me, you will be like the two who, O wolf, accompany each other."

﴿...to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice﴾ — meaning, like my other wives among the women.

﴿And We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾ — meaning Paradise.

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun, from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Yazid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', who said: Umar used to recite in the dawn prayer Surah Yusuf and al-Ahzab, and when he reached ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾ he raised his voice with it. It was said to him, and he said: "I am reminding them of the covenant."

The scholars differed concerning the ruling on the choice. Umar and Ibn Mas'ud said: If a man gives his wife the choice and she chooses her husband, there is nothing upon him; and if she chooses herself, she is divorced [three times] [[In the Isfahan copy: then three.]]. This is also the view of Malik.

Al-Shafi'i said: If he intended divorce in the giving of choice, it is a divorce; otherwise it is not. Those who did not consider the choice itself a divorce argued by His saying: ﴿and I will release you with a fair release﴾, and by the saying of Aishah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us the choice, and we chose him, and we did not count it as a divorce."

His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women, if you fear Allah. So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.﴾ Al-Farra' said: He did not say "like one of them," because aḥad (أحد) is general and suitable for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 285], and He said: ﴿Then there is none of you who could withhold from Him﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 47].

﴿...lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾ — meaning, lewdness and weakness of faith. ﴿...but speak with appropriate speech﴾ — sound and good.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 33, verse 33 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And stay in your houses﴾. Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi' and 'Asim read it with a fatha on the qaf (*waqarna*). Others read it with a kasra. Whoever reads it with a fatha, its meaning is *waqarna*, i.e., remain in your houses, from your saying "I settled (*qarartu*) in the place, I settle (*aqarru*) with a settling (*qararan*)." *Qarartu* and *aqarru* are two dialects. The first *ra'* (which is the middle radical of the verb) was dropped and its vowel was transferred to the *qaf*, so it took a fatha, like their saying *zalilta* and *zalta* (in the form *zalta*).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So you remain jesting﴾ (56:65), and ﴿You continued (*zalta*) devoted to it﴾ (20:97). The original form is *zalilta*, and one of the two *lam*s was dropped. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Abi 'Abla, *waqararna* with a fatha on the *ra'*, according to the original form in the dialect of those who say *qarartu aqarru qararan*.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Our teachers among the people of Arabic used to reject this reading, but it is permissible in our view, like His saying ﴿*zaltum*﴾." Whoever reads it with a kasra on the *qaf*, it is an imperative from *al-waqar* (dignity, gravity), like your saying from *al-wa'd* (promise): *idn* (*'idna*), and from *al-wasl* (connection): *ṣil'n*, meaning: "be people of dignity," that is, calm, quiet and deliberate, from their saying: "So-and-so *waqara* (becomes dignified), *yaqaru*, *wuquran*, when he is still and at rest."

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: My father told me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, who said: "Someone who heard 'A'isha reciting *waqarna fi buyutikunna* told me, and she would weep until her head-covering (*khimar*) was soaked."

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from 'Abd Allah ibn Humayd, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Hisham, from Muhammad, who said: "I was told that it was said to Sawda, wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him):

'Why don't you perform the Hajj or the 'umra as your sisters do?' She said: 'I have performed the Hajj and the 'umra, and Allah the Exalted commanded me to remain in my house. By Allah, I will not leave my house until I die.'"

He said: "By Allah, she did not leave the door of her chamber until her funeral was carried out."

His saying: ﴿And do not display your adornment (*tabarruj*) as in the first days of ignorance﴾ (33:33). Mujahid and Qatada said: *tabarruj* is strutting, arrogance and coquetry. It was also said: it is showing adornment and displaying charms to men. Regarding "the first ignorance" they differed. Al-Sha'bi said: it is the period between 'Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them both). Abu al-'Aliya said: it is the time of Dawud and Sulayman, and a woman would wear a shirt of pearls, unsewn at the sides, so that her back would be visible through it.

Al-Kalbi said: the ignorance is the time in which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born. Women of that time would take a coat of mail made of pearls, wear it, and then walk in the middle of the road with nothing on but that, presenting themselves to men. That was in the time of the tyrant Nimrod, and at that time all the people were disbelievers.

Al-Hakam said: it is the period between Adam and Nuh, eight hundred years. Their women were the ugliest of women and their men were handsome, so a woman would desire a man for herself.

'Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited this verse and said: "The first ignorance was between Nuh and Idris (peace be upon them both), and it lasted a thousand years. Two lineages of the children of Adam existed: one of them dwelt in the plain and the other dwelt in the mountain. The men of the mountain were beautiful, but the women were ugly, and the women of the plain were beautiful, but the men were ugly. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain in the form of a youth and hired himself to him, serving him. Iblis made something like the instrument with which shepherds pipe, and he produced a sound the people had never heard before. This reached those around them, so they flocked to him to listen to it, and they made a festival that they would gather for once a year. The women would display themselves to the men and the men would adorn themselves for the women. Then a man from the people of the mountain came upon them while they were at that festival, and he saw the women and their beauty. He went to his companions and told them about it, so they moved to them and settled among them, and immorality spread among them. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and do not display your adornment as in the first ignorance﴾."

Qatada said: it is the period before Islam. ﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity (*rijs*), O people of the House (*Ahl al-Bayt*), and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ (33:33). "*Rijs*" is the sin that Allah forbade women from. This was said by Muqatil. Qatada said: it means evil. Ibn Zayd said: it means Satan.

"O people of the House" means: O people of the house of Muhammad. "And purify you with a thorough purification" means: from the filth of the ignorance. Mujahid said: "*rijs*" is doubt, and "purify you" is from polytheism.

They differed concerning who is meant by His saying "O people of the House." A group said: it refers specifically to the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and the address was in the masculine because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them, and when the masculine and feminine are combined, the masculine takes precedence.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Affan, who said: Abu Yahya informed me, from Salih ibn Musa, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾ in reference to the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him)." He said: "And 'Abd Allah recited: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom﴾ (33:34)."

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Ubaydi, from Ahmad ibn Najda, from al-Hammani, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Asbagh ibn 'Alqama. And 'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed me, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ibn [Abu] [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Abu.]] Humayd informed me, from Yahya ibn Wadih, from al-Asbagh ibn 'Alqama, from 'Ikrima concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾. He said: "It is not what you think. It refers specifically to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

He said: "'Ikrima used to proclaim this in the market." Muqatil also held this view and said: "It means all the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him), with no man among them."

[[(The statements of the exegetes and scholars on its being specific to the People of the Cloak) Abu Bakr al-Naqqash said in his tafsir: "Most of the exegetes agreed that it was revealed concerning 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God's blessings be upon them" (*Jawahir al-'Iqdayn*: 198, first chapter, and *Tafsir Ayat al-Mawadda*: 112).

And my master Muhammad ibn Ahmad Bunays said in his commentary on al-Busiri's *Hamziyya*: "Most of the exegetes hold that it was revealed concerning 'Ali, Fatima and the two grandsons, may Allah be pleased with them" (*Lawami' Anwar al-Kawkab al-Durri*: 2/86).

And the scholar my master Muhammad Jasus said in his commentary on the *Shama'il*: "... Then al-Hasan ibn 'Ali came and he admitted him, then al-Husayn came and entered with them, then Fatima came and he admitted her, then 'Ali came and he admitted him, then he said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾." This is an indication that they are the ones meant by "People of the House" in the verse (*Sharh al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya*: 1/107, appendix to the chapter on what was reported about the Messenger of Allah's clothing).

Al-Samhudi said: "A group, among them al-Kalbi, said: they are 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn specifically, on account of the earlier hadiths" (*Jawahir al-'Iqdayn*: 198, first chapter).

Al-Tahawi said in *Mushkil al-Athar*, after mentioning the hadiths of the Cloak: "What we have narrated in these reports, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to Umm Salama, of what we have mentioned in them, indicates that it was not intended that they were among those meant in the verse recited in this chapter, and that those meant by what is in them are the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, to the exclusion of others" (*Mushkil al-Athar*: 1/230, hadith 782, chapter 106, on what was narrated from the Prophet concerning the verse).

And after mentioning the hadiths of the Prophet's (ﷺ) recitation of the verse at Fatima's door, he said: "In this too is evidence that this verse concerns them" (*Mushkil al-Athar*: 1/231, hadith 785, chapter 106).

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: "I say: the family of Muhammad (ﷺ) are those whose affairs return to him. Whoever's affairs were most intensely and completely tied to him, they are the family. There is no doubt that Fatima, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn had the strongest ties with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this is known by mass-transmitted report, so it is necessary that they be the family."

He also said: "People have differed about the family. It was said: they are the relatives; it was said: they are his community. If we take it to mean kinship, then they are the family; if we take it to mean the community who accepted his call, then they too are the family. So it is established that in all interpretations they are the family. As for others, are they included under the term 'family'? That is disputed." Al-Kashshaf's author reported that when the verse of love (*al-mawadda*) was revealed, it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, from your relatives, who are these whose love has become obligatory upon us?" He (ﷺ) said: "'Ali, Fatima and their two sons." So it is established that these four are the relatives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and when this is established, they must be especially honored, and several things indicate it..." etc. (*Tafsir al-Razi*: 27/166, on the verse of love, 42:23).

He said in another place: "Views differ concerning the People of the House. The better view is to say: they are his descendants, his wives, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are among them, and 'Ali is among them, because he was of his household through his association with the Prophet's daughter and his constant companionship with the Prophet (ﷺ)" (*Tafsir al-Razi*: 25/209).

Abu Bakr al-Hadrami said in *Rashfat al-Sadi*: "What the majority of scholars have held, what the great imams have affirmed, and what the proofs and evidences have established is that the People of the House meant in the verse are our master 'Ali, Fatima and their two sons... Their being singled out in this way was from him (ﷺ) only by a divine command and heavenly revelation... The hadiths on this subject are numerous, and from what I have cited of them it is known with certainty that the People of the House meant in the verse are 'Ali, Fatima and their two sons, may Allah be pleased with them. There is no regard for what the author of *Ruh al-Bayan* mentioned, that the specification of the five mentioned, peace be upon them, as the People of the House is among the sayings of the Shi'a, for that is pure recklessness and is astonishing; and by the hadiths preceding and what is in the books of the Sunni people the dawn becomes clear to one with eyes..." up to his saying: "The community has agreed upon this, so there is no need to lengthen the argument for it" (*Rashfat al-Sadi min Bahr Fada'il Bani al-Nabi al-Hadi*: 13, 14, 16, Cairo ed., and 23 and 40, Beirut ed., first chapter, mention of their excellence through what Allah revealed concerning them).

Ibn Hajar said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ (33:33). Most of the exegetes hold that it was revealed concerning 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn (*al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa*: 143, Cairo ed., and 220, Beirut ed., chapter 11, on the verses revealed concerning them, first verse).

He said in another place, after affirming the blessing upon the family: "So the meaning of the People of the House in it, and in everything that has come concerning their excellence or the excellence of the family or the near kin, is all his family (ﷺ), and they are the believers of the Banu Hashim and al-Muttalib. By this it is known that he (ﷺ) said all of that" (his meaning being the reports that omitted "the family," as in the two *Sahihs*, and the reports that affirmed "the family"). "So some narrators memorized what others did not. Then the joining of the wives and the descendants with the family in many reports suggests that these two are not of the family, which is clear regarding the wives according to the more correct view on the family, that they are the believers of Banu Hashim and al-Muttalib. As for the descendants, they are of the family according to all the views. So mentioning them after the family is to indicate their great nobility" (*al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa*: 146, Cairo ed., and 224-225, Beirut ed., chapter 11, the verses revealed concerning them, second verse).

Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on *Sahih Muslim*: "As for his saying in the other report: 'His wives are of the People of his House, but his House's people are those who are forbidden the sadaqa.' He said: 'And in the other report: "We said: Are his wives of his House's people? He said: No."' These two reports apparently contradict each other, and what is well known in most reports outside Muslim is that he said: 'His wives are not of his House's people.' So the first report is interpreted to mean that they are of his House's people in the sense that they dwell in it and he supports them... and they are not included among those forbidden the sadaqa" (*Sahih Muslim with al-Nawawi's commentary*: 15/175, hadith 6175, Book of Virtues, the virtues of 'Ali).

Al-Samhudi said: "Al-Nawawi, in his *Sharh al-Muhadhdhab*, related another view of our companions: that they are his 'itra (kin), those who are attributed to him (ﷺ). He said: They are the children of Fatima and their descendants forever. Al-Azhari and others related it from him." End of quotation.

Some of them related it with the addition of the wives entering (*Jawahir al-'Iqdayn*: 211, first chapter, and in its margin: *Sharh al-Muhadhdhab*: 3/448).

Imam Majd al-Din al-Fayruzabadi said: "The tenth question: Do women enter into such an address (blessing upon the Prophet)? The majority of the legal theorists (*usuliyyun*) held that they do not enter, and al-Shafi'i stated it explicitly; he was criticized for it, and the critic was in error" (*al-Sila wa al-Bishr fi al-Salat 'ala Khayr al-Bashar*: 32, first chapter).

Mulla 'Ali al-Qari said: "The more correct view is that the excellence of their sons follows the order of the excellence of their fathers, except the children of Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her, for they are given precedence over the children of Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, because of their closeness to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They are the pure 'itra and the good descendants whom Allah removed impurity from and purified with a thorough purification" (*Sharh Kitab al-Fiqh al-Akbar* of Abu Hanifa: 210, a question on the preference of the Companions' children).

Al-Samhudi said after mentioning the hadiths on the Prophet's placing his family in his own position, and mentioning the verse of mubahala (mutual invocation) and that it concerns them: "These are the People of the Cloak, so they are the ones meant by the two verses (the mubahala and the purification)" (*Jawahir al-'Iqdayn*: 204, first chapter).

Al-Hamzawi said: "The one who argues against generality was supported by what was reported through sound chains: 'That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came with 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn...' and he mentioned the hadiths of the Cloak, until he said: It is possible that the specification by the Cloak to these four is due to a divine command, which is indicated by the hadith of Umm Salama, who said: 'I raised the cloak to enter with them, but he pulled it from my hand'" (*Mashariq al-Anwar* of al-Hamzawi: 113, fifth chapter of the third section, the excellence of the People of the House).

Al-Qastallani said: "The preponderant view is that they are those for whom the sadaqa is forbidden, as al-Shafi'i stated and as the majority chose, and it is supported by his saying (ﷺ) to al-Hasan ibn 'Ali: 'We, the family of Muhammad, the sadaqa is not lawful for us.' It was also said that by the family of Muhammad is meant his wives and descendants." Then he mentioned after that the words of Ibn 'Atiyya, who said: "The majority hold that they are 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and their proof is (*'ankum* and *wa yutahhirakum*) with the *mim*" (*al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya*: 2/517, 529, second chapter of the seventh section).

Abu Mansur Ibn 'Asakir al-Shafi'i said, after mentioning the statement of Umm Salama: "'The People of the House were the Messenger of Allah, 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn': this is a sound hadith... and the verse was revealed specifically concerning these mentioned persons" (*Kitab al-Arba'in fi Manaqib Ummahat al-Mu'minin*: 106, hadith 36, mention of what was narrated of the excellence of all of them).

Ibn Balban (d. 739 AH) said in his arrangement of *Sahih Ibn Hibban*: "Mention of the report explicitly stating that these four whom we previously mentioned are the People of the House of the Chosen One (ﷺ)," then he mentioned the hadith of the verse's revelation concerning them, from Wathila (*al-Ihsan bi-Tartib Sahih Ibn Hibban*: 9/61, hadith 6937, Book of Virtues; the hadith will come in full). Ibn al-Sabbagh said in his *Fusul*: "The People of the House, according to what the exegetes mentioned in the commentary on the verse of mubahala, and according to what is reported from Umm Salama, are: the Prophet (ﷺ), 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn" (*Muqaddimat al-Mu'allif*: 22).

Al-Hakim al-Naysaburi said, after the hadith of the Cloak and the blessing upon the family and that it concerns them: "I only cited it so that the seeker may know that the People of the House and the family are all one" (*al-Mustadrak*: 3/148, Book of Knowledge, mention of the virtues of the People of the House, peace be upon them).

Al-Hafiz al-Kanji said: "The sound view is that the People of the House are 'Ali, Fatima and the two al-Hasans" (*Kifayat al-Talib*: 54, first chapter).]]

Al-Qunduzi said in his *Yanabi' al-Mawaddah*: Most of the exegetes (*mufassirun*) hold that it was revealed concerning ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. The pronoun in ﴿ʿankum wa-yuṭahhirakum﴾ (﴿from you and purify you﴾) is masculine, which indicates this. (*Yanabi' al-Mawaddah*: 1/294, Istanbul ed. 1301 AH, and 352, Najaf ed., chapter 59, fourth section.)

Muhibb al-Din al-Tabari said: A chapter on demonstrating that Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the *ahl al-bayt* (the people of the household) referred to in His saying, ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾ (33:33), and the Prophet's (ﷺ) covering them with a cloak and his supplication for them. (*Dhakhair al-ʿUqba*: 21.)

Al-Sakhawi said in *al-Qawl al-Badi'* on the form of the prayer in the tashahhud: The reference is to those upon whom charity is forbidden. He mentioned that this is the view chosen by the majority and the explicit position of al-Shafiʿi, and that the position of Ahmad is that they are the *ahl al-bayt*. It was also said that the intended meaning is his wives and his descendants... (From the margin of *al-Sawaʿiq al-Muhriqa* of ʿAbd al-Wahhab ʿAbd al-Latif: 146, Cairo ed. 1385 AH.)

Al-Qasimi said: But are his wives among his *ahl al-bayt*? There are two opinions, which are two narrations from Ahmad.
The first is that they are not among the *ahl al-bayt*, and this is narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam. (*Tafsir al-Qasimi*, titled *Mahasin al-Ta'wil*: 13/4854, at the verse, Cairo, ʿIsa al-Halabi.)

Al-Alusi said: You know that what is authentically established from the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, "I am leaving among you two successors (*khalifatayn*); and in another narration, two weighty things (*thaqalayn*): the Book of Allah, a rope extended between heaven and earth, and my offspring, my *ahl al-bayt*. They will not separate until they come to me at the Basin (*al-Hawd*)," indicates that the purified women are not included among the *ahl al-bayt* who are one of the two weighty things. (*Tafsir Ruh al-Maʿani*: 12/24, at the verse.)

The poet al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Jabir al-Hubl said in his *Diwan*:
The family of the Prophet are the followers of his creed
from among the believers of his close kin by lineage.
This is the statement of Ibn Idris, which the scholars narrated from him,
so he turned away from the path of falsehood.
Our view is that they are the children of Fatimah, and this is correct without doubt or hesitation.
(*Jinayat al-Akwaʿ*: 28.)

Al-Hafiz al-Badakhshani said: "The people of the cloak" (*ʿAl al-ʿAba'*) refers to these individuals, because it is authentically reported from ʿAʾishah, Umm Salamah and others, through many narrations, that the Prophet (ﷺ) covered these four with a cloak that he was wearing. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾.

Tawfiq Abu ʿIlm said: In my opinion, the *ahl al-bayt* are the people of the cloak: ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and whoever descends from the lineage of al-Zahra' and the father of the two grandsons (Abu al-Hasanayn), may Allah be pleased with them all. (*Ahl al-Bayt*: 92, appendix to the first chapter, and 8, the introduction.)

In a passage responding to ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Bukhari, he said: As for his claim that the purpose of the verse of purification is the wives, we have clarified, in a manner that leaves nothing more to add, that what is intended by *ahl al-bayt* is the pure progeny (*ʿitrah*), not the wives. (*Ahl al-Bayt*: 35, first chapter.)

He also said: As for what the larger and greater group of exegetes rely upon, it is manifest in what is narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning five: me, ʿAli, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah." (*Ahl al-Bayt*: 13, first chapter.)

Al-Shawkani said in *Irshad al-Fuhul*, refuting those who say it is specific to the women: This is answered by saying that it has been established by a sound proof that it was revealed concerning ʿAli, Fatimah, and the two grandsons. (*Irshad al-Fuhul ila Tahqiq al-Haqq fi ʿIlm al-Usul*: 83, eighth section of the third objective; and *Ahl al-Bayt* of Tawfiq Abu ʿIlm: 36, first chapter.)

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Shami said: The major books of the Sunnah and all the books of the Shiʿah have agreed that the intended meaning of *ahl al-bayt* in the verse of purification is the Prophet (ﷺ), ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, because they are those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained as the intended meaning of *ahl al-bayt* in the verse. Every statement that contradicts the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whether distant or near, is to be thrown against the wall. The Messenger's (ﷺ) explanation takes precedence over the explanation of anyone else, since no one knows the intent of his Lord better than he does. (*Jinayat al-Akwaʿ*: 125, sixth chapter.)

Shaykh al-Shablanji said: Moreover, what the Prophet (ﷺ) did when he wished to hold the mubahalah (mutual imprecation) with the delegation of Najran, as the exegetes mentioned, supports the view that they are ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. (*Nur al-Absar*: 122, Hyderabad ed., and 223, Qom ed., second chapter, on the virtues of al-Hasan and al-Husayn.)

Shaykh al-Sindi said in his book (*Dirasat al-Labib fi al-Uswah al-Hasanah bi-l-Habib*): This investigation into the explanation of "*ahl al-bayt*" determines the intended meaning of them in the verse of purification, together with many explicit sound hadiths proclaiming that the intended meaning of them is the pure five, may Allah be pleased with them all. We have some pages in verifying this, a volume in our notebook, which the seeker of truth must consult. (Cited from *ʿAbaqat al-Anwar*: 1/350, Qom ed., and 911, Isfahan ed., section on the hadith of the two weighty things.)

Al-Rifaʿi said: It was also said: ʿAli, Fatimah and their two sons, and this is the reliable view upon which the majority of scholars rely. (*al-Mashraʿ al-Rawi*: 1/17.)

Dr. ʿAbbas al-ʿAqqad said: The exegetes differed concerning who the *ahl al-bayt* are.
As for Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in his *Tafsir* (6/783), al-Zamakhshari in his *Kashshaf*, al-Qurtubi in his *Tafsir*, *Fath al-Qadir* of al-Shawkani, al-Tabari in his *Tafsir*, al-Suyuti in *al-Durr al-Manthur* (5/169), Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani in *al-Isabah* (4/407), al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak*, al-Dhahabi in his *Talkhis* (3/146), and Imam Ahmad in the third volume, page 259, they all said: The *ahl al-bayt* are ʿAli, the Lady Fatimah al-Zahra', al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them. He then proceeded to cite the evidences. (*Fatimah al-Zahra'* by al-ʿAqqad: 70, Cairo, Dar al-Maʿarif, third edition.)

Others said: By it the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) meant ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them.

ʿAqil ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani informed me, from al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, narrated to me by Ibn al-Muthanna, from Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Rayyan al-Ghubari, from Musdal, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAtiyyah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This verse was revealed concerning me, ʿAli, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾." (*Majma' al-Zawa'id*: 9/167.)

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father, from Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Numayr, from ʿAbd al-Malik, meaning Ibn Abi Sulayman, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Someone who heard Umm Salamah narrated to me that she mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house when Fatimah came to him with a pot containing *harirah*, and she entered with it to him. He said to her: "Call your husband and your two sons." She said: So ʿAli, al-Hasan and al-Husayn came and entered upon him and sat eating from that *harirah*, while he was on his bed on a raised platform (*dukkan*), and beneath him was a Khaybari cloak. She said: I was in the chamber praying, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾.

She said: So he took the excess of the cloak and covered them with it, then he extended his hand and raised it toward heaven, then said: "O Allah, these are my *ahl al-bayt* and my close intimates (*hamati*), so remove from them the impurity and purify them thoroughly." She said: I put my head into the room and said: "And am I with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You are on the way to good, you are on the way to good."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Thaqafi informed me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from Yazid ibn Harun, from al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab, who said: A paternal cousin of mine from the Banu al-Harith ibn Taym Allah, called (Majma'), narrated to me, saying: I entered with my mother upon ʿAʾishah, and my mother asked her: "Did you see your departure on the day of the Camel?" She said: "It was a decree from Allah the Glorified." Then she asked her about ʿAli, and she said: "You ask me about the most beloved of people to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the husband of the most beloved of people to the Messenger of Allah. I saw ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered under a garment, then said: 'O Allah, these are my *ahl al-bayt* and my close intimates, so remove from them the impurity and purify them thoroughly.'"

She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I from your family?" He said: "Step aside, for you are on the way to good."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Abu Habish al-Muqri', who said: Abu al-Qasim al-Muqri' informed me, saying: Abu Zurʿah informed me, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Shaybah narrated to me, Ibn Abi Fudayk informed me, Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to me, from Isma'il ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Tayyar, from his father, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the mercy descending from heaven, he said: "Who will call?" twice. Zaynab said [*as is noted, the speaker is sometimes Umm Salamah and sometimes Zaynab, and in some narrations ʿAʾishah; the scholars, among them Ibn Hajar and al-Samhuri, explained that the verse was revealed several times in the houses of Fatimah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab and ʿAʾishah, and I have elaborated on that together with what relates to the verse in the book *Tahharat Al Muhammad* (ﷺ)*]: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Call for me ʿAli, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn." He said: So he placed al-Hasan on his right and al-Husayn on his left, and ʿAli and Fatimah in front of him, then covered them with a Khaybari cloak. Then he said: "O Allah, every prophet has a household, and these are my household." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾, the verse.

Zaynab said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not enter with you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Stay where you are, for you are on the way to good, if Allah wills." (*Musnad Ahmad*: 6/304; *Sunan al-Tirmidhi*: 5/361.)

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed me, from Muhammad ibn Musʿab, from al-Awza'i, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi ʿAmmar, who said: I entered upon Wathilah ibn al-Asqaʿ, and with him there were people who mentioned ʿAli and reviled him, so I reviled him too. When they stood up, he said to me: "Did you revile this man?" I said: "I saw the people reviling him, so I reviled him along with them."

He said: "Shall I not tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" I said: "Yes." He said: "I went to Fatimah to ask her about ʿAli, and she said: 'He has gone toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So I sat, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came with ʿAli, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, each one of them holding the hand of the other, until he entered. He brought ʿAli and Fatimah near and seated them before him, and seated al-Hasan and al-Husayn each on a thigh. Then he wrapped his garment, or he said his cloak, around them, then recited this verse: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾. Then he said: 'O Allah, these are my *ahl al-bayt*, and my *ahl al-bayt* have the better claim.'"

It was also said: They are the Banu Hashim.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Habish al-Muqri', from Muhammad ibn ʿImran, who said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' informed me, from his father, from Saʿid ibn Masruq, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I adjure you by Allah regarding my *ahl al-bayt*," twice. We said to Zayd ibn Arqam: "And who are his *ahl al-bayt*?" He said: "Those who are forbidden to receive charity: the family of ʿAli, the family of al-ʿAbbas, the family of ʿAqil, and the family of Jaʿfar."

Abu ʿAbd Allah informed me, saying: Abu Saʿid Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn ʿUmar ibn Habish al-Razi informed me, from Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Shibli Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, who said: Abu Kurayb informed me, from Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from Nufay' Abu Dawud, from Abu al-Hamra', who said: I stayed in Madinah nine months, as if it were one day, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to come every morning and stand at the door of ʿAli and Fatimah and say: "The prayer." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾.

Abu ʿAbd Allah informed me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Razi, from al-Harith ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khazin, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbbayah ibn al-Rib'i, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah divided creation into two halves, and placed me in the better of the two halves. This is the saying of Him, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And the companions of the right hand—what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ (56:27). So I am the best of the companions of the right hand."

Then He divided the two halves into thirds, and placed me in the best third. This is His saying: ﴿So the companions of the right hand—what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand—what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost﴾ (56:8–10). So I am among the foremost [and I am among the best of the foremost]. Then He divided the thirds into tribes, and placed me in the best tribe. This is His saying: ﴿And We made you nations and tribes﴾ (49:13), the verse, and I am the most righteous of the children of Adam and the most honored of them before Allah, and without boasting.

Then He divided the tribes into houses, and placed me in the best house. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾ (33:33).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verses 34–38:

﴿Remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and the wisdom.﴾ "The verses of God" means the Qur'an, and "the wisdom" means the Sunnah (the Prophet's practice), according to Qatadah. Muqatil said: the rulings and admonitions of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, God is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾

Its statement: ﴿Indeed, God is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾

Its statement: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ (the verse). The reason for this is that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of God, God has mentioned men in the Qur'an and has not mentioned women with good. There is no good among us by which we are mentioned. We fear that our obedience will not be accepted from us." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah and Unaysah bint Ka'b al-Ansariyyah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Why does our Lord mention men in the Qur'an and not mention women in anything of His Book? We fear that there is no good in them, and God has no need of them." So this verse was revealed.

Uthman ibn al-Hakam narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah, who said: I heard Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him), say: "I said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'O Messenger of God, why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are mentioned?'"

She said: "Then one day at noon I was startled by nothing but a inkwell on the pulpit while I was combing my hair. I braided my hair, then went out to one of the rooms of my house and placed my ear near the palm-branch (the wall of the room). Then he was saying on the pulpit: 'O people, indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ to His saying: ﴿...and a great reward.﴾'"

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It reached me that Asma bint Umays returned from Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. She entered upon the wives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Has anything of the Qur'an been revealed about us?" They said: "No." So she came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, indeed the women are in loss and ruin." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And why is that?" She said: "Because they are not mentioned with good as men are mentioned." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shabbah, from al-Furati [that is Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati, author of the Tafsir (Qur'anic commentary), known as al-Bustani], from Ibrahim ibn Sa'id, from Ubaydullah, from Shayban, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn al-Aqram, from al-Aghar Abi Muslim, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wakes up at night and wakes his wife, and they both pray two rak'ahs together, they will both be written among ﴿the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him.﴾"

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan, from Jaghuyah ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Hanzalah al-Tamimi, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Israfil came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Say, O Muhammad: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except with God, as many as what He knows, as much as the weight of what He knows, and as much as the fill of what He knows." Whoever says it, six qualities will be written for him: he will be written among ﴿the men who remember God much﴾, he will be better than one who remembers Him night and day, he will have a planting in Paradise, his sins will fall away from him as the dry leaves of a tree fall away, God will look upon him, and whoever God looks upon, He will not punish.

Mujahid said: A servant does not become of ﴿those who remember God much﴾ until he remembers God standing, sitting, and lying on his side.

Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: Whoever entrusts his affair to God is included in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾. Whoever affirms that God is his Lord and that Muhammad is His Messenger, and his heart does not contradict his tongue, is included in His saying: ﴿...the believing men and believing women...﴾. Whoever obeys God in the obligatory acts and the Messenger in the Sunnah is included in His saying: ﴿...the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women...﴾. Whoever guards his speech from falsehood is included in His saying: ﴿...the truthful men and truthful women...﴾. Whoever prays and does not know who is on his right and left is included in His saying: ﴿...the humble men and humble women...﴾. Whoever is patient in obedience, patient against sin, and patient in calamity is included in His saying: ﴿...the patient men and patient women...﴾. Whoever gives charity of a dirham every week is included in His saying: ﴿...the charitable men and charitable women...﴾. Whoever fasts the white days of each month (the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of the lunar month) is included in His saying: ﴿...the fasting men and fasting women...﴾. Whoever guards his private parts from what is not lawful is included in His saying: ﴿...the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them...﴾. Whoever prays the five prayers with their due rights is included in His saying: ﴿...the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him. God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

His statement, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (the verse).

It was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh ibn Ri'ab ibn al-Nu'man ibn Habarah ibn Murrah ibn Ghanm ibn Dawdan al-Asadiyyah, and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh. Zaynab's mother was Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) proposed to her on behalf of his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had bought Zayd in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) from Ukaz; he had been among the captives of the Jahiliyyah. He freed him and adopted him. So Zayd was an Arab in the Jahiliyyah and a freedman in Islam.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) proposed to Zaynab, she was pleased, [thinking] that he was proposing for himself. When she learned that he was proposing on behalf of Zayd, she refused and objected and said: "I am the most complete of the women of Quraysh and the daughter of your aunt. I would not do that, O Messenger of God, and I do not want it for myself." Her brother Abdullah said the same. Zaynab was fair and beautiful, but there was sharpness in her. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair...﴾ meaning Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his sister Zaynab. ﴿...that they should have any choice in their affair.﴾

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/16, the verse referenced.]

﴿...the choice...﴾ means the selection. The reading of the common people is "al-khiyarah" with a kasrah on the kha' and a fathah on the ya'. Ibn al-Sumayt read it with a sukun on the ya', and both are dialectal forms. ﴿...in their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾

She offered herself (in marriage) to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I have accepted." Then he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah, and she and her brother were displeased and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), yet he married us to his slave." He said: "No, by God, O Messenger of God, I have seen nothing from her but good, but she magnifies herself over me by her nobility and hurts me with her tongue." When her waiting period ended, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Zayd: "I do not find anyone more trustworthy in my own soul than you. Go to Zaynab and propose to her on my behalf."

Whoever fasts the white days of each month (the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of the lunar month) is included in His saying: ﴿...the fasting men and fasting women...﴾. I braided my hair, then went out to one of the rooms of my house and placed my ear near the palm-branch (the wall of the room). [Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/16, the verse referenced.]

Ibn al-Sumayt read it with a sukun on the ya', and both are dialectal forms. ﴿...in their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾

So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) married her to Zayd, and he consummated the marriage with her. She offered herself (in marriage) to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "I have accepted." Then he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah, and she and her brother were displeased and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), yet he married us to his slave." He said: "What is the matter with you? Has something about her made you suspicious?" He said: "No, by God, O Messenger of God, I have seen nothing from her but good, but she magnifies herself over me by her nobility and hurts me with her tongue." So I turned my back to her and said: 'O Zaynab, rejoice, for the Messenger of God is proposing to you.' She rejoiced at that and said: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord.' Then she went to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿We married her to you.﴾ So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) married her and consummated the marriage with her. Ibn Abbas said: "It is her love." Qatadah said: "He wished that he had divorced her." ﴿And you feared the people.﴾ Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: "You were shy of them." It was said: "You feared the blame of people, that they would say: he ordered a man to divorce his wife, then married her after he divorced her." ﴿And God has more right that you fear Him.﴾ Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Aishah said: "No verse was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that was harder on him than this verse."

It has been narrated from Zayn al-Abidin concerning this verse what:

Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Talhah ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub, who both said: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid said, from Ibn Abi Mihran: Muhammad ibn Yahya Abi Umar al-Arni narrated to me, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who said: "We heard it from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who repeated it and said: Ali ibn al-Husayn asked me: 'What does al-Hasan say about His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and you concealed within yourself what God is going to reveal﴾ [and you feared the people] ﴿and God has more right that you fear Him﴾?'"

I said: "He says that when Zayd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Prophet of God, I want to divorce Zaynab,' it pleased him. He said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.﴾" Ali ibn al-Husayn said: "It is not so. God, Mighty and Majestic, had informed him that she would be among his wives, for Zayd would divorce her. When Zayd came and said, 'I want to divorce Zaynab,' he said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.﴾" He said: "Then why did you say: 'Keep your wife to yourself,' when I had informed you that she would be among your wives?"

This interpretation agrees with the recitation, because God, Mighty and Majestic, decreed and made known the manifestation of what was concealed, and God does not break His promise. Then we do not find that He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear the matter except by the marriage, in His saying: ﴿We married her to you.﴾

If the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had concealed his love for her, or wished to divorce her, it would not have been permissible for God, Exalted, to have him conceal what He had promised to make manifest. This indicates that he (peace be upon him) was only reproached for his saying: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself,﴾ while he knew that she would be his wife, and for concealing what God had told him, out of shyness to say to Zayd: "She who is under you will be my wife." And God knows best.

Aishah said: "I am the one whose innocence was revealed in His Book when Ibn al-Mu'attal placed me on the riding-beast." Zaynab said: "What did you say when you mounted it?" That is because Zaynab stayed with Zayd for a time. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went to Zayd one day for a need, and he saw her standing in a shift and head-covering. She pleased him, and it was as if she had fallen into his heart. He said: "Glory be to the One who turns hearts!" and he left.

When Zayd came, she told him of that, and Zayd perceived it. She became displeasing to him at that moment, so the dislike of her was cast into Zayd's heart, and he wanted to separate from her. He came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "I want to separate from my companion."

He said: "What is the matter with you? Has something about her made you suspicious?" He said: "No, by God, O Messenger of God, I have seen nothing from her but good, but she magnifies herself over me by her nobility and hurts me with her tongue." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.﴾ Then Zayd divorced her after that. When her waiting period ended, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Zayd: "I do not find anyone more trustworthy in my own soul than you. Go to Zaynab and propose to her on my behalf."

Zayd said: "So I went, and she was kneading her dough. When I saw her, she became great in my chest, until I could not look at her when I knew that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and said: 'O Zaynab, rejoice, for the Messenger of God is proposing to you.' She rejoiced at that and said: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord.' Then she went to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿We married her to you.﴾ So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) married her and consummated the marriage with her. He did not hold a wedding feast for any of his wives as he held one for her: he slaughtered a sheep and fed the people bread and meat until the day was extended."

That is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom God bestowed favor [with Islam] and you bestowed favor [with manumission]﴾, and he is Zayd ibn Harithah. ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ means Zaynab bint Jahsh, and she was the daughter of the Prophet's paternal aunt (peace be upon him).

﴿...and fear God regarding her,﴾ ﴿and you concealed within yourself what God is going to reveal,﴾ that if he divorced her, you would marry her.

Ibn Abbas said: "It is her love." Qatadah said: "He wished that he had divorced her." ﴿And you feared the people.﴾ Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: "You were shy of them." It was said: "You feared the blame of people, that they would say: he ordered a man to divorce his wife, then married her after he divorced her." ﴿And God has more right that you fear Him.﴾ Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Aishah said: "No verse was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that was harder on him than this verse."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, from al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi, who said: Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Aqil al-Naysaburi informed me, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: "If the Prophet (ﷺ) had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿and you concealed within yourself what God is going to reveal.﴾"

It has been narrated from Zayn al-Abidin concerning this verse what:

Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Talhah ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub, who both said: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid said, from Ibn Abi Mihran: Muhammad ibn Yahya Abi Umar al-Arni narrated to me, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who said: "We heard it from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who repeated it and said: Ali ibn al-Husayn asked me: 'What does al-Hasan say about His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and you concealed within yourself what God is going to reveal﴾ [and you feared the people] ﴿and God has more right that you fear Him﴾?'"

I said: "He says that when Zayd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Prophet of God, I want to divorce Zaynab,' it pleased him. He said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.﴾" Ali ibn al-Husayn said: "It is not so. God, Mighty and Majestic, had informed him that she would be among his wives, for Zayd would divorce her. When Zayd came and said, 'I want to divorce Zaynab,' he said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.﴾" He said: "Then why did you say: 'Keep your wife to yourself,' when I had informed you that she would be among your wives?"

This interpretation agrees with the recitation, because God, Mighty and Majestic, decreed and made known the manifestation of what was concealed, and God does not break His promise. Then we do not find that He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear the matter except by the marriage, in His saying: ﴿We married her to you.﴾

If the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had concealed his love for her, or wished to divorce her, it would not have been permissible for God, Exalted, to have him conceal what He had promised to make manifest. This indicates that he (peace be upon him) was only reproached for his saying: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself,﴾ while he knew that she would be his wife, and for concealing what God had told him, out of shyness to say to Zayd: "She who is under you will be my wife." And God knows best.

This is a good, accepted, strong view, though the other view does not impugn the state of the Prophet (ﷺ), because a servant is not blamed for what occurs in his heart of such things as long as he does not intend sin.

His statement: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her...﴾, that is, his need of marrying her. ﴿...We married her to you.﴾ Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him), saying: "I am the most honored of you in guardianship, and the most honored of you in ambassador: your guardians were your relatives, but God, Mighty and Majestic, married me."

Abu Bakr al-Juzqi informed us, who said: Abu al-Abbas al-Daghuli informed us, who said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah ibn Qahdhadh informed me together, from Ja'far [ibn Muhammad] ibn Awn, from al-Mu'alla ibn Irfan, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who said: Zaynab and Aishah boasted, and Zaynab said: "I am the one whose marriage was sent down from heaven." Aishah said: "I am the one whose innocence was revealed in His Book when Ibn al-Mu'attal placed me on the riding-beast." Zaynab said: "What did you say when you mounted it?" She said: "I said: ﴿God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.﴾" Zaynab said: "It is the word of the believers."

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Zaynab used to say to the Prophet (peace be upon him): "I take pride in you through three things, and no other of your wives can take pride in them: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; God married me to you in heaven; and the ambassador was Jibril."

[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/500, the verse referenced; Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/19.]

His statement: ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons, when those sons have no longer any need of them,﴾ those who were adopted, ﴿when they have no longer any need of them,﴾ by marriage, and divorced them, or died and left them. Al-Hasan said: The Arabs thought that the prohibition on an adopted son was interlinked like the bond of kinship, so God, Exalted, distinguished between the adopted son and the blood relative, and showed them that the wives of adopted sons are not forbidden to them. For this reason He said: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 23]. Then He bound it with ﴿And the command of God is ever accomplished,﴾ certain without doubt, and He had decreed for Zaynab that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) would marry her.

It is in the accusative by removing the preposition. It was said: it is an action, the way of God. It was said: it is an exhortation, meaning: seek the way of God among the earlier prophets, that is, He does not hold them to account for what He made lawful for them.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It refers to Dawud (peace be upon him), when God brought together him and the woman he desired; likewise He brought together Muhammad and Zaynab when he desired her. It was also said: the reference by "the way" is to marriage, and that it is from the way of the prophets. It was said: it refers to the multiplicity of wives, like the story of Dawud and Sulayman (peace be upon him).

﴿And the command of God is a decree determined,﴾ a past, certain matter. Ibn Abbas said: "It was part of His decree that the woman whom Dawud was tested with would bear a son like Sulayman, and would perish after him."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verses 34–38:

Its statement: ﴿Indeed, God is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾

Its statement: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ (the verse). The reason for this is that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of God, God has mentioned men in the Qur'an and has not mentioned women with good. There is no good among us by which we are mentioned. We fear that our obedience will not be accepted from us." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah and Unaysah bint Ka'b al-Ansariyyah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Why does our Lord mention men in the Qur'an and not mention women in anything of His Book? We fear that there is no good in them, and God has no need of them." So this verse was revealed.

Uthman ibn al-Hakam narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah, who said: I heard Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him), say: "I said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'O Messenger of God, why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are mentioned?'"

She said: "Then one day at noon I was startled by nothing but a inkwell on the pulpit while I was combing my hair. I braided my hair, then went out to one of the rooms of my house and placed my ear near the palm-branch (the wall of the room). Then he was saying on the pulpit: 'O people, indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ to His saying: ﴿...and a great reward.﴾'"

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It reached me that Asma bint Umays returned from Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. She entered upon the wives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Has anything of the Qur'an been revealed about us?" They said: "No." So she came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, indeed the women are in loss and ruin." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And why is that?" She said: "Because they are not mentioned with good as men are mentioned." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shabbah, from al-Furati [that is Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati, author of the Tafsir (Qur'anic commentary), known as al-Bustani], from Ibrahim ibn Sa'id, from Ubaydullah, from Shayban, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn al-Aqram, from al-Aghar Abi Muslim, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wakes up at night and wakes his wife, and they both pray two rak'ahs together, they will both be written among ﴿the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him.﴾"

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan, from Jaghuyah ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Hanzalah al-Tamimi, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Israfil came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Say, O Muhammad: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except with God, as many as what He knows, as much as the weight of what He knows, and as much as the fill of what He knows." Whoever says it, six qualities will be written for him: he will be written among ﴿the men who remember God much﴾, he will be better than one who remembers Him night and day, he will have a planting in Paradise, his sins will fall away from him as the dry leaves of a tree fall away, God will look upon him, and whoever God looks upon, He will not punish.

Mujahid said: A servant does not become of ﴿those who remember God much﴾ until he remembers God standing, sitting, and lying on his side.

Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: Whoever entrusts his affair to God is included in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾. Whoever affirms that God is his Lord and that Muhammad is His Messenger, and his heart does not contradict his tongue, is included in His saying: ﴿...the believing men and believing women...﴾. Whoever obeys God in the obligatory acts and the Messenger in the Sunnah is included in His saying: ﴿...the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women...﴾. Whoever guards his speech from falsehood is included in His saying: ﴿...the truthful men and truthful women...﴾. Whoever prays and does not know who is on his right and left is included in His saying: ﴿...the humble men and humble women...﴾. Whoever is patient in obedience, patient against sin, and patient in calamity is included in His saying: ﴿...the patient men and patient women...﴾. Whoever gives charity of a dirham every week is included in His saying: ﴿...the charitable men and charitable women...﴾. Whoever fasts the white days of each month (the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of the lunar month) is included in His saying: ﴿...the fasting men and fasting women...﴾. Whoever guards his private parts from what is not lawful is included in His saying: ﴿...the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them...﴾. Whoever prays the five prayers with their due rights is included in His saying: ﴿...the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him. God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

His statement, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (the verse).

It was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh ibn Ri'ab ibn al-Nu'man ibn Habarah ibn Murrah ibn Ghanm ibn Dawdan al-Asadiyyah, and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh. Zaynab's mother was Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) proposed to her on behalf of his freedman Zayd ibn Harithah. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had bought Zayd in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) from Ukaz; he had been among the captives of the Jahiliyyah. He freed him and adopted him. So Zayd was an Arab in the Jahiliyyah and a freedman in Islam.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) proposed to Zaynab, she was pleased, [thinking] that he was proposing for himself. When she learned that he was proposing on behalf of Zayd, she refused and objected and said: "I am the most complete of the women of Quraysh and the daughter of your aunt. I would not do that, O Messenger of God, and I do not want it for myself." Her brother Abdullah said the same. Zaynab was fair and beautiful, but there was sharpness in her. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair...﴾ meaning Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his sister Zaynab. ﴿...that they should have any choice in their affair.﴾

The people of Kufa and Ayyub read "yakun" with the ya' (masculine), and Abu Ubayd chose this reading, saying: because of the separation between the feminine marker and the verb. Likewise Hisham narrated from the people of Syria. The rest read it with the ta' (feminine).

﴿...the choice...﴾ means the selection. The reading of the common people is "al-khiyarah" with a kasrah on the kha' and a fathah on the ya'. When this verse was revealed, she said: "I am pleased, O Messenger of God," and she placed her affair in the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Her brother did the same. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) married her to Zayd, and he consummated the marriage with her. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 39–55 (part 1 of 2):

The phrase "Allah's words: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾": its position (maḥall) is in the genitive (khafḍ) as a qualifier (naʿt) of ﴿those who passed away before﴾...

﴿And they fear Him and fear none but Allah.﴾ They do not fear the talk of people or their blame concerning what Allah has made lawful for them and enjoined upon them. ﴿And Allah suffices as a Reckoner﴾: a Guardian over the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner for them.

Then it was revealed concerning the people's saying that Muhammad had married the wife of his son: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any man among you﴾, meaning of those who did not beget him, so that his marriage to the wife of his (adopted) son would be forbidden to him after the latter had divorced her; this refers to Zayd. He was (only) the father of al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Mutahhir and Ibrahim.

﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾, i.e., the last of them, the one with whom Allah sealed prophethood, so there is no prophet after him. Had Muhammad had a son, he would have been a prophet.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, from Makki ibn Abdan, from Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-ʿAqib (the Last) after whom there is no prophet." [Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/254; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i: 6/489, with variation.]

The readers differed concerning ﴿Seal of the Prophets﴾. Al-Hasan and ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the ta' (khātam), as a noun, meaning "the last of the prophets", like His words ﴿its seal is musk﴾, i.e., its end. The others read it with a kasra on the ta' (khātim), as an agent noun, meaning that he is the one who seals the prophets with prophethood.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah did not enjoin any obligation upon His servants without setting for it a known limit, then He excused its performers in circumstances of excuse, except for remembrance, for He did not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He did not excuse anyone from abandoning it except one overcome in his reason. He commanded them to remember Him in all conditions, saying: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 103], and He said: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾, by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in private and in public, and in every condition. Mujahid said: The much remembrance is that you do not forget Him ever.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shabbih, from al-Furati [the author of the tafsir was Abu ʿAmr], from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman, from his father, from Abu Lahiʿa, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Increase your remembrance of Allah until they say, 'He is mad.'"

﴿And glorify Him, and pray to Him in the morning (bukrah) and the afternoon (aṣīlan)﴾: on the authority of Qatadah, bukrah means the dawn prayer and aṣīlan means the afternoon prayer.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means the afternoon prayer and the two night prayers (al-ʿishayn). Mujahid said: it means say: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah." So he expressed the glorification (tasbih) as a representative of its companions; these are words that the pure, the one in major ritual impurity (junub), and the one in minor impurity (muhdith) may all say.

His words: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you﴾ — with mercy. Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel said to Musa: "Does our Lord pray?" This statement weighed heavily upon Musa, so Allah revealed to him that he should say to them: "Indeed I pray, and My prayer is My mercy, and My mercy has encompassed everything."

It was said: "yuṣallī" means He spreads the good remembrance of you among His servants. Al-Akhfash said: He blesses you. ﴿And His angels﴾ by asking forgiveness and supplicating, ﴿that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light﴾. ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾

Anas ibn Malik said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "Allah has not singled you out with any honor except that He has made us share in it," so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., the greeting of the believers, ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, i.e., see Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿will be "Peace"﴾, i.e., He will greet them with peace and keep them safe from all calamities and afflictions.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Marwan, from Abi, from Ibrahim ibn ʿIsa, from ʿAli ibn ʿAli: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali told me concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: The angels will greet them on the Day of Resurrection and give them good tidings when they come out of their graves. It was also said: it is at the time of death, and the pronoun refers to the Angel of Death, as an implicit reference to something not mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Zayyat, from Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Ghalib, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wafid Abu Raja', from Muhammad ibn Malik, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: "On the day they meet the Angel of Death. He does not take the soul of a believer except that he greets him with peace."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ibn Habish the reciter, Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qattan told me at al-Raqqa, from ʿUmar ibn Mudrik the storyteller, who said: Abu al-Akhraş Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Baghawi informed me, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Abu Hashim, from Abu al-Akhwas, from Ibn Masʿud who said: When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings of peace."

﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, which is Paradise.
