Mujahid said: it means he may set aside whom he wills of them without divorce, and return to himself whom he wills of them after setting her aside, without renewing the dowry and contract.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: you may divorce whom you will of them and keep whom you will.

al-Hasan said: you may leave the marriage of whom you wish and marry whom you wish from the women of your community.

He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) proposed to a woman, it was not lawful for any man to propose to her until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) either married her or left her.

It was also said: "And you may accept whom you will of the believing women who give themselves to you, and take her to yourself, and leave whom you will so that you do not accept her."

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah related from his father from ʿAʾishah that she used to reproach the women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and she said: "Is a woman not ashamed to give herself or offer herself to a man without a dowry?" Then this verse was revealed. ʿAʾishah said: "I said to the Messenger of Allah: Indeed your Lord hastens to fulfill your desire."

﴿And whoever you seek﴾, i.e., you desire and intend to reach, ﴿of those you had set aside﴾, so you reach her and have intercourse with her after setting her aside, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾. Allah the Exalted thereby permitted him to forgo dividing among them, so that he may postpone whichever of them he wills during her turn, and not approach her, and approach whichever of them he wills outside her turn; he may return to his bed whomever he had set aside, and there is no fault upon him in what he does, as a privilege for him over other men and as an ease for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means: whoever of your wives with you has passed from you, and you have let her go, then We have made lawful for you [others], so it is not proper for you to increase upon the number of your wives who are with you.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾: more pleasing to their souls and less grievous to them when they know that this is from Allah and by His command, and that the concession came from Him. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ concerning the matter of women and inclination toward some of them. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this﴾. The people of Basra read it with a ta' (taḥillu), and others with a ya' (yaḥillu). ﴿Women after this﴾, i.e., after these nine women whom you gave the choice, and they chose you over what they chose of Allah and His Messenger and the Hereafter; He restricted it to them. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah. ʿIkrimah and al-Dahhak said: It is not lawful for you of women except those whom We have made lawful for you, and this is His words: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 50]. Then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾, meaning those We made lawful for you as described earlier.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) had died, would it have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "What would prevent him from that, and what would make it unlawful for him?" I said: "His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾." He said: "Allah only made lawful for him a certain kind of women." Then He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾, then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this.﴾

Abu Salih said: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman or an Arab woman, and afterwards he could marry, if he wished, three hundred women from his own people, from the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and maternal uncles and aunts. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: Its meaning is ﴿Women are not lawful for you﴾ other than Muslim women. As for Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you, and they should not be among the Mothers of the Believers.

Abu Razin said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, meaning slave-girls for marriage. ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾. Mujahid and Abu Razin said: meaning, nor may you exchange Muslim women for others from among the Jews, Christians and polytheists, ﴿even though their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning captives and unbelieving slave-girls.

Al-Dahhak said: meaning, nor may you exchange your wives who are in your possession for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others. Thus it was forbidden for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divorce the women who were with him, since he had made them Mothers of the Believers, and forbidden them to anyone else once they had chosen him. As for marrying other women, it was not prohibited to him; rather it was made lawful for him, if he wished. The following supports this:

What 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Abu 'Asim informed me, from Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him.

Ibn Zayd said: In the Jahiliyyah, the Arabs used to exchange their wives: this man gives his wife to that one, and takes that one's wife. So Allah said: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning, exchange your wives for the wives of others, by giving your wife and taking his wife. Except what your right hand possesses: there is no harm in exchanging your slave-girl for whatever you wish, but as for free women, no.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Ubaydi, from Ahmad ibn Najdah, from al-Hammani, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The exchange in the Jahiliyyah was that a man would say to another man: Exchange your wife with me and I will exchange mine with you; you vacate your wife for me and I will vacate mine for you. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾ ... He said: 'Uyayna ibn Husayn entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while 'A'isha was with him, and he entered without permission. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Uyayna, where is the seeking of permission?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, since I came of age I have not sought permission from any man of Mudar. Then he said: Who is this red-cheeked one beside you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers." 'Uyayna said: Shall I not vacate for you the best of creation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden that." When he left, 'A'isha said: Who was this, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "This is a foolish man who is obeyed, and he is, as you see, the chief of his people."

Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿even though their beauty pleases you﴾, said: meaning Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyyah, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. In this is evidence for the permissibility of looking at the woman one wishes to marry, and reports have come permitting this.

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, that al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah wished to marry a woman, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you two." [17] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/134.]]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Harb, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Khaythamah, from his paternal uncle Sulayman ibn Abi Khaythamah, who said: I saw Muhammad ibn Maslamah pursuing Nabitah bint al-Dahhak on one of the paths of Madinah. I said: Are you doing this? He said: Yes, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah places in a man's heart the proposal of a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her." [18]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man wished to marry a woman from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Look at her, for in the eyes of the women of the Ansar there is something." [19] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/77; Musnad Ahmad: 2/1286.]]

Al-Humaydi said: meaning, smallness (of the eyes). ﴿And Allah is ever over all things a Watcher﴾, an Guardian.

His exalted saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ Most of the exegetes said: this verse was revealed concerning the wedding feast of Zaynab.

Anas ibn Malik said: I am the most knowledgeable of people concerning the verse of hijab. Ubayy ibn Ka'b asked me about it when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh, and he held a feast for her with dates, sawiq, and a sheep was slaughtered. My mother Umm Sulaym sent to him a dish of hays in a stone bowl. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded me to invite his companions to the meal. I invited them, and the people kept coming, eating and leaving, then another group would come, eat and leave.

I said: O Prophet of Allah, I have invited people until I can find no one left to invite. He said: "Lift up your food." They lifted it, and the people left, but three men remained, talking in the house, and they prolonged their stay. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and I stood with him so that they would leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked off toward the room of 'A'isha and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house." They said: "And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah. How did you find your family?" Then he returned and came to the chambers of his wives and greeted them, and they prayed for him. He returned to Zaynab's house, and found the three still sitting and talking in the house. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely shy, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned back. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) turn away from his house, they left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his house and placed a curtain between me and him, and this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: This occurred in the house of Umm Salamah. A group entered her house and ate, then prolonged their conversation, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bothered by them, but he was too shy to tell them to leave, and ﴿Allah does not feel shy before the truth﴾. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission, unless you are invited to a meal, not waiting for its ripeness﴾, meaning its readiness and time of cooking.

Regarding ﴿ināhu﴾ there are two forms: anā and innā, with the alif kasrah and fathah, like ʾallā and ʾillā, ma'a and ma'a. Its plural is inā', like ālā' and am'ā'. The verb from it is anā yaʾnā, inā with a short alif, and ānā with a long alif. Al-Huṭay'ah said:

"And I reached the evening meal toward Suhayl, or Sha'ra, and the time (anā) lengthened for me."

And al-Shaybani said:

"Death was pregnant with him on a day of its time, and for every pregnant woman there is a term."

There is another form: ān yaʾīn, aynā.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning some believers who would watch for the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) meal, entering upon him before the food was ready, then they would eat and not leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bothered by them, so this verse was revealed.

﴿Not waiting for it﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier. ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse﴾, meaning, when you have eaten the food, scatter and leave his house. ﴿And do not remain, seeking familiar conversation﴾, meaning seeking the pleasure of conversation. Its position is in the genitive, coordinated with his saying ﴿not waiting﴾, so it reads: nor (remaining) seeking familiar conversation. ﴿Indeed that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning, He does not abandon disciplining you and bringing you to the truth, and that does not prevent Him from doing so.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib informed us verbally, saying: Abu Musa 'Imran ibn Musa ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq informed me, saying: Abu 'Amr 'Uthman ibn Kharzad [[So in the original; perhaps it is: al-Wazzan.]] al-Antaki informed me, from 'Amr ibn Marzuq, from Juwayriyyah ibn Asma', who said: This verse was recited before Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, and he said: This is [an etiquette] which Allah taught to the burdensome guests.

I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad say: I heard al-Ghallabi say: I heard Ibn 'A'ishah say: It is enough for burdensome guests that Allah, Exalted, did not tolerate them, and said: ﴿But when you have eaten, disperse﴾.

His saying: ﴿And when you ask them for an article, ask them from behind a curtain﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Zuhri... [the chain as given] from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he would pass by his wives. He came to a woman he had married, and he spoke with her; there were people with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out and was delayed, then he fulfilled his need and returned, and they had left. He entered and drew a curtain between himself and me. He said: I told Abu Talhah, and he said: If it is as you say, something will surely be revealed about this. So the verse of hijab was revealed.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed me that al-Husayn ibn Ya'qub related to him, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: O Messenger of Allah, the pious and the wicked enter upon you; if only you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab. Then the verse of hijab was revealed.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sharqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Salih ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr: that 'A'isha said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Veil your wives; but he did not do so. The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go out at night to Layl, before al-Manasi', which is an ugly open ground. Sawdah bint Zam'ah went out, and she was a tall woman. 'Umar saw her while he was in a gathering and said: I recognized you, O Sawdah, out of eagerness that the hijab be revealed. So Allah revealed the hijab.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by licence, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn 'Affan, who said: Abu Usamah informed me, from Mukhalad ibn Sa'id, from 'Amir, who said: 'Umar passed by the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was with the women in the mosque, and he said to them: Veil yourselves, for you have a superiority over the women, just as your husband has superiority over men. They had not waited long before Allah revealed the verse of hijab.

'Ata' ibn Abi al-Sa'ib related from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ordered the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to observe hijab. Zaynab said: O son of al-Khattab, you are jealous over us, while revelation descends in our houses. So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for an article, ask them from behind a curtain; that is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾.

It was said concerning the occasion of the revelation of hijab:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad informed us that al-Mu'afa related to him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, from Hisham, from Layth, from Mujahid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of one of them touched the hand of 'A'isha, who was with them. The Prophet disliked that, so the verse of hijab was revealed.

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muzakki informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Masarkhasi informed me, from Shaybban ibn Farrukh al-Ablli, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I used to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without permission. One day I came to enter, and he said: Stay where you are, my son; there has come after you the rule that no one enters upon us except with permission.

His saying: ﴿And it is not for you﴾, meaning, it is not proper nor fitting for you, ﴿to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed that, in the sight of Allah, is a great matter.﴾ It was revealed concerning a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dies, I will surely marry 'A'isha bint Abi Bakr.

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Dawud, from 'Amir: that the Prophet (ﷺ) died while he owned Qutaylah bint al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, and had not consummated with her. Then 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her after that, and this was very hard on Abu Bakr. 'Umar said to him: O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, she is not among his wives; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not give her the choice, nor did he veil her, and he had cleared her of himself through the apostasy she committed with her people. He said: Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed.

Ma'mar related from al-Zuhri that al-'Aliyah bint Tayyib, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) divorced, married a man and bore him children, and that was before it was forbidden to people to marry the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ His exalted saying: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers...﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, sons and relatives said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): And are we also to speak to them from behind a curtain? So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers...﴾

﴿...nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess﴾, regarding abandoning hijab before these, and that these may see them.

Mujahid said: ﴿There is no blame upon them﴾ in removing their outer garments in front of them.

﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is ever over all things a Witness.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 39–55 (part 1 of 2):

The phrase "Allah's words: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾": its position (maḥall) is in the genitive (khafḍ) as a qualifier (naʿt) of ﴿those who passed away before﴾...

﴿And they fear Him and fear none but Allah.﴾ They do not fear the talk of people or their blame concerning what Allah has made lawful for them and enjoined upon them. ﴿And Allah suffices as a Reckoner﴾: a Guardian over the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner for them.

Then it was revealed concerning the people's saying that Muhammad had married the wife of his son: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any man among you﴾, meaning of those who did not beget him, so that his marriage to the wife of his (adopted) son would be forbidden to him after the latter had divorced her; this refers to Zayd. He was (only) the father of al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Mutahhir and Ibrahim.

﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾, i.e., the last of them, the one with whom Allah sealed prophethood, so there is no prophet after him. Had Muhammad had a son, he would have been a prophet.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, from Makki ibn Abdan, from Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-ʿAqib (the Last) after whom there is no prophet." [Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/254; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i: 6/489, with variation.]

The readers differed concerning ﴿Seal of the Prophets﴾. Al-Hasan and ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the ta' (khātam), as a noun, meaning "the last of the prophets", like His words ﴿its seal is musk﴾, i.e., its end. The others read it with a kasra on the ta' (khātim), as an agent noun, meaning that he is the one who seals the prophets with prophethood.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah did not enjoin any obligation upon His servants without setting for it a known limit, then He excused its performers in circumstances of excuse, except for remembrance, for He did not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He did not excuse anyone from abandoning it except one overcome in his reason. He commanded them to remember Him in all conditions, saying: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 103], and He said: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾, by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in private and in public, and in every condition. Mujahid said: The much remembrance is that you do not forget Him ever.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shabbih, from al-Furati [the author of the tafsir was Abu ʿAmr], from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman, from his father, from Abu Lahiʿa, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Increase your remembrance of Allah until they say, 'He is mad.'"

﴿And glorify Him, and pray to Him in the morning (bukrah) and the afternoon (aṣīlan)﴾: on the authority of Qatadah, bukrah means the dawn prayer and aṣīlan means the afternoon prayer.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means the afternoon prayer and the two night prayers (al-ʿishayn). Mujahid said: it means say: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah." So he expressed the glorification (tasbih) as a representative of its companions; these are words that the pure, the one in major ritual impurity (junub), and the one in minor impurity (muhdith) may all say.

His words: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you﴾ — with mercy. Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel said to Musa: "Does our Lord pray?" This statement weighed heavily upon Musa, so Allah revealed to him that he should say to them: "Indeed I pray, and My prayer is My mercy, and My mercy has encompassed everything."

It was said: "yuṣallī" means He spreads the good remembrance of you among His servants. Al-Akhfash said: He blesses you. ﴿And His angels﴾ by asking forgiveness and supplicating, ﴿that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light﴾. ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾

Anas ibn Malik said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "Allah has not singled you out with any honor except that He has made us share in it," so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., the greeting of the believers, ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, i.e., see Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿will be "Peace"﴾, i.e., He will greet them with peace and keep them safe from all calamities and afflictions.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Marwan, from Abi, from Ibrahim ibn ʿIsa, from ʿAli ibn ʿAli: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali told me concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: The angels will greet them on the Day of Resurrection and give them good tidings when they come out of their graves. It was also said: it is at the time of death, and the pronoun refers to the Angel of Death, as an implicit reference to something not mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Zayyat, from Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Ghalib, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wafid Abu Raja', from Muhammad ibn Malik, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: "On the day they meet the Angel of Death. He does not take the soul of a believer except that he greets him with peace."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ibn Habish the reciter, Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qattan told me at al-Raqqa, from ʿUmar ibn Mudrik the storyteller, who said: Abu al-Akhraş Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Baghawi informed me, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Abu Hashim, from Abu al-Akhwas, from Ibn Masʿud who said: When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings of peace."

﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, which is Paradise.

His words: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner, and as one calling to Allah by His permission, and as a illuminating lamp﴾, by which the people of religion are guided.

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: When the verses ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 1] were revealed, the Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah, this is a favor; what about us?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm﴾: be patient with them and do not retaliate.

It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

His words: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them (tamassūhunna), i.e., had intercourse with them, then you have no waiting period (ʿidda) for them to count (taʿtaddūnahā), i.e., to reckon against them by menstrual cycles and months. So provide for them (fa-matti'ūhunna), i.e., give them what they may enjoy.* Ibn ʿAbbas said: This applies when no dowry (ṣadāq) was specified for her; but if a dowry was set for her, then she is entitled to half of it. Qatadah said: this verse is abrogated by His words: ﴿Then half of what you have specified﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 237]. It was also said: it is a command of recommendation (nadb), so the provision is recommended while half the dowry is obligatory. ﴿And release them (sarriḥūhunna) and let them go (khallū sabīlahunna) with a fair release (sarāḥan jamīlan)﴾, according to what is customary. The verse contains evidence that divorce before marriage does not take effect, whether specified or general, contrary to the people of Kufa.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i, from ʿAbd al-Salam ibn ʿAsim al-Razi, who said: Abu Zuhayr informed me, from al-Ahlaj, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit who said: I was sitting with ʿAli ibn al-Husayn when a man came to him and said: "I said: On the day I marry so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, she is divorced." He said: "Go and marry her, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic began with marriage before divorce, and He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾, and He did not say 'when you divorce them and then marry them'," and he did not consider it anything.

The evidence for this is what:

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, from ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mundhir al-Naysaburi informed me in Mecca, from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from ʿAta', from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no divorce before marriage." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/660; Mustadrak al-Hakim: 2/205.]

His words: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments (ujūrahunna)﴾, i.e., their dowries (mahrahunna), ﴿and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾, such as Safiyyah, Juwayriyah and Mariyah; ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, from the women of ʿAbd al-Muttalib; ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, from the women of Banu Zuhrah, ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. Whoever among them did not emigrate, it is not lawful for him to marry her. Ibn Masʿud read: "wa-al-lātī hājarna" with a waw.

ʿAqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir who said: Abu Kurayb informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Musa, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Umm Hani' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him, and he accepted my excuse. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ up to His words ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. She said: So he was not lawful for me, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed ones (al-ṭulaqāʾ).

﴿And a believing woman﴾, i.e., and We have made lawful for you a believing woman ﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ without a dowry. The common readers read ﴿in﴾ with a kasra on the alif, as a conditional and future; al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the alif, as past and obligatory. ﴿If the Prophet wishes to marry her, that is for him alone, to the exclusion of the believers﴾: it is not permissible for a woman to give herself to a man without witnesses, a guardian, or a dowry, except for the Prophet (peace be upon him); this is among his particular privileges in marriage, like the option (of choice) and the number (of wives). And what was related: that he freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.

If he had married her with the wording of a gift, the marriage would not be concluded. This is the view of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Zuhri, Mujahid, ʿAta', Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Rabiʿah, Abu ʿUbayd and most jurists.

Al-Nakhaʿi and the people of Kufa said: If she gave herself to him and he accepted her with witnesses and a dowry, the marriage is concluded and the dowry becomes binding; so they permitted marriage with the wording of a gift. They said: The Prophet's (peace be upon him) privilege lay in dispensing with the dowry. The evidence for al-Shafiʿi's position is that Allah the Exalted named marriage with two names, tazwij and nikah, so it is not concluded by other than these.

The scholars differed concerning the woman who gave herself to the Messenger of Allah, and whether there was a wife of the Prophet (ﷺ) like that. Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: there was no woman with the Prophet (ﷺ) who gave herself to him, and there was no wife with him (peace be upon him) except through a marriage contract or ownership by right hand; Allah said ﴿if she gives herself﴾ only as a conditional and consequent clause.

Others said: rather, there was with him one who had been given. They differed about her. Qatadah said: she was Maymunah bint al-Harith. Al-Shaʿbi said: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm al-Masakin, a woman of the Ansar.

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Umm Sharik bint Jabir of Banu Asad.

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas of Banu Sulaym.

﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them﴾, i.e., what We have obligated upon the believers ﴿concerning their wives﴾. Mujahid said: i.e., four, which they may not exceed. Qatadah said: it is that there is no marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses. ﴿And what their right hands possess﴾, i.e., the female slaves and bondwomen, ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for you﴾ in marrying them. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

His words: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾, i.e., delay; ﴿and you may take to you whom you will﴾, i.e., include. The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse.

Abu Razin and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed when some of the Mothers of the Believers became jealous of the Prophet (ﷺ) and some of them requested an increase in maintenance; so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) abstained from them for a month, until the verse of choice was revealed, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and to release whoever chose this world, and to keep whoever chose Allah and His Messenger, on the condition that they remain Mothers of the Believers and never marry again; and on the condition that he may take to himself whom he wills and postpone whom he wills, and they would be content with that, whether he divided among them or did not divide, or divided for some and not for others, or preferred some over others in maintenance, division and companionship, or treated them equally; and the matter in all of this is up to him, he does as he wills. This was among his particular privileges (peace be upon him).

They agreed to all of that and chose it on this condition. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), despite what Allah had granted him in this regard, treated them equally in division, except for one woman whom he wished to divorce; she agreed to give up her turn, and he made her day for ʿAʾishah, and she was Sawdah bint Zamʿah.

Mansur related from Abu Razin who said: When the verse of choice was revealed, they feared he would divorce them, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah, grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state," so this verse was revealed. Among those whom he postponed were Sawdah, Juwayriyah, Safiyyah, Maymunah and Umm Habibah; he divided among them as he wished and when he wished. Among those he took to himself were ʿAʾishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab, may Allah have mercy on them; he divided among them equally, not preferring some over others. So he postponed five and took four.

Mujahid said: it means he may set aside whom he wills of them without divorce, and return to himself whom he wills of them after setting her aside, without renewing the dowry and contract.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: you may divorce whom you will of them and keep whom you will.

al-Hasan said: you may leave the marriage of whom you wish and marry whom you wish from the women of your community.

He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) proposed to a woman, it was not lawful for any man to propose to her until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) either married her or left her.

It was also said: "And you may accept whom you will of the believing women who give themselves to you, and take her to yourself, and leave whom you will so that you do not accept her."

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah related from his father from ʿAʾishah that she used to reproach the women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and she said: "Is a woman not ashamed to give herself or offer herself to a man without a dowry?" Then this verse was revealed. ʿAʾishah said: "I said to the Messenger of Allah: Indeed your Lord hastens to fulfill your desire."

﴿And whoever you seek﴾, i.e., you desire and intend to reach, ﴿of those you had set aside﴾, so you reach her and have intercourse with her after setting her aside, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾. Allah the Exalted thereby permitted him to forgo dividing among them, so that he may postpone whichever of them he wills during her turn, and not approach her, and approach whichever of them he wills outside her turn; he may return to his bed whomever he had set aside, and there is no fault upon him in what he does, as a privilege for him over other men and as an ease for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means: whoever of your wives with you has passed from you, and you have let her go, then We have made lawful for you [others], so it is not proper for you to increase upon the number of your wives who are with you.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾: more pleasing to their souls and less grievous to them when they know that this is from Allah and by His command, and that the concession came from Him. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ concerning the matter of women and inclination toward some of them. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this﴾. The people of Basra read it with a ta' (taḥillu), and others with a ya' (yaḥillu). ﴿Women after this﴾, i.e., after these nine women whom you gave the choice, and they chose you over what they chose of Allah and His Messenger and the Hereafter; He restricted it to them. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah. ʿIkrimah and al-Dahhak said: It is not lawful for you of women except those whom We have made lawful for you, and this is His words: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 50]. Then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾, meaning those We made lawful for you as described earlier.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) had died, would it have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "What would prevent him from that, and what would make it unlawful for him?" I said: "His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾." He said: "Allah only made lawful for him a certain kind of women." Then He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾, then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this.﴾

Abu Salih said: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman or an Arab woman, and afterwards he could marry, if he wished, three hundred women from his own people, from the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and maternal uncles and aunts. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: Its meaning is ﴿Women are not lawful for you﴾ other than Muslim women. As for Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you, and they should not be among the Mothers of the Believers.

Abu Razin said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, meaning slave-girls for marriage. ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾. Mujahid and Abu Razin said: meaning, nor may you exchange Muslim women for others from among the Jews, Christians and polytheists, ﴿even though their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning captives and unbelieving slave-girls.

Al-Dahhak said: meaning, nor may you exchange your wives who are in your possession for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others. Thus it was forbidden for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divorce the women who were with him, since he had made them Mothers of the Believers, and forbidden them to anyone else once they had chosen him. As for marrying other women, it was not prohibited to him; rather it was made lawful for him, if he wished. The following supports this:

What 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Abu 'Asim informed me, from Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him.

Ibn Zayd said: In the Jahiliyyah, the Arabs used to exchange their wives: this man gives his wife to that one, and takes that one's wife. So Allah said: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning, exchange your wives for the wives of others, by giving your wife and taking his wife. Except what your right hand possesses: there is no harm in exchanging your slave-girl for whatever you wish, but as for free women, no.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Ubaydi, from Ahmad ibn Najdah, from al-Hammani, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The exchange in the Jahiliyyah was that a man would say to another man: Exchange your wife with me and I will exchange mine with you; you vacate your wife for me and I will vacate mine for you. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾ ... He said: 'Uyayna ibn Husayn entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while 'A'isha was with him, and he entered without permission. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Uyayna, where is the seeking of permission?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, since I came of age I have not sought permission from any man of Mudar. Then he said: Who is this red-cheeked one beside you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers." 'Uyayna said: Shall I not vacate for you the best of creation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden that." When he left, 'A'isha said: Who was this, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "This is a foolish man who is obeyed, and he is, as you see, the chief of his people."

Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿even though their beauty pleases you﴾, said: meaning Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyyah, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. In this is evidence for the permissibility of looking at the woman one wishes to marry, and reports have come permitting this.

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, that al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah wished to marry a woman, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you two." [17] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/134.]]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Harb, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Khaythamah, from his paternal uncle Sulayman ibn Abi Khaythamah, who said: I saw Muhammad ibn Maslamah pursuing Nabitah bint al-Dahhak on one of the paths of Madinah. I said: Are you doing this? He said: Yes, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah places in a man's heart the proposal of a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her." [18]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man wished to marry a woman from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Look at her, for in the eyes of the women of the Ansar there is something." [19] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/77; Musnad Ahmad: 2/1286.]]

Al-Humaydi said: meaning, smallness (of the eyes). ﴿And Allah is ever over all things a Watcher﴾, an Guardian.

His exalted saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ Most of the exegetes said: this verse was revealed concerning the wedding feast of Zaynab.

Anas ibn Malik said: I am the most knowledgeable of people concerning the verse of hijab. Ubayy ibn Ka'b asked me about it when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh, and he held a feast for her with dates, sawiq, and a sheep was slaughtered. My mother Umm Sulaym sent to him a dish of hays in a stone bowl. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded me to invite his companions to the meal. I invited them, and the people kept coming, eating and leaving, then another group would come, eat and leave.

I said: O Prophet of Allah, I have invited people until I can find no one left to invite. He said: "Lift up your food." They lifted it, and the people left, but three men remained, talking in the house, and they prolonged their stay. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and I stood with him so that they would leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked off toward the room of 'A'isha and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house." They said: "And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah. How did you find your family?" Then he returned and came to the chambers of his wives and greeted them, and they prayed for him. He returned to Zaynab's house, and found the three still sitting and talking in the house. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely shy, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned back. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) turn away from his house, they left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his house and placed a curtain between me and him, and this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: This occurred in the house of Umm Salamah. A group entered her house and ate, then prolonged their conversation, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bothered by them, but he was too shy to tell them to leave, and ﴿Allah does not feel shy before the truth﴾. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission, unless you are invited to a meal, not waiting for its ripeness﴾, meaning its readiness and time of cooking.

Regarding ﴿ināhu﴾ there are two forms: anā and innā, with the alif kasrah and fathah, like ʾallā and ʾillā, ma'a and ma'a. Its plural is inā', like ālā' and am'ā'. The verb from it is anā yaʾnā, inā with a short alif, and ānā with a long alif. Al-Huṭay'ah said:

"And I reached the evening meal toward Suhayl, or Sha'ra, and the time (anā) lengthened for me."

And al-Shaybani said:

"Death was pregnant with him on a day of its time, and for every pregnant woman there is a term."

There is another form: ān yaʾīn, aynā.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning some believers who would watch for the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) meal, entering upon him before the food was ready, then they would eat and not leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bothered by them, so this verse was revealed.

﴿Not waiting for it﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier. ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse﴾, meaning, when you have eaten the food, scatter and leave his house. ﴿And do not remain, seeking familiar conversation﴾, meaning seeking the pleasure of conversation. Its position is in the genitive, coordinated with his saying ﴿not waiting﴾, so it reads: nor (remaining) seeking familiar conversation. ﴿Indeed that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning, He does not abandon disciplining you and bringing you to the truth, and that does not prevent Him from doing so.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib informed us verbally, saying: Abu Musa 'Imran ibn Musa ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq informed me, saying: Abu 'Amr 'Uthman ibn Kharzad [[So in the original; perhaps it is: al-Wazzan.]] al-Antaki informed me, from 'Amr ibn Marzuq, from Juwayriyyah ibn Asma', who said: This verse was recited before Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, and he said: This is [an etiquette] which Allah taught to the burdensome guests.

I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad say: I heard al-Ghallabi say: I heard Ibn 'A'ishah say: It is enough for burdensome guests that Allah, Exalted, did not tolerate them, and said: ﴿But when you have eaten, disperse﴾.

His saying: ﴿And when you ask them for an article, ask them from behind a curtain﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Zuhri... [the chain as given] from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he would pass by his wives. He came to a woman he had married, and he spoke with her; there were people with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out and was delayed, then he fulfilled his need and returned, and they had left. He entered and drew a curtain between himself and me. He said: I told Abu Talhah, and he said: If it is as you say, something will surely be revealed about this. So the verse of hijab was revealed.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed me that al-Husayn ibn Ya'qub related to him, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: O Messenger of Allah, the pious and the wicked enter upon you; if only you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab. Then the verse of hijab was revealed.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sharqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Salih ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr: that 'A'isha said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Veil your wives; but he did not do so. The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go out at night to Layl, before al-Manasi', which is an ugly open ground. Sawdah bint Zam'ah went out, and she was a tall woman. 'Umar saw her while he was in a gathering and said: I recognized you, O Sawdah, out of eagerness that the hijab be revealed. So Allah revealed the hijab.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by licence, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn 'Affan, who said: Abu Usamah informed me, from Mukhalad ibn Sa'id, from 'Amir, who said: 'Umar passed by the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was with the women in the mosque, and he said to them: Veil yourselves, for you have a superiority over the women, just as your husband has superiority over men. They had not waited long before Allah revealed the verse of hijab.

'Ata' ibn Abi al-Sa'ib related from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ordered the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to observe hijab. Zaynab said: O son of al-Khattab, you are jealous over us, while revelation descends in our houses. So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for an article, ask them from behind a curtain; that is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾.

It was said concerning the occasion of the revelation of hijab:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad informed us that al-Mu'afa related to him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, from Hisham, from Layth, from Mujahid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of one of them touched the hand of 'A'isha, who was with them. The Prophet disliked that, so the verse of hijab was revealed.

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muzakki informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Masarkhasi informed me, from Shaybban ibn Farrukh al-Ablli, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I used to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without permission. One day I came to enter, and he said: Stay where you are, my son; there has come after you the rule that no one enters upon us except with permission.

His saying: ﴿And it is not for you﴾, meaning, it is not proper nor fitting for you, ﴿to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed that, in the sight of Allah, is a great matter.﴾ It was revealed concerning a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dies, I will surely marry 'A'isha bint Abi Bakr.

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Dawud, from 'Amir: that the Prophet (ﷺ) died while he owned Qutaylah bint al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, and had not consummated with her. Then 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her after that, and this was very hard on Abu Bakr. 'Umar said to him: O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, she is not among his wives; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not give her the choice, nor did he veil her, and he had cleared her of himself through the apostasy she committed with her people. He said: Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed.

Ma'mar related from al-Zuhri that al-'Aliyah bint Tayyib, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) divorced, married a man and bore him children, and that was before it was forbidden to people to marry the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ His exalted saying: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers...﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, sons and relatives said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): And are we also to speak to them from behind a curtain? So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers...﴾

﴿...nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess﴾, regarding abandoning hijab before these, and that these may see them.

Mujahid said: ﴿There is no blame upon them﴾ in removing their outer garments in front of them.

﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is ever over all things a Witness.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 39–55 (part 1 of 2):

The phrase "Allah's words: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾": its position (maḥall) is in the genitive (khafḍ) as a qualifier (naʿt) of ﴿those who passed away before﴾...

﴿And they fear Him and fear none but Allah.﴾ They do not fear the talk of people or their blame concerning what Allah has made lawful for them and enjoined upon them. ﴿And Allah suffices as a Reckoner﴾: a Guardian over the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner for them.

Then it was revealed concerning the people's saying that Muhammad had married the wife of his son: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any man among you﴾, meaning of those who did not beget him, so that his marriage to the wife of his (adopted) son would be forbidden to him after the latter had divorced her; this refers to Zayd. He was (only) the father of al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Mutahhir and Ibrahim.

﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾, i.e., the last of them, the one with whom Allah sealed prophethood, so there is no prophet after him. Had Muhammad had a son, he would have been a prophet.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, from Makki ibn Abdan, from Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-ʿAqib (the Last) after whom there is no prophet." [Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/254; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i: 6/489, with variation.]

The readers differed concerning ﴿Seal of the Prophets﴾. Al-Hasan and ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the ta' (khātam), as a noun, meaning "the last of the prophets", like His words ﴿its seal is musk﴾, i.e., its end. The others read it with a kasra on the ta' (khātim), as an agent noun, meaning that he is the one who seals the prophets with prophethood.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah did not enjoin any obligation upon His servants without setting for it a known limit, then He excused its performers in circumstances of excuse, except for remembrance, for He did not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He did not excuse anyone from abandoning it except one overcome in his reason. He commanded them to remember Him in all conditions, saying: ﴿So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 103], and He said: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾, by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in health and in sickness, in private and in public, and in every condition. Mujahid said: The much remembrance is that you do not forget Him ever.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shabbih, from al-Furati [the author of the tafsir was Abu ʿAmr], from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman, from his father, from Abu Lahiʿa, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Increase your remembrance of Allah until they say, 'He is mad.'"

﴿And glorify Him, and pray to Him in the morning (bukrah) and the afternoon (aṣīlan)﴾: on the authority of Qatadah, bukrah means the dawn prayer and aṣīlan means the afternoon prayer.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means the afternoon prayer and the two night prayers (al-ʿishayn). Mujahid said: it means say: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah." So he expressed the glorification (tasbih) as a representative of its companions; these are words that the pure, the one in major ritual impurity (junub), and the one in minor impurity (muhdith) may all say.

His words: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you﴾ — with mercy. Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel said to Musa: "Does our Lord pray?" This statement weighed heavily upon Musa, so Allah revealed to him that he should say to them: "Indeed I pray, and My prayer is My mercy, and My mercy has encompassed everything."

It was said: "yuṣallī" means He spreads the good remembrance of you among His servants. Al-Akhfash said: He blesses you. ﴿And His angels﴾ by asking forgiveness and supplicating, ﴿that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light﴾. ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾

Anas ibn Malik said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "Allah has not singled you out with any honor except that He has made us share in it," so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

﴿Their greeting﴾, i.e., the greeting of the believers, ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, i.e., see Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿will be "Peace"﴾, i.e., He will greet them with peace and keep them safe from all calamities and afflictions.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Marwan, from Abi, from Ibrahim ibn ʿIsa, from ʿAli ibn ʿAli: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali told me concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: The angels will greet them on the Day of Resurrection and give them good tidings when they come out of their graves. It was also said: it is at the time of death, and the pronoun refers to the Angel of Death, as an implicit reference to something not mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Zayyat, from Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Ghalib, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wafid Abu Raja', from Muhammad ibn Malik, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, concerning His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him is "Peace"﴾. He said: "On the day they meet the Angel of Death. He does not take the soul of a believer except that he greets him with peace."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ibn Habish the reciter, Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qattan told me at al-Raqqa, from ʿUmar ibn Mudrik the storyteller, who said: Abu al-Akhraş Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Baghawi informed me, from Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Abu Hashim, from Abu al-Akhwas, from Ibn Masʿud who said: When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings of peace."

﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, which is Paradise.

His words: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner, and as one calling to Allah by His permission, and as a illuminating lamp﴾, by which the people of religion are guided.

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: When the verses ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 1] were revealed, the Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah, this is a favor; what about us?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm﴾: be patient with them and do not retaliate.

It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

His words: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them (tamassūhunna), i.e., had intercourse with them, then you have no waiting period (ʿidda) for them to count (taʿtaddūnahā), i.e., to reckon against them by menstrual cycles and months. So provide for them (fa-matti'ūhunna), i.e., give them what they may enjoy.* Ibn ʿAbbas said: This applies when no dowry (ṣadāq) was specified for her; but if a dowry was set for her, then she is entitled to half of it. Qatadah said: this verse is abrogated by His words: ﴿Then half of what you have specified﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 237]. It was also said: it is a command of recommendation (nadb), so the provision is recommended while half the dowry is obligatory. ﴿And release them (sarriḥūhunna) and let them go (khallū sabīlahunna) with a fair release (sarāḥan jamīlan)﴾, according to what is customary. The verse contains evidence that divorce before marriage does not take effect, whether specified or general, contrary to the people of Kufa.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i, from ʿAbd al-Salam ibn ʿAsim al-Razi, who said: Abu Zuhayr informed me, from al-Ahlaj, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit who said: I was sitting with ʿAli ibn al-Husayn when a man came to him and said: "I said: On the day I marry so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, she is divorced." He said: "Go and marry her, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic began with marriage before divorce, and He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾, and He did not say 'when you divorce them and then marry them'," and he did not consider it anything.

The evidence for this is what:

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, from ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mundhir al-Naysaburi informed me in Mecca, from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from ʿAta', from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no divorce before marriage." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/660; Mustadrak al-Hakim: 2/205.]

His words: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments (ujūrahunna)﴾, i.e., their dowries (mahrahunna), ﴿and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾, such as Safiyyah, Juwayriyah and Mariyah; ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, from the women of ʿAbd al-Muttalib; ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, from the women of Banu Zuhrah, ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. Whoever among them did not emigrate, it is not lawful for him to marry her. Ibn Masʿud read: "wa-al-lātī hājarna" with a waw.

ʿAqil ibn Muhammad informed me, from al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir who said: Abu Kurayb informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Musa, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Umm Hani' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him, and he accepted my excuse. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ up to His words ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. She said: So he was not lawful for me, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed ones (al-ṭulaqāʾ).

﴿And a believing woman﴾, i.e., and We have made lawful for you a believing woman ﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ without a dowry. The common readers read ﴿in﴾ with a kasra on the alif, as a conditional and future; al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the alif, as past and obligatory. ﴿If the Prophet wishes to marry her, that is for him alone, to the exclusion of the believers﴾: it is not permissible for a woman to give herself to a man without witnesses, a guardian, or a dowry, except for the Prophet (peace be upon him); this is among his particular privileges in marriage, like the option (of choice) and the number (of wives). And what was related: that he freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.

If he had married her with the wording of a gift, the marriage would not be concluded. This is the view of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Zuhri, Mujahid, ʿAta', Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Rabiʿah, Abu ʿUbayd and most jurists.

Al-Nakhaʿi and the people of Kufa said: If she gave herself to him and he accepted her with witnesses and a dowry, the marriage is concluded and the dowry becomes binding; so they permitted marriage with the wording of a gift. They said: The Prophet's (peace be upon him) privilege lay in dispensing with the dowry. The evidence for al-Shafiʿi's position is that Allah the Exalted named marriage with two names, tazwij and nikah, so it is not concluded by other than these.

The scholars differed concerning the woman who gave herself to the Messenger of Allah, and whether there was a wife of the Prophet (ﷺ) like that. Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: there was no woman with the Prophet (ﷺ) who gave herself to him, and there was no wife with him (peace be upon him) except through a marriage contract or ownership by right hand; Allah said ﴿if she gives herself﴾ only as a conditional and consequent clause.

Others said: rather, there was with him one who had been given. They differed about her. Qatadah said: she was Maymunah bint al-Harith. Al-Shaʿbi said: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm al-Masakin, a woman of the Ansar.

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Umm Sharik bint Jabir of Banu Asad.

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas of Banu Sulaym.

﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them﴾, i.e., what We have obligated upon the believers ﴿concerning their wives﴾. Mujahid said: i.e., four, which they may not exceed. Qatadah said: it is that there is no marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses. ﴿And what their right hands possess﴾, i.e., the female slaves and bondwomen, ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for you﴾ in marrying them. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

His words: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾, i.e., delay; ﴿and you may take to you whom you will﴾, i.e., include. The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse.

Abu Razin and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed when some of the Mothers of the Believers became jealous of the Prophet (ﷺ) and some of them requested an increase in maintenance; so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) abstained from them for a month, until the verse of choice was revealed, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and to release whoever chose this world, and to keep whoever chose Allah and His Messenger, on the condition that they remain Mothers of the Believers and never marry again; and on the condition that he may take to himself whom he wills and postpone whom he wills, and they would be content with that, whether he divided among them or did not divide, or divided for some and not for others, or preferred some over others in maintenance, division and companionship, or treated them equally; and the matter in all of this is up to him, he does as he wills. This was among his particular privileges (peace be upon him).

They agreed to all of that and chose it on this condition. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), despite what Allah had granted him in this regard, treated them equally in division, except for one woman whom he wished to divorce; she agreed to give up her turn, and he made her day for ʿAʾishah, and she was Sawdah bint Zamʿah.

Mansur related from Abu Razin who said: When the verse of choice was revealed, they feared he would divorce them, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah, grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state," so this verse was revealed. Among those whom he postponed were Sawdah, Juwayriyah, Safiyyah, Maymunah and Umm Habibah; he divided among them as he wished and when he wished. Among those he took to himself were ʿAʾishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab, may Allah have mercy on them; he divided among them equally, not preferring some over others. So he postponed five and took four.

Mujahid said: it means he may set aside whom he wills of them without divorce, and return to himself whom he wills of them after setting her aside, without renewing the dowry and contract.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: you may divorce whom you will of them and keep whom you will.

al-Hasan said: you may leave the marriage of whom you wish and marry whom you wish from the women of your community.

He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) proposed to a woman, it was not lawful for any man to propose to her until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) either married her or left her.

It was also said: "And you may accept whom you will of the believing women who give themselves to you, and take her to yourself, and leave whom you will so that you do not accept her."

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah related from his father from ʿAʾishah that she used to reproach the women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and she said: "Is a woman not ashamed to give herself or offer herself to a man without a dowry?" Then this verse was revealed. ʿAʾishah said: "I said to the Messenger of Allah: Indeed your Lord hastens to fulfill your desire."

﴿And whoever you seek﴾, i.e., you desire and intend to reach, ﴿of those you had set aside﴾, so you reach her and have intercourse with her after setting her aside, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾. Allah the Exalted thereby permitted him to forgo dividing among them, so that he may postpone whichever of them he wills during her turn, and not approach her, and approach whichever of them he wills outside her turn; he may return to his bed whomever he had set aside, and there is no fault upon him in what he does, as a privilege for him over other men and as an ease for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means: whoever of your wives with you has passed from you, and you have let her go, then We have made lawful for you [others], so it is not proper for you to increase upon the number of your wives who are with you.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾: more pleasing to their souls and less grievous to them when they know that this is from Allah and by His command, and that the concession came from Him. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ concerning the matter of women and inclination toward some of them. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this﴾. The people of Basra read it with a ta' (taḥillu), and others with a ya' (yaḥillu). ﴿Women after this﴾, i.e., after these nine women whom you gave the choice, and they chose you over what they chose of Allah and His Messenger and the Hereafter; He restricted it to them. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah. ʿIkrimah and al-Dahhak said: It is not lawful for you of women except those whom We have made lawful for you, and this is His words: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 50]. Then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾, meaning those We made lawful for you as described earlier.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa from Ziyad, a man of the Ansar, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) had died, would it have been lawful for him to marry?" He said: "What would prevent him from that, and what would make it unlawful for him?" I said: "His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾." He said: "Allah only made lawful for him a certain kind of women." Then He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives ...﴾, then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this.﴾

Abu Salih said: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman or an Arab woman, and afterwards he could marry, if he wished, three hundred women from his own people, from the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and maternal uncles and aunts. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: Its meaning is ﴿Women are not lawful for you﴾ other than Muslim women. As for Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you, and they should not be among the Mothers of the Believers.

Abu Razin said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, meaning slave-girls for marriage. ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾. Mujahid and Abu Razin said: meaning, nor may you exchange Muslim women for others from among the Jews, Christians and polytheists, ﴿even though their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning captives and unbelieving slave-girls.

Al-Dahhak said: meaning, nor may you exchange your wives who are in your possession for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others. Thus it was forbidden for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divorce the women who were with him, since he had made them Mothers of the Believers, and forbidden them to anyone else once they had chosen him. As for marrying other women, it was not prohibited to him; rather it was made lawful for him, if he wished. The following supports this:

What 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Abu 'Asim informed me, from Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him.

Ibn Zayd said: In the Jahiliyyah, the Arabs used to exchange their wives: this man gives his wife to that one, and takes that one's wife. So Allah said: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning, exchange your wives for the wives of others, by giving your wife and taking his wife. Except what your right hand possesses: there is no harm in exchanging your slave-girl for whatever you wish, but as for free women, no.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Ubaydi, from Ahmad ibn Najdah, from al-Hammani, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The exchange in the Jahiliyyah was that a man would say to another man: Exchange your wife with me and I will exchange mine with you; you vacate your wife for me and I will vacate mine for you. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾ ... He said: 'Uyayna ibn Husayn entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while 'A'isha was with him, and he entered without permission. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Uyayna, where is the seeking of permission?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, since I came of age I have not sought permission from any man of Mudar. Then he said: Who is this red-cheeked one beside you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers." 'Uyayna said: Shall I not vacate for you the best of creation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden that." When he left, 'A'isha said: Who was this, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "This is a foolish man who is obeyed, and he is, as you see, the chief of his people."

Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿even though their beauty pleases you﴾, said: meaning Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyyah, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. In this is evidence for the permissibility of looking at the woman one wishes to marry, and reports have come permitting this.

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, that al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah wished to marry a woman, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you two." [17] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/134.]]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Harb, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Khaythamah, from his paternal uncle Sulayman ibn Abi Khaythamah, who said: I saw Muhammad ibn Maslamah pursuing Nabitah bint al-Dahhak on one of the paths of Madinah. I said: Are you doing this? He said: Yes, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah places in a man's heart the proposal of a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her." [18]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man wished to marry a woman from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Look at her, for in the eyes of the women of the Ansar there is something." [19] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/77; Musnad Ahmad: 2/1286.]]

Al-Humaydi said: meaning, smallness (of the eyes). ﴿And Allah is ever over all things a Watcher﴾, an Guardian.

His exalted saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ Most of the exegetes said: this verse was revealed concerning the wedding feast of Zaynab.

Anas ibn Malik said: I am the most knowledgeable of people concerning the verse of hijab. Ubayy ibn Ka'b asked me about it when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh, and he held a feast for her with dates, sawiq, and a sheep was slaughtered. My mother Umm Sulaym sent to him a dish of hays in a stone bowl. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded me to invite his companions to the meal. I invited them, and the people kept coming, eating and leaving, then another group would come, eat and leave.

I said: O Prophet of Allah, I have invited people until I can find no one left to invite. He said: "Lift up your food." They lifted it, and the people left, but three men remained, talking in the house, and they prolonged their stay. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and I stood with him so that they would leave. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked off toward the room of 'A'isha and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house." They said: "And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah. How did you find your family?" Then he returned and came to the chambers of his wives and greeted them, and they prayed for him. He returned to Zaynab's house, and found the three still sitting and talking in the house. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely shy, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned back. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) turn away from his house, they left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his house and placed a curtain between me and him, and this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: This occurred in the house of Umm Salamah. A group entered her house and ate, then prolonged their conversation, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bothered by them, but he was too shy to tell them to leave, and ﴿Allah does not feel shy before the truth﴾.
