"O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [23] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/424.]

And by his chain, from Malik, from Nuʿaym, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mujmir, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from Abu Masʿud al-Ansari, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us while we were sitting in the assembly of Saʿd ibn ʿUbada. Bashir ibn [Saʿd] [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbdullah.] said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah; so how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent until we wished he had not asked. Then he said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim among the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And the greeting is as you have known it." [24] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/274; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/310.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, with my reading to him, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan related to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Nuʿaym informed me, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAwn, from Abu Fakhita, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) said: "When you send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then do so beautifully, for you do not know, perhaps that is presented to him." They said: "Teach us." He said: "Say: O Allah, make Your blessings, Your mercy and Your blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the pious, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide of goodness and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station, by which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy."

ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Janb informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Abu Muʿawiya informed me, from al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Umm al-Hasan, from her father, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "This is from the hidden knowledge, and if you had asked me about it I would not have told you. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has appointed two angels for me. No one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant and then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah, the Exalted, and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a servant and he does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.'"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾, meaning by their disobedience to Him and their opposition to His command. ʿIkrima said: they are the makers of images who aim to create a creation like the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

In some reports Allah, His majesty be exalted, says: "And who is more unjust than one who wishes to create like My creation? Let him create a grain or an atom," and he (peace be upon him) said: "Allah curses the image-makers." [Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/188; al-Durr al-Manthur 1/367.]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. As for the Jews, they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ and they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor﴾. The Christians said: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ and ﴿third of three﴾. The polytheists said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah, and the idols are His partners."

Qatada said: concerning this verse, there have always been people of the ignorant children of Adam until they inflicted harm upon their Lord. It was said: the meaning of ﴿harm Allah﴾ is that they deviate regarding His names and attributes. The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: it means they harm the friends of Allah, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [12:82], and the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he returned from Tabuk and Uhud appeared to him: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." The word (its people) was omitted, so Allah, the Exalted, intended to emphasize the prohibition of harming His friends, and made harming them as harming Him.

﴿And His Messenger﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: when he (ﷺ) was struck on the face, his front tooth was broken, and it was said to him: "Poet, sorcerer, a taught madman."

Al-ʿAwfi related from him that it was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. It was also said: by abandoning his sunna and opposing his law.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ Meaning: without their having done anything that would make harming them obligatory.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: "Beware of harming the believer, for he is the beloved of his Lord. He loved Allah, so Allah loves him, and he became angry for his Lord, so Allah becomes angry for him, and Allah protects him and punishes whoever harms him." Mujahid said: it means they accuse them and throw at them what they did not do.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), for some hypocrites used to harm him and speak to him in insulting ways.

It was said: it concerns the affair of ʿAʾisha.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Medina, following women when they went out at night to relieve themselves for their needs. They would see a woman and approach her, touch her; if she was silent, they would follow her, and if she rebuked them, they would desist. They used to seek only the female slaves, for at that time a free woman could not be distinguished from a slave woman, since their dress was the same: they went out in one garment, and the veil of the free woman and the slave woman was the same. The women complained of this to their husbands, who told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ Then He forbade free women from imitating slave women, saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments over themselves﴾ [33:59], meaning: let them let down their cloaks and wraps, and veil themselves with them, covering their faces and heads, so that it is known that they are free women, and so that they are not molested and not harmed.

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that they be known and not be harmed﴾, and ﴿Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed of their neglect of the sunna, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, for He concealed them and protected them. Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayda said: Allah commanded believing women to cover their heads and faces with outer garments and to show only one eye. Anas said: a slave girl passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab veiled, so he struck her with his whip and said: "O shameless one! Do you imitate free women? Throw off the veil!"

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ (meaning fornication), i.e. the fornicators, ﴿and the agitators in Medina﴾ with falsehood and lies. That is because some of them, whenever the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, would spread among the people that they had been killed and defeated, and would say: "The enemy has come upon you," and similar things.

Al-Kalbi said: they loved to spread reports, and ﴿that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾...

﴿We shall surely set you against them﴾: we shall incite you against them and empower you over them. ﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbors in it except for a little﴾: meaning they will not dwell with you in Medina except briefly, until they are expelled from it, ﹙cursed﹚, accursed and driven away, in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl). It was also said: in the accusative of censure. ﴿Wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a thorough killing.﴾ Qatada said: It has been related to us that the hypocrites wished to show what was in their hearts of hypocrisy, so Allah threatened them in this verse, and they concealed it.

ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Nisawi, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from ʿAbdullah ibn Yunus, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Aban, from Anas, who said: there was something between a man and Abu Bakr, and the man spoke ill of Abu Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until blood flushed his face, and he said: "Woe to you! Leave my companions and my in-laws; guard me regarding them, for over them there is a guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever does not guard me regarding them, Allah will disown him, and whom Allah disowns, He is about to seize." [25]

Cursed, wherever they are found, they shall be seized and killed with a thorough killing.

﴿The sunna of Allah﴾, i.e., as the sunna of Allah concerning those who passed before, ﴿and you will not find any change in the sunna of Allah﴾. ﴿People ask you about the Hour. Say: its knowledge is only with Allah. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper.﴾

His saying: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾, back and front, as they are dragged upon it. The common reading is with a damma on the ta' and a fatḥa on the lam, in the passive (majhūl). It is related from Abu Jaʿfar with a fatḥa on the ta' and the lam, meaning "they turn about" (yatagallab). ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (nuqallibu) with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the lam, and wujūhuhum in the accusative.

﴿They say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ in the world. ﴿And they say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters (sādatana), our leaders and our chiefs in polytheism and error. And they led us astray from the way."﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Hatim read (sādātanā), in the plural with alif and a kasra on the tā', as a plural of plural. ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment,﴾ meaning twice our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾: Yahya ibn Wathhab and ʿAsim read kabīran with the bāʾ, which is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullah. The rest read it with the thāʾ (kathīran), which is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd. Then they both said: "We have chosen the thāʾ because of His saying: ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾ [2:159] and His saying: ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and all of mankind﴾ [2:161]; this bears witness to abundance."

Abu al-Husayn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed me, saying: I heard Abu al-Hasan ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi, from memory, dictating, say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-ʿAsqalani in ʿAsqalan and Ramla also say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sarri say: I saw in a dream as if I were in the mosque of ʿAsqalan, and a man was debating with me, saying: "﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾," and I was saying "kathīran." Then there was the Prophet (ﷺ), and in the middle of the mosque there was a minaret with a door, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was heading toward it. I said: "This is the Prophet (ﷺ)." I said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He turned away from me. I came to his right side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me," and he turned away from me. I stood in front of his chest and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna related to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: that you were never asked for anything and said 'No'." He smiled, then said: "O Allah, forgive him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and this man are debating the saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾, and he says kabīran and I say kathīran." He said: he entered the minaret saying "kathīran," until his voice faded from me. [26] — meaning with the thāʾ.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 56–68:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.﴾ The common reading is with the ta' in وَمَلائِكَتَهُ in the accusative (naṣb). Ibn ʿAbbas read وَمَلائِكَتُهُ in the nominative (rafʿ), as a conjunction with the place (maḥall) of the word اللَّهَ before inna entered. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians...﴾ [5:69], and this example has already passed. ﴿يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ﴾ means they praise him and invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they seek blessing (yatabarrakūn). ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ means: invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him, ﴿وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً﴾ and greet him with the greeting of Islam.

Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, from al-Mutarri, from ʿAli ibn Harb, from Ibn Fudayl, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Fadl al-ʿAdl related to us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad al-Saffar, from al-Husayn ibn ʿUrwa, from Hushaym ibn Bashir, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla related to us, saying: Ka'b ibn ʿUjra told me, he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have known how to greet you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [21] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/162; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/309.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from ʿAmmar ibn Rajaʾ, from Ibn ʿAmir, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar, from Yazid ibn Mihran, from ʿAbdullah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, he said:

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting, we have known it; so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim." [22] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/47; Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/157.]

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faqih related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he said:

"As I read to Ibn Nafi', and Mutarrif related to me, from Malik, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn Sulayman al-Zuraqi, Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi informed me that they said:

"O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [23] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/424.]

And by his chain, from Malik, from Nuʿaym, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mujmir, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from Abu Masʿud al-Ansari, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us while we were sitting in the assembly of Saʿd ibn ʿUbada. Bashir ibn [Saʿd] [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbdullah.] said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah; so how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent until we wished he had not asked. Then he said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim among the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And the greeting is as you have known it." [24] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/274; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/310.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, with my reading to him, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan related to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Nuʿaym informed me, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAwn, from Abu Fakhita, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) said: "When you send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then do so beautifully, for you do not know, perhaps that is presented to him." They said: "Teach us." He said: "Say: O Allah, make Your blessings, Your mercy and Your blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the pious, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide of goodness and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station, by which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy."

ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Janb informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Abu Muʿawiya informed me, from al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Umm al-Hasan, from her father, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "This is from the hidden knowledge, and if you had asked me about it I would not have told you. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has appointed two angels for me. No one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant and then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah, the Exalted, and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a servant and he does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.'"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾, meaning by their disobedience to Him and their opposition to His command. ʿIkrima said: they are the makers of images who aim to create a creation like the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. As for the Jews, they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ and they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor﴾. The Christians said: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ and ﴿third of three﴾. The polytheists said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah, and the idols are His partners."

Qatada said: concerning this verse, there have always been people of the ignorant children of Adam until they inflicted harm upon their Lord. It was said: the meaning of ﴿harm Allah﴾ is that they deviate regarding His names and attributes. The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: it means they harm the friends of Allah, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [12:82], and the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he returned from Tabuk and Uhud appeared to him: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." The word (its people) was omitted, so Allah, the Exalted, intended to emphasize the prohibition of harming His friends, and made harming them as harming Him.

﴿And His Messenger﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: when he (ﷺ) was struck on the face, his front tooth was broken, and it was said to him: "Poet, sorcerer, a taught madman."

Al-ʿAwfi related from him that it was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. It was also said: by abandoning his sunna and opposing his law.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ Meaning: without their having done anything that would make harming them obligatory.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: "Beware of harming the believer, for he is the beloved of his Lord. He loved Allah, so Allah loves him, and he became angry for his Lord, so Allah becomes angry for him, and Allah protects him and punishes whoever harms him." Mujahid said: it means they accuse them and throw at them what they did not do.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), for some hypocrites used to harm him and speak to him in insulting ways.

It was said: it concerns the affair of ʿAʾisha.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Medina, following women when they went out at night to relieve themselves for their needs. They would see a woman and approach her, touch her; if she was silent, they would follow her, and if she rebuked them, they would desist. They used to seek only the female slaves, for at that time a free woman could not be distinguished from a slave woman, since their dress was the same: they went out in one garment, and the veil of the free woman and the slave woman was the same. The women complained of this to their husbands, who told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ Then He forbade free women from imitating slave women, saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments over themselves﴾ [33:59], meaning: let them let down their cloaks and wraps, and veil themselves with them, covering their faces and heads, so that it is known that they are free women, and so that they are not molested and not harmed.

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayda said: Allah commanded believing women to cover their heads and faces with outer garments and to show only one eye. Anas said: a slave girl passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab veiled, so he struck her with his whip and said: "O shameless one! Do you imitate free women? Throw off the veil!"

﴿We shall surely set you against them﴾: we shall incite you against them and empower you over them. ﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbors in it except for a little﴾: meaning they will not dwell with you in Medina except briefly, until they are expelled from it, ﹙cursed﹚, accursed and driven away, in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl). ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Nisawi, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from ʿAbdullah ibn Yunus, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Aban, from Anas, who said: there was something between a man and Abu Bakr, and the man spoke ill of Abu Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until blood flushed his face, and he said: "Woe to you! Leave my companions and my in-laws; guard me regarding them, for over them there is a guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever does not guard me regarding them, Allah will disown him, and whom Allah disowns, He is about to seize." [25]

Cursed, wherever they are found, they shall be seized and killed with a thorough killing.

﴿The sunna of Allah﴾, i.e., as the sunna of Allah concerning those who passed before, ﴿and you will not find any change in the sunna of Allah﴾. ﴿People ask you about the Hour. Say: its knowledge is only with Allah. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper.﴾

His saying: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾, back and front, as they are dragged upon it. The common reading is with a damma on the ta' and a fatḥa on the lam, in the passive (majhūl). It is related from Abu Jaʿfar with a fatḥa on the ta' and the lam, meaning "they turn about" (yatagallab). ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (nuqallibu) with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the lam, and wujūhuhum in the accusative.

﴿They say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ in the world. ﴿And they say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters (sādatana), our leaders and our chiefs in polytheism and error. And they led us astray from the way."﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Hatim read (sādātanā), in the plural with alif and a kasra on the tā', as a plural of plural. ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment,﴾ meaning twice our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾: Yahya ibn Wathhab and ʿAsim read kabīran with the bāʾ, which is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullah. The rest read it with the thāʾ (kathīran), which is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd. Then they both said: "We have chosen the thāʾ because of His saying: ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾ [2:159] and His saying: ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and all of mankind﴾ [2:161]; this bears witness to abundance."

Abu al-Husayn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed me, saying: I heard Abu al-Hasan ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi, from memory, dictating, say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-ʿAsqalani in ʿAsqalan and Ramla also say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sarri say: I saw in a dream as if I were in the mosque of ʿAsqalan, and a man was debating with me, saying: "﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾," and I was saying "kathīran." Then there was the Prophet (ﷺ), and in the middle of the mosque there was a minaret with a door, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was heading toward it. I said: "This is the Prophet (ﷺ)." I said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He turned away from me. I came to his right side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me," and he turned away from me. I stood in front of his chest and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna related to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: that you were never asked for anything and said 'No'." He smiled, then said: "O Allah, forgive him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and this man are debating the saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾, and he says kabīran and I say kathīran." He said: he entered the minaret saying "kathīran," until his voice faded from me. [26] — meaning with the thāʾ.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 56–68:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.﴾ The common reading is with the ta' in وَمَلائِكَتَهُ in the accusative (naṣb). Ibn ʿAbbas read وَمَلائِكَتُهُ in the nominative (rafʿ), as a conjunction with the place (maḥall) of the word اللَّهَ before inna entered. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians...﴾ [5:69], and this example has already passed. ﴿يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ﴾ means they praise him and invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they seek blessing (yatabarrakūn). ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ means: invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him, ﴿وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً﴾ and greet him with the greeting of Islam.

Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, from al-Mutarri, from ʿAli ibn Harb, from Ibn Fudayl, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Fadl al-ʿAdl related to us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad al-Saffar, from al-Husayn ibn ʿUrwa, from Hushaym ibn Bashir, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla related to us, saying: Ka'b ibn ʿUjra told me, he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have known how to greet you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [21] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/162; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/309.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from ʿAmmar ibn Rajaʾ, from Ibn ʿAmir, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar, from Yazid ibn Mihran, from ʿAbdullah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, he said:

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting, we have known it; so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim." [22] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/47; Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/157.]

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faqih related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he said:

"As I read to Ibn Nafi', and Mutarrif related to me, from Malik, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn Sulayman al-Zuraqi, Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi informed me that they said:

"O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [23] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/424.]

And by his chain, from Malik, from Nuʿaym, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mujmir, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from Abu Masʿud al-Ansari, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us while we were sitting in the assembly of Saʿd ibn ʿUbada. Bashir ibn [Saʿd] [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbdullah.] said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah; so how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent until we wished he had not asked. Then he said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim among the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And the greeting is as you have known it." [24] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/274; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/310.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, with my reading to him, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan related to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Nuʿaym informed me, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAwn, from Abu Fakhita, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) said: "When you send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then do so beautifully, for you do not know, perhaps that is presented to him." They said: "Teach us." He said: "Say: O Allah, make Your blessings, Your mercy and Your blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the pious, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide of goodness and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station, by which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy."

ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Janb informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Abu Muʿawiya informed me, from al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Umm al-Hasan, from her father, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "This is from the hidden knowledge, and if you had asked me about it I would not have told you. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has appointed two angels for me. No one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant and then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah, the Exalted, and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a servant and he does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.'"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾, meaning by their disobedience to Him and their opposition to His command. ʿIkrima said: they are the makers of images who aim to create a creation like the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

In some reports Allah, His majesty be exalted, says: "And who is more unjust than one who wishes to create like My creation? Let him create a grain or an atom," and he (peace be upon him) said: "Allah curses the image-makers." [Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/188; al-Durr al-Manthur 1/367.]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. As for the Jews, they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ and they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor﴾. The Christians said: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ and ﴿third of three﴾. The polytheists said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah, and the idols are His partners."

Qatada said: concerning this verse, there have always been people of the ignorant children of Adam until they inflicted harm upon their Lord. It was said: the meaning of ﴿harm Allah﴾ is that they deviate regarding His names and attributes. The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: it means they harm the friends of Allah, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [12:82], and the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he returned from Tabuk and Uhud appeared to him: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." The word (its people) was omitted, so Allah, the Exalted, intended to emphasize the prohibition of harming His friends, and made harming them as harming Him.

﴿And His Messenger﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: when he (ﷺ) was struck on the face, his front tooth was broken, and it was said to him: "Poet, sorcerer, a taught madman."

Al-ʿAwfi related from him that it was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. It was also said: by abandoning his sunna and opposing his law.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ Meaning: without their having done anything that would make harming them obligatory.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: "Beware of harming the believer, for he is the beloved of his Lord. He loved Allah, so Allah loves him, and he became angry for his Lord, so Allah becomes angry for him, and Allah protects him and punishes whoever harms him." Mujahid said: it means they accuse them and throw at them what they did not do.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), for some hypocrites used to harm him and speak to him in insulting ways.

It was said: it concerns the affair of ʿAʾisha.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Medina, following women when they went out at night to relieve themselves for their needs. They would see a woman and approach her, touch her; if she was silent, they would follow her, and if she rebuked them, they would desist. They used to seek only the female slaves, for at that time a free woman could not be distinguished from a slave woman, since their dress was the same: they went out in one garment, and the veil of the free woman and the slave woman was the same. The women complained of this to their husbands, who told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ Then He forbade free women from imitating slave women, saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments over themselves﴾ [33:59], meaning: let them let down their cloaks and wraps, and veil themselves with them, covering their faces and heads, so that it is known that they are free women, and so that they are not molested and not harmed.

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that they be known and not be harmed﴾, and ﴿Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed of their neglect of the sunna, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, for He concealed them and protected them. Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayda said: Allah commanded believing women to cover their heads and faces with outer garments and to show only one eye. Anas said: a slave girl passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab veiled, so he struck her with his whip and said: "O shameless one! Do you imitate free women? Throw off the veil!"

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ (meaning fornication), i.e. the fornicators, ﴿and the agitators in Medina﴾ with falsehood and lies. That is because some of them, whenever the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, would spread among the people that they had been killed and defeated, and would say: "The enemy has come upon you," and similar things.

Al-Kalbi said: they loved to spread reports, and ﴿that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾...

﴿We shall surely set you against them﴾: we shall incite you against them and empower you over them. ﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbors in it except for a little﴾: meaning they will not dwell with you in Medina except briefly, until they are expelled from it, ﹙cursed﹚, accursed and driven away, in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl). It was also said: in the accusative of censure. ﴿Wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a thorough killing.﴾ Qatada said: It has been related to us that the hypocrites wished to show what was in their hearts of hypocrisy, so Allah threatened them in this verse, and they concealed it.

ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Nisawi, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from ʿAbdullah ibn Yunus, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Aban, from Anas, who said: there was something between a man and Abu Bakr, and the man spoke ill of Abu Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until blood flushed his face, and he said: "Woe to you! Leave my companions and my in-laws; guard me regarding them, for over them there is a guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever does not guard me regarding them, Allah will disown him, and whom Allah disowns, He is about to seize." [25]

Cursed, wherever they are found, they shall be seized and killed with a thorough killing.

﴿The sunna of Allah﴾, i.e., as the sunna of Allah concerning those who passed before, ﴿and you will not find any change in the sunna of Allah﴾. ﴿People ask you about the Hour. Say: its knowledge is only with Allah. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper.﴾

His saying: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾, back and front, as they are dragged upon it. The common reading is with a damma on the ta' and a fatḥa on the lam, in the passive (majhūl). It is related from Abu Jaʿfar with a fatḥa on the ta' and the lam, meaning "they turn about" (yatagallab). ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (nuqallibu) with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the lam, and wujūhuhum in the accusative.

﴿They say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ in the world. ﴿And they say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters (sādatana), our leaders and our chiefs in polytheism and error. And they led us astray from the way."﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Hatim read (sādātanā), in the plural with alif and a kasra on the tā', as a plural of plural. ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment,﴾ meaning twice our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾: Yahya ibn Wathhab and ʿAsim read kabīran with the bāʾ, which is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullah. The rest read it with the thāʾ (kathīran), which is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd. Then they both said: "We have chosen the thāʾ because of His saying: ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾ [2:159] and His saying: ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and all of mankind﴾ [2:161]; this bears witness to abundance."

Abu al-Husayn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed me, saying: I heard Abu al-Hasan ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi, from memory, dictating, say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-ʿAsqalani in ʿAsqalan and Ramla also say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sarri say: I saw in a dream as if I were in the mosque of ʿAsqalan, and a man was debating with me, saying: "﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾," and I was saying "kathīran." Then there was the Prophet (ﷺ), and in the middle of the mosque there was a minaret with a door, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was heading toward it. I said: "This is the Prophet (ﷺ)." I said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He turned away from me. I came to his right side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me," and he turned away from me. I stood in front of his chest and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna related to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: that you were never asked for anything and said 'No'." He smiled, then said: "O Allah, forgive him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and this man are debating the saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾, and he says kabīran and I say kathīran." He said: he entered the minaret saying "kathīran," until his voice faded from me. [26] — meaning with the thāʾ.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ Meaning: without their having done anything that would make harming them obligatory.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: "Beware of harming the believer, for he is the beloved of his Lord. He loved Allah, so Allah loves him, and he became angry for his Lord, so Allah becomes angry for him, and Allah protects him and punishes whoever harms him." Mujahid said: it means they accuse them and throw at them what they did not do.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), for some hypocrites used to harm him and speak to him in insulting ways.

It was said: it concerns the affair of ʿAʾisha.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Medina, following women when they went out at night to relieve themselves for their needs. They would see a woman and approach her, touch her; if she was silent, they would follow her, and if she rebuked them, they would desist. They used to seek only the female slaves, for at that time a free woman could not be distinguished from a slave woman, since their dress was the same: they went out in one garment, and the veil of the free woman and the slave woman was the same. The women complained of this to their husbands, who told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ Then He forbade free women from imitating slave women, saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments over themselves﴾ [33:59], meaning: let them let down their cloaks and wraps, and veil themselves with them, covering their faces and heads, so that it is known that they are free women, and so that they are not molested and not harmed.

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that they be known and not be harmed﴾, and ﴿Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed of their neglect of the sunna, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, for He concealed them and protected them. Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUbayda said: Allah commanded believing women to cover their heads and faces with outer garments and to show only one eye. Anas said: a slave girl passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab veiled, so he struck her with his whip and said: "O shameless one! Do you imitate free women? Throw off the veil!"

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ (meaning fornication), i.e. the fornicators, ﴿and the agitators in Medina﴾ with falsehood and lies. That is because some of them, whenever the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, would spread among the people that they had been killed and defeated, and would say: "The enemy has come upon you," and similar things.

Al-Kalbi said: they loved to spread reports, and ﴿that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾...

﴿We shall surely set you against them﴾: we shall incite you against them and empower you over them. ﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbors in it except for a little﴾: meaning they will not dwell with you in Medina except briefly, until they are expelled from it, ﹙cursed﹚, accursed and driven away, in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl). It was also said: in the accusative of censure. ﴿Wherever they are found they will be seized and killed with a thorough killing.﴾ Qatada said: It has been related to us that the hypocrites wished to show what was in their hearts of hypocrisy, so Allah threatened them in this verse, and they concealed it.

ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Nisawi, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from ʿAbdullah ibn Yunus, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Aban, from Anas, who said: there was something between a man and Abu Bakr, and the man spoke ill of Abu Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until blood flushed his face, and he said: "Woe to you! Leave my companions and my in-laws; guard me regarding them, for over them there is a guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever does not guard me regarding them, Allah will disown him, and whom Allah disowns, He is about to seize." [25]

Cursed, wherever they are found, they shall be seized and killed with a thorough killing.

﴿The sunna of Allah﴾, i.e., as the sunna of Allah concerning those who passed before, ﴿and you will not find any change in the sunna of Allah﴾. ﴿People ask you about the Hour. Say: its knowledge is only with Allah. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper.﴾

His saying: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾, back and front, as they are dragged upon it. The common reading is with a damma on the ta' and a fatḥa on the lam, in the passive (majhūl). It is related from Abu Jaʿfar with a fatḥa on the ta' and the lam, meaning "they turn about" (yatagallab). ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (nuqallibu) with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the lam, and wujūhuhum in the accusative.

﴿They say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ in the world. ﴿And they say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters (sādatana), our leaders and our chiefs in polytheism and error. And they led us astray from the way."﴾ Al-Hasan, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Hatim read (sādātanā), in the plural with alif and a kasra on the tā', as a plural of plural. ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment,﴾ meaning twice our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾: Yahya ibn Wathhab and ʿAsim read kabīran with the bāʾ, which is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullah. The rest read it with the thāʾ (kathīran), which is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd. Then they both said: "We have chosen the thāʾ because of His saying: ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾ [2:159] and His saying: ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and all of mankind﴾ [2:161]; this bears witness to abundance."

Abu al-Husayn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed me, saying: I heard Abu al-Hasan ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Shadhan al-Baghdadi, from memory, dictating, say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-ʿAsqalani in ʿAsqalan and Ramla also say: I heard Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sarri say: I saw in a dream as if I were in the mosque of ʿAsqalan, and a man was debating with me, saying: "﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾," and I was saying "kathīran." Then there was the Prophet (ﷺ), and in the middle of the mosque there was a minaret with a door, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was heading toward it. I said: "This is the Prophet (ﷺ)." I said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He turned away from me. I came to his right side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me," and he turned away from me. I stood in front of his chest and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna related to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: that you were never asked for anything and said 'No'." He smiled, then said: "O Allah, forgive him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and this man are debating the saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾, and he says kabīran and I say kathīran." He said: he entered the minaret saying "kathīran," until his voice faded from me. [26] — meaning with the thāʾ.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verse 56–68:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.﴾ The common reading is with the ta' in وَمَلائِكَتَهُ in the accusative (naṣb). Ibn ʿAbbas read وَمَلائِكَتُهُ in the nominative (rafʿ), as a conjunction with the place (maḥall) of the word اللَّهَ before inna entered. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians...﴾ [5:69], and this example has already passed. ﴿يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ﴾ means they praise him and invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they seek blessing (yatabarrakūn). ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ means: invoke mercy upon him and supplicate for him, ﴿وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً﴾ and greet him with the greeting of Islam.

Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, from al-Mutarri, from ʿAli ibn Harb, from Ibn Fudayl, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Fadl al-ʿAdl related to us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad al-Saffar, from al-Husayn ibn ʿUrwa, from Hushaym ibn Bashir, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla related to us, saying: Ka'b ibn ʿUjra told me, he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have known how to greet you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [21] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/162; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/309.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from ʿAmmar ibn Rajaʾ, from Ibn ʿAmir, from ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar, from Yazid ibn Mihran, from ʿAbdullah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, he said:

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting, we have known it; so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim." [22] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/47; Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/157.]

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faqih related to us, from Makki ibn ʿAbdan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he said:

"As I read to Ibn Nafi', and Mutarrif related to me, from Malik, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn Sulayman al-Zuraqi, Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi informed me that they said:

"O Messenger of Allah, how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." [23] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/424.]

And by his chain, from Malik, from Nuʿaym, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mujmir, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from Abu Masʿud al-Ansari, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us while we were sitting in the assembly of Saʿd ibn ʿUbada. Bashir ibn [Saʿd] [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbdullah.] said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah; so how should we send blessings upon you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent until we wished he had not asked. Then he said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim among the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And the greeting is as you have known it." [24] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/274; Sunan al-Darimi: 1/310.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, with my reading to him, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan related to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from ʿAbd ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Nuʿaym informed me, from al-Masʿudi, from ʿAwn, from Abu Fakhita, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) said: "When you send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then do so beautifully, for you do not know, perhaps that is presented to him." They said: "Teach us." He said: "Say: O Allah, make Your blessings, Your mercy and Your blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the pious, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide of goodness and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station, by which the first and the last will envy him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy."

ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Janb informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Talib, from Yazid ibn Harun, who said: Abu Muʿawiya informed me, from al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Umm al-Hasan, from her father, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "This is from the hidden knowledge, and if you had asked me about it I would not have told you. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has appointed two angels for me. No one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant and then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah, the Exalted, and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a servant and he does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah and His angels say in reply to those two angels: 'Amen.'"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah﴾, meaning by their disobedience to Him and their opposition to His command. ʿIkrima said: they are the makers of images who aim to create a creation like the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

In some reports Allah, His majesty be exalted, says: "And who is more unjust than one who wishes to create like My creation? Let him create a grain or an atom," and he (peace be upon him) said: "Allah curses the image-makers." [Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/188; al-Durr al-Manthur 1/367.]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. As for the Jews, they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ and they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor﴾. The Christians said: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ and ﴿third of three﴾. The polytheists said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah, and the idols are His partners."

Qatada said: concerning this verse, there have always been people of the ignorant children of Adam until they inflicted harm upon their Lord. It was said: the meaning of ﴿harm Allah﴾ is that they deviate regarding His names and attributes. The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: it means they harm the friends of Allah, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [12:82], and the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he returned from Tabuk and Uhud appeared to him: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it." The word (its people) was omitted, so Allah, the Exalted, intended to emphasize the prohibition of harming His friends, and made harming them as harming Him.

﴿And His Messenger﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: when he (ﷺ) was struck on the face, his front tooth was broken, and it was said to him: "Poet, sorcerer, a taught madman."

Al-ʿAwfi related from him that it was revealed concerning those who slandered the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. It was also said: by abandoning his sunna and opposing his law.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it, they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ Meaning: without their having done anything that would make harming them obligatory.

It was said: it concerns the affair of ʿAʾisha.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Medina, following women when they went out at night to relieve themselves for their needs. **Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 33, verses 69–73:**

His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses; but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾. "Wajihan" means noble, esteemed, accepted, of high standing. The scholars differed over what they harmed Moses with.

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Hamid ibn al-Sharafi informed me, from Muhammad and Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir and Ahmad ibn Yusuf, who said: Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Mutayri informed me, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Mu'addib informed me, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, each looking at the private parts of the others. Moses (peace be upon him) used to bathe alone. So they said: 'By Allah, the only thing preventing Moses from bathing with us is that he has a hernia (adar).' [[Adar: its verbal noun is al-adar; a man who is adar is one with a swelling in the testicle.]] Once he went to bathe alone and put his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. He pursued it saying, 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until the Children of Israel saw Moses' private parts and said, 'By Allah, there is no defect in Moses.' Then the rock stopped after they had looked at him, so he took his garment and began striking the rock." [27] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/73; Sahih Muslim: 7/99.]]

Abu Hurayra said: "On the rock there are marks, six or seven, from the striking of Moses (peace be upon him)."

Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin narrated from Abu Hurayra regarding this verse, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a man of great modesty and concealment; he hardly showed any of his skin out of shyness. Those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He only conceals himself this much because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a hernia.' Allah wished to clear him of what they said. One day Moses was alone, so he placed his garment on a rock and bathed. When he finished his bath, he went to take his garment, but the rock fled with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, who saw him, the best of people in form and most balanced in appearance. Then the rock stopped, and he took his garment and put it on, and began striking the rock. The assembly said: 'May Allah curse the liars of the Children of Israel!' That was the innocence with which Allah cleared him." [28] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/515; al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 7/455.]]

Others said: their harm to him was their accusing him of killing his brother Harun.

Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid al-Tabari: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, from Abbad, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿like those who harmed Moses﴾. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Hamid ibn al-Sharafi informed me, from Muhammad and Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir and Ahmad ibn Yusuf, who said: Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Mutayri informed me, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Mu'addib informed me, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, each looking at the private parts of the others. Moses (peace be upon him) used to bathe alone. So they said: 'By Allah, the only thing preventing Moses from bathing with us is that he has a hernia (adar).' [[Adar: its verbal noun is al-adar; a man who is adar is one with a swelling in the testicle.]] Once he went to bathe alone and put his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. He pursued it saying, 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until the Children of Israel saw Moses' private parts and said, 'By Allah, there is no defect in Moses.' Then the rock stopped after they had looked at him, so he took his garment and began striking the rock." [27] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/73; Sahih Muslim: 7/99.]]

Abu Hurayra said: "On the rock there are marks, six or seven, from the striking of Moses (peace be upon him)."

Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin narrated from Abu Hurayra regarding this verse, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a man of great modesty and concealment; he hardly showed any of his skin out of shyness. Those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He only conceals himself this much because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a hernia.' Allah wished to clear him of what they said. One day Moses was alone, so he placed his garment on a rock and bathed. When he finished his bath, he went to take his garment, but the rock fled with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, who saw him, the best of people in form and most balanced in appearance. Then the rock stopped, and he took his garment and put it on, and began striking the rock. The assembly said: 'May Allah curse the liars of the Children of Israel!' That was the innocence with which Allah cleared him." [28] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/515; al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 7/455.]]

Others said: their harm to him was their accusing him of killing his brother Harun.

Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Yazid al-Tabari: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, from Abbad, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿like those who harmed Moses﴾. He said: Moses and Harun ascended the mountain, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said: "You killed him, and he loved us more than you did and was gentler to us than you." So they harmed him with this. Allah commanded the angels, and they carried Harun's body and passed by the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Thus Allah cleared Moses of that. They took him away and buried him, but no one from among the creatures of Allah saw his grave except the vulture, so Allah made it deaf and mute.

Abu al-Aliya said: It was that Qarun hired a prostitute to accuse Moses (peace be upon him) by throwing herself at him before the assembly. Allah protected her from that, cleared Moses of it, and destroyed Qarun.

This story has already passed.

﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and speak words that are upright﴾. "Sadidan" means true, direct. Ibn Abbas said: correct. Qatada and Muqatil said: just. Al-Mu'arrikh said: straight. Ikrima said: it is the saying "There is no god but Allah." Ibn Hayyan said: meaning, speak upright words concerning the matter of Zaynab and Zayd, and do not attribute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what he cannot bear. ﴿He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great success﴾.

His words: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾. It was said: the offering was to these things themselves, and Allah gave them understanding of His address and made them speak. It was also said: it was offered to those in them among the angels.

It was said: it was offered to their people entirely, not to their very substances, like His words: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [[Surah Yusuf: 82.]] [meaning its people].

﴿But they refused to bear it, out of fear and dread, not out of disobedience or defiance.﴾ The offering was an option, not a compulsion. ﴿And man bore it.﴾

The commentators differed about the Trust. Most exegetes said: it is obedience and the obligations that Allah imposed upon His servants. It was offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains: if they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them. So they disliked that and were apprehensive, not out of disobedience, but out of glorifying the religion of Allah, that they should not undertake it. They said: "No, we are subjected to Your command; we seek neither reward nor punishment."

Then Allah the Exalted said to Adam: "I offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they could not bear it. Will you take it with what it entails?" He said: "O Lord, what does it entail?" He said: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished." So Adam (peace be upon him) took it and said: "Between my ear and my shoulder." Allah the Exalted said: "As you have taken it, I will help you. Make a veil for your sight: when you fear that you might look at what is not lawful for you, lower its veil. Make two lips and a lock for your tongue: when you fear, close them. Make a covering for your private parts and do not uncover them in what I have forbidden you."

They said: Adam remained only the length of time between noon and afternoon prayer before he was removed from Paradise.

Mujahid said: The Trust is the obligations and the limits of religion. Abu al-Aliya said: it is what they were commanded and forbidden. Zayd ibn Aslam and others said: it is fasting, ritual bathing from impurity, and what is hidden of the laws of religion.

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us, from al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asqalani, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi, who said: Abu al-Awwam al-Qattan informed us, from Qatada and Aban ibn Abi Abbas, from Khulayd al-Asri, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with five things, along with faith, will enter Paradise: one who preserves the five prayers with their ablutions, bowings, prostrations and appointed times; who gives zakat from his wealth willingly, and he used to say, '[By] Allah, none does that except a believer'; and who fulfils the trust." They said: "O Abu al-Darda', what is the fulfilling of the trust?" He said: "Ritual bathing from impurity." [[In the source: it was said: "O Prophet of Allah."]] He said: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic did not entrust the son of Adam with anything of His religion other than this." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/68 at the verse; Kanz al-Ummal: 15/887, no. 43513; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/47.]]

And with that chain, from Ibn Jarir, from Ibn Bashshar, from Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "Among the Trust is that a woman is entrusted with her private part."

Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-As said: The first thing Allah created of man was his private part, and He said: "This is a trust I have deposited with you." So the private part is a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the hand is a trust, the foot is a trust, and there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness.

Some said: it is the trusts of people and fulfilling covenants; it is incumbent upon every believer not to deceive another believer or a covenanted person in anything, small or great. This is the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. Al-Suddi said with his chain: It is Adam's entrusting his son Qabil with his household and offspring, and Qabil's betrayal of that by killing his brother. He mentioned the story until he said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to Adam: "O Adam, do you know that I have a house on earth?" He said: "No, O Allah." He said: "I have a house in Makkah, so go to it." Adam said to the heaven: "Guard my son with the trust," but it refused; he said the same to the earth, and it refused; he said it to the mountains, and they refused; and he said it to Qabil, who said: "Yes, go and return, and you will find your family as you wish." So Adam (peace be upon him) set off, and when he returned, Qabil had killed Habil. That is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾, meaning Qabil, when he bore Adam's trust and then did not guard his family.

Others said: ﴿and man bore it﴾ means Adam. Then their expressions differed on the meaning of "zalum" (wrongdoer) and "jahul" (ignorant). Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant﴾, deceived about the command of Allah and what he took on of the trust. Qatada said: a wrongdoer to the trust, ignorant of its right. Al-Kalbi said: a wrongdoer when he disobeyed his Lord, ignorant, not knowing the punishment for abandoning the trust. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿he was indeed a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ in the sight of the angels, not in the sight of Allah.

﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and women, and the polytheist men and women, and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾
